title: Exclusive Control Of Quantum Memory Erasure
authors: Mir Alimuddin, Nathan Shettell, Raja Yehia, Antonio Acín, And Federico Centrone
abstract:
Author(s): Mir Alimuddin, Nathan Shettell, Raja Yehia, Antonio Acín, and Federico Centrone

Erasing memory is a fundamental operational task in quantum information processing, governed by Landauer's principle, which links information loss to thermodynamic work. We introduce and analyze assisted quantum erasure, where correlations with a remote system reduce the energetic cost of resetting …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043078] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes assisted quantum erasure, showing how correlations with a remote system can reduce the thermodynamic work cost of resetting a quantum memory beyond the standard Landauer bound.
motivation: Memory erasure is a fundamental quantum information task governed by Landauer's principle, which ties information loss to thermodynamic work, and the work asks whether external quantum correlations can alter this energetic cost.
method: The authors define assisted quantum erasure protocols in which a memory is erased while correlated with a remote system, and they quantify the energetic cost using information-theoretic and thermodynamic tools.
result: They find that correlations can reduce the work required for erasure, establishing an assisted erasure advantage and clarifying how remote quantum information influences Landauer-type energetic bounds.
conclusion: The work extends Landauer's principle to correlated quantum memories and highlights the operational role of correlations in quantum thermodynamic erasure tasks.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an information-theoretic model of agents as complex self-organizing systems and analyzes the work capacity of memory channels, showing that thermodynamic efficiency requires forgetting parts of past actions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how information-processing constraints shape the thermodynamics of adaptive agents, particularly the role of memory in work extraction and efficiency.
method: They formulate an information-theoretic model of agents and study the work capacity of channels with memory, linking memory retention and forgetting to thermodynamic performance.
result: The analysis shows that agents operating at thermodynamic efficiency must discard some information about their past actions, revealing a trade-off between memory and work capacity.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamics-of-agents framework connecting information flow, memory, and work extraction, with implications for the physical limits of self-organizing systems.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a conic optimization method for computing finite-size quantum key distribution rates using Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and faster numerical convergence.
motivation: Finite-size key rate estimation is a critical bottleneck in practical QKD security analyses, where one needs tight bounds on Rényi entropies while maintaining computational efficiency.
method: The authors formulate key rate estimation as a conic optimization problem involving Rényi entropic quantities, enabling tighter finite-size security bounds with fast numerical convergence.
result: The approach provides improved finite-size QKD key rates compared with existing methods and demonstrates efficient numerical performance.
conclusion: Conic optimization offers a practical route to tighter finite-size QKD security bounds based on Rényi entropies, strengthening quantum cryptography security analyses.

title: No-Go Theorem For Gaussian Quantum Repeaters From Fractional Extendibility
authors: Rabsan Galib Ahmed And Graeme Smith
abstract:
Author(s): Rabsan Galib Ahmed and Graeme Smith

Photon loss in optical channels fundamentally limits long-range reliable quantum communication. A standard approach to overcoming this limitation is the use of quantum repeater nodes, which typically perform experimentally demanding non-Gaussian operations. However, whether Gaussian repeater protoco…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170804] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a no-go theorem showing that Gaussian quantum repeater protocols cannot overcome optical loss, using fractional extendibility of Gaussian channels.
motivation: Photon loss fundamentally limits long-range quantum communication, and quantum repeaters are the standard solution, but they typically require non-Gaussian operations; it was unclear whether purely Gaussian repeater protocols could suffice.
method: The authors derive a no-go theorem for Gaussian quantum repeaters based on the concept of fractional extendibility, a channel resource measure for Gaussian channels.
result: They show that Gaussian repeater protocols are subject to fundamental limitations that prevent them from enabling reliable long-range quantum communication over lossy channels.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations are necessary for quantum repeaters to overcome optical loss, establishing a fundamental boundary for Gaussian repeater architectures.

title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Zhi Li, Takato Mori, And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Li, Takato Mori, and Beni Yoshida

Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041013] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: Tripartite Haar-random quantum states contain no bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement distillable by local operations.
motivation: Entanglement structure in random many-party states is central to quantum information, yet whether bipartite entanglement can be extracted from tripartite Haar-random states under local operations was unclear.
method: The authors analyze tripartite Haar-random states and prove limitations on bipartite entanglement distillation under local operations, likely using random-matrix and entanglement-theoretic techniques.
result: They show that no bipartite EPR entanglement can be distilled from tripartite Haar random states via local operations, establishing a strong no-go result for bipartite entanglement extraction.
conclusion: The work clarifies the entanglement structure of random tripartite states and has implications for entanglement theory and operational protocols in quantum information.

title: Consistent Time Reversal And Reliable And Accurate Inference In The Presence Of Memory
authors: Tassilo Schwarz, Anatoly B. Kolomeisky, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Tassilo Schwarz, Anatoly B. Kolomeisky, and Aljaž Godec

Thermodynamic inference from coarse observations remains a key challenge. Memory, in particular correlations between consecutively observed mesostates, blur signatures of irreversibility and must be accounted for in defining physical time reversal, which remains an open problem. We derive an experim…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 187401] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a consistent time-reversal framework and inference scheme for thermodynamic inference from coarse observations when memory correlations are present.
motivation: Thermodynamic inference from limited observations is challenging because memory between consecutive mesostates obscures irreversibility and complicates the definition of physical time reversal.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that accounts for memory correlations and defines a consistent time reversal for coarse-grained stochastic trajectories.
result: The framework enables reliable and accurate thermodynamic inference in the presence of memory, improving irreversibility estimates from incomplete observations.
conclusion: Properly accounting for memory is essential for consistent time reversal and trustworthy thermodynamic inference in stochastic systems.

title: Multipartite Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger Nonclassicality From Interwoven Frustrated Down-conversion
authors: Marek Żukowski, Paweł Cieśliński, Marcin Markiewicz, And Konrad Schlichtholz
abstract:
Author(s): Marek Żukowski, Paweł Cieśliński, Marcin Markiewicz, and Konrad Schlichtholz

We present a theory of an interference process that starts with [MATH] coherently pumped two-mode parametric down-conversion (PDC) sources, whose output modes are directed to [MATH] observers such that each observer receives modes from two different source crystals. Each observation station is equipped wi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042222] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory showing how interwoven frustrated parametric down-conversion can generate multipartite Bell-GHZ nonclassicality.
motivation: Multipartite nonclassicality, especially GHZ-type Bell nonlocality, is a central resource for quantum information, but efficient schemes for generating it from parametric down-conversion remain of strong interest.
method: The authors analyze an interference process with multiple coherently pumped two-mode parametric down-conversion sources, where each observer receives modes from two different crystals and performs measurements at a local station.
result: The theory identifies conditions under which the interwoven frustrated down-conversion setup produces multipartite Bell-GHZ nonclassicality among the observers.
conclusion: Interwoven frustrated parametric down-conversion provides a viable theoretical route to multipartite GHZ nonclassicality relevant for foundational tests and quantum information protocols.

title: Quantum Key Distribution With Entanglement-swapped Photons From A Quantum Emitter
authors: Michele B. Rota, Francesco Basso Basset, Alessandro Laneve, Francesco Salusti, Nicolas Claro-Rodriguez, Giuseppe Ronco, Mattia Beccaceci, Tobias M. Krieger, Quirin Buchinger, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Sandra Stroj, Mariia Gumberidze, Vladyslav Usenko, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Mario A. Usuga Castaneda, Armando Rastelli, Klaus D. Jöns, And Rinaldo Trotta
abstract:
Author(s): Michele B. Rota, Francesco Basso Basset, Alessandro Laneve, Francesco Salusti, Nicolas Claro-Rodriguez, Giuseppe Ronco, Mattia Beccaceci, Tobias M. Krieger, Quirin Buchinger, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Sandra Stroj, Mariia Gumberidze, Vladyslav Usenko, Sven Höfling, Tobias Huber-Loyola, Mario A. Usuga Castaneda, Armando Rastelli, Klaus D. Jöns, and Rinaldo Trotta

Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a fundamental functionality of quantum networks. Extending its range requires quantum repeaters, a technology still under development and not yet demonstrated in combination with quantum cryptographic protocols. Here, we address the elementary operation of a viable …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043096] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates QKD using entanglement-swapped photons emitted by a quantum emitter, realizing an elementary building block for quantum repeater-based networks.
motivation: Extending QKD over long distances requires quantum repeaters, but repeater technology has not yet been combined with practical quantum cryptographic protocols.
method: Photons from a quantum emitter are entangled and then entanglement-swapped to establish correlations between remote parties, enabling a QKD protocol over the swapped link.
result: The authors show that entanglement-swapped photons from a quantum emitter can support QKD, providing a proof-of-principle demonstration of a repeater-compatible cryptographic link.
conclusion: This work connects quantum-emitter-based entanglement swapping with QKD, advancing experimental progress toward quantum repeater networks.

title: Sample Complexity Of Purity And Inner Product Estimation
authors: Weiyuan Gong, Jonas Haferkamp, Qi Ye, And Zhihan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Weiyuan Gong, Jonas Haferkamp, Qi Ye, and Zhihan Zhang

We study the sample complexity of the prototypical tasks quantum purity estimation and quantum inner product estimation. The former has been a key subroutine for experimental benchmarking and entropy estimation, while the latter is a core task for cross-platform validation that compares the unknown …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043077] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the sample complexity of quantum purity and inner-product estimation, two fundamental state-analysis tasks.
motivation: Purity estimation underpins benchmarking and entropy estimation, while inner-product estimation is central to cross-platform validation and comparing unknown quantum states.
method: It provides a theoretical sample-complexity analysis of these estimation tasks, likely deriving upper and lower bounds for protocols that use limited copies of quantum states.
result: The paper characterizes the copy/sample complexity of purity and inner-product estimation, clarifying the fundamental resource requirements for these tasks.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum state-property estimation and provides benchmarks for experimental and algorithmic quantum information processing.

title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian Of Mean Force And Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Author(s): Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, and Ángel Rivas

A unified theoretical framework allows one to measure thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information, offering a practical foundation for designing next-generation quantum thermal devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043014] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified framework for defining thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using local information via an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force.
motivation: Strong-coupling quantum thermodynamics is challenging because conventional definitions of work, heat, and free energy rely on global system-bath descriptions that are often experimentally inaccessible.
method: The authors introduce and analyze an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force to formulate local thermodynamic quantities for strongly coupled quantum systems, providing a practical theoretical framework for quantum thermal devices.
result: The framework enables measurement of thermodynamic quantities from local information alone, establishing a consistent strong-coupling description without requiring full access to the bath or global Hamiltonian.
conclusion: This work offers a practical foundation for designing and analyzing next-generation quantum thermal devices operating in the strong-coupling regime.

title: Sparse Anisotropic Positive Maps For Qutrit Entanglement: Exact Indecomposability And Positive-partial-transpose Geometry
authors: Massimiliano F. Sacchi
abstract:
Author(s): Massimiliano F. Sacchi

Positive but not completely positive maps provide one of the most direct ways to detect entanglement beyond the positive-partial-transpose (PPT) criterion. We introduce and analyze an exactly solvable two-parameter family of sparse bistochastic positive maps on qutrits, in which two coherence channe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042455] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an exactly solvable two-parameter family of sparse bistochastic positive maps on qutrits for entanglement detection beyond the PPT criterion.
motivation: Positive but not completely positive maps are a direct tool for detecting entangled states that evade the positive-partial-transpose criterion, motivating exactly solvable constructions with clear geometric characterization.
method: The author constructs and analyzes a two-parameter family of sparse anisotropic positive maps on qutrits involving coherence channels, establishing exact indecomposability and studying the associated PPT geometry.
result: The family provides analytically tractable entanglement witnesses/maps and characterizes regions where the maps are positive but not completely positive, yielding exact indecomposability conditions.
conclusion: This work enriches the theory of entanglement detection by positive maps and clarifies the geometry of PPT entanglement for qutrits through a solvable sparse-map family.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse For Fast Analytic Control Of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
authors: Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041018] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables and derives composite pulses for fast analytic control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors require fast, accurate control, but standard quantum signal processing typically assumes commuting control variables and is not directly suited to such noncommuting hybrid settings.
method: The authors develop a non-Abelian quantum signal processing framework for noncommuting control variables and use it to construct composite-pulse control protocols for hybrid oscillator-qubit systems.
result: The framework yields analytic composite-pulse controls that enable fast control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
conclusion: Non-Abelian quantum signal processing provides a practical route to analytical high-speed control in hybrid quantum processors combining oscillators and qubits.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to characterize how resource-constrained quantum many-body systems can nevertheless generate universal randomness and deep thermalization.
motivation: Understanding whether limited quantum resources suffice for universal random ensembles and thermalization is central to quantum information and many-body physics.
method: The authors define Scrooge ensembles as constrained families of quantum states and analyze their universality for randomness and deep thermalization across quantum many-body systems.
result: They find that even stingy, resource-limited ensembles can exhibit universal randomness and deep thermalization, establishing broad universality.
conclusion: The work sharpens the minimal requirements for universal quantum randomness and thermalization and connects constrained ensembles to deep thermalization phenomena.

title: Superconducting Qutrit Link Beyond The Qubit Limit
authors: Xiang Li, Zheng-Yang Mei, Yang He, Si-Lu Zhao, Yan-Jun Liu, Xiao-Hui Song, Kai Xu, Zhong-Cheng Xiang, Dong-Ning Zheng, And Heng Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Zheng-Yang Mei, Yang He, Si-Lu Zhao, Yan-Jun Liu, Xiao-Hui Song, Kai Xu, Zhong-Cheng Xiang, Dong-Ning Zheng, and Heng Fan

Deterministic remote entanglement of superconducting qutrits via time-bin microwave photons surpasses the negativity bound of two-qubit states.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180801] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates deterministic remote entanglement between superconducting qutrits using time-bin microwave photons, achieving correlations that surpass the negativity bound of two-qubit states.
motivation: Extending quantum links from qubits to higher-dimensional qudits can enable richer quantum correlations and higher information capacity, but deterministic remote entanglement of superconducting qutrits had not been demonstrated.
method: Superconducting qutrits are coupled via time-bin microwave photons to generate remote entanglement deterministically, with tomographic characterization of the resulting qutrit-qutrit state.
result: The experiment observes remote qutrit entanglement whose negativity exceeds the maximum possible for any two-qubit state, confirming genuine qutrit entanglement beyond the qubit limit.
conclusion: This work establishes a superconducting qutrit link for deterministic remote entanglement, extending quantum network capabilities beyond qubit-based architectures.

title: Bidirectional Teleportation Using Scrambling Dynamics: A Practical Protocol
authors: Amit Vikram, Edwin Chaparro, Muhammad Miskeen Khan, Andrew Lucas, Chris Akers, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Amit Vikram, Edwin Chaparro, Muhammad Miskeen Khan, Andrew Lucas, Chris Akers, and Ana Maria Rey

We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic swap gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. Our protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill type recovery scheme, associated with the black hole information paradox, with quantum teleportation an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180403] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a practical bidirectional teleportation protocol that uses quantum information scrambling to implement a SWAP gate between collective degrees of freedom without universal local control.
motivation: Many quantum platforms lack the local control needed for standard SWAP gates, motivating protocols that exploit global scrambling dynamics to exchange quantum information.
method: The protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill-type recovery scheme from black-hole information theory with quantum teleportation to realize bidirectional state transfer between collective modes.
result: It shows that scrambling dynamics can enable a generic SWAP gate and teleportation in systems without universal local control.
conclusion: This provides a practical route to quantum information exchange in collectively controlled systems and connects scrambling, teleportation, and black-hole-inspired recovery.

title: Hierarchy Of Entanglement Detection Criteria For Random High-dimensional States
authors: Akhil Kumar Awasthi, Sudipta Mondal, Rivu Gupta, And Aditi Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Akhil Kumar Awasthi, Sudipta Mondal, Rivu Gupta, and Aditi Sen(De)

Entanglement is a cornerstone in quantum information science, yet detecting it efficiently remains a challenging task. Focusing on states with nonpositive partial transpose, we establish a hierarchy among entropy-based, majorization, realignment, and reduction criteria for Haar uniformly generated r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042461] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a hierarchy among several entanglement-detection criteria for Haar-random high-dimensional states with nonpositive partial transpose.
motivation: Entanglement detection remains challenging, especially for high-dimensional mixed states, and different criteria are known to detect different subsets of entangled states.
method: The authors compare entropy-based, majorization, realignment, and reduction criteria on Haar uniformly generated random high-dimensional states with nonpositive partial transpose.
result: They derive a hierarchy showing the relative detection power of these criteria for the considered random state ensembles.
conclusion: The hierarchy clarifies which detection methods are more effective for random high-dimensional NPT states and provides guidance for practical entanglement detection.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how auxiliary circuit modes induce multiphoton resonances that degrade the coherence and tunneling-time behavior of Kerr-cat qubits under strong driving.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits are promising superconducting bosonic qubits with biased noise protection, but their performance under strong drives can be limited by unwanted circuit modes.
method: The authors theoretically study the Kerr-cat qubit coupled to auxiliary circuit modes and identify multiphoton resonance processes activated under strong driving.
result: Auxiliary modes are shown to trigger multiphoton resonances that break down the Kerr-cat qubit tunneling time and coherence in the strong-drive regime.
conclusion: The work clarifies a decoherence mechanism in Kerr-cat qubits and provides guidance for mitigating auxiliary-mode-induced breakdown in superconducting circuit designs.

title: Certifying Localizable Quantum Properties With Constant Sample Complexity
authors: Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, And Xiongfeng Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, and Xiongfeng Ma

Researchers develop a versatile quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using local Pauli measurements.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041027] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: A versatile certification framework that verifies global quantum state properties and state fidelity from local Pauli measurements with constant sample complexity.
motivation: Certifying global properties of large entangled states (e.g., GHZ-type fidelity, entanglement witnesses) usually requires resource-intensive global measurements or tomography; the authors seek a scalable, measurement-efficient alternative.
method: The framework combines local Pauli measurements with a structural 'localizability' decomposition of observables/properties, giving estimator constructions and rigorous sample-complexity bounds for fidelity and property certification.
result: The protocol certifies global state properties and fidelities using a number of measurement samples independent of system size, thus overcoming the usual exponential or polynomial-in-n scaling of tomography-based approaches.
conclusion: Local Pauli measurements suffice for efficient, scalable certification of nonlocal quantum properties, providing a practical tool for verifying entanglement resources in near-term and large-scale quantum devices.

title: Partial Reversibility And Counterdiabatic Driving In Nearly Integrable Systems
authors: Rohan Banerjee, Shahyad Khamnei, Anatoli Polkovnikov, And Stewart Morawetz
abstract:
Author(s): Rohan Banerjee, Shahyad Khamnei, Anatoli Polkovnikov, and Stewart Morawetz

Adiabatic (or reversible) processes are the key concept unifying our understanding of thermodynamics and dynamical systems. Reversibility in the thermodynamic sense is understood as entropy-preserving processes, such as in the idealized Carnot engine, whereas in integrable dynamical systems, it is u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042625] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes partial reversibility in nearly integrable systems and connects it to counterdiabatic driving, bridging thermodynamic reversibility with dynamical adiabaticity.
motivation: Reversibility is central to thermodynamics and dynamical systems, but its meaning in nearly integrable quantum systems and its relation to counterdiabatic control remain insufficiently understood.
method: The authors introduce and analyze a notion of partial reversibility for nearly integrable systems and study how counterdiabatic driving can approximately restore reversible adiabatic dynamics.
result: They show that counterdiabatic protocols can achieve partial reversibility in nearly integrable systems, with the degree of reversibility controlled by integrability-breaking and driving parameters.
conclusion: The work clarifies the interplay between thermodynamic reversibility, adiabatic dynamics, and counterdiabatic control, with implications for quantum thermodynamic protocols in complex systems.

title: Predicting Magic From Very Few Measurements
authors: J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, And R. A. Macêdo
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, and R. A. Macêdo

A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness—the resource that enables universal quantum computation—from a small number of Pauli measurements, extending its estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043009] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a near-optimal method to quantify nonstabilizerness, or magic, from very few Pauli measurements, enabling estimation for system sizes beyond standard techniques.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is the key resource enabling universal quantum computation, but existing methods for quantifying it require too many measurements or are limited to small systems.
method: The authors develop a measurement-efficient protocol based on a small number of Pauli measurements to estimate magic, likely using randomized or optimized Pauli sampling and resource-theoretic bounds.
result: Their method achieves near-optimal scaling and extends magic estimation to larger system sizes than previously possible, with rigorous performance guarantees.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable tool for quantifying nonstabilizerness, advancing operational resource theories and enabling experimental characterization of magic in larger quantum systems.

title: Ising On The Donut: Regimes Of Topological Quantum Error Correction From Statistical Mechanics
authors: Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, and Dominic J. Williamson

An exact mapping to the 2D Ising model produces closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code, offering an analytic tool kit for benchmarking topological codes beyond current computational limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043004] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps the toric code's logical failure behavior exactly to the 2D Ising model, yielding closed-form logical failure rates for topological quantum error correction.
motivation: Benchmarking topological codes at large sizes is computationally demanding, so analytic tools are needed to characterize error-correction regimes beyond current numerical limits.
method: The authors construct an exact statistical-mechanical mapping between the toric code and the 2D Ising model, then use it to derive closed-form expressions for logical failure rates.
result: The mapping provides analytic logical failure rates and identifies distinct regimes of topological quantum error correction from the corresponding Ising-model phases.
conclusion: This offers a practical analytic toolkit for benchmarking topological codes and connecting quantum error correction to statistical mechanics.

title: Millimeter Wave Readout Of A Superconducting Qubit
authors: Akash V. Dixit, Zachary L. Parrott, Dennis Chunikhin, Trevyn F. Q. Larson, Bradley D. Hauer, And John D. Teufel
abstract:
Author(s): Akash V. Dixit, Zachary L. Parrott, Dennis Chunikhin, Trevyn F. Q. Larson, Bradley D. Hauer, and John D. Teufel

A new device uses millimeter-wave radiation to accurately read the states of superconducting qubits without altering them.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180803] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates non-destructive readout of a superconducting qubit using millimeter-wave radiation.
motivation: Efficient and non-perturbative readout is essential for scaling superconducting qubit systems, and higher-frequency millimeter-wave readout may offer advantages over conventional microwave approaches.
method: The authors integrate a superconducting qubit with a millimeter-wave readout device and measure the qubit-state-dependent response to millimeter-wave radiation.
result: They achieve accurate readout of the superconducting qubit states without altering the qubit state during measurement.
conclusion: Millimeter-wave radiation is a viable readout modality for superconducting qubits, with potential implications for future quantum processor architectures.

title: Deep Thermalization And Measurements Of Quantum Resources
authors: Naga Dileep Varikuti, Soumik Bandyopadhyay, And Philipp Hauke
abstract:
Author(s): Naga Dileep Varikuti, Soumik Bandyopadhyay, and Philipp Hauke

Quantum resource theories provide a unified framework for characterizing useful quantum phenomena subject to physical constraints, but are notoriously hard to assess in experimental systems. In this Letter, we introduce a unified protocol for quantifying the resource-generating power of arbitrary qu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180401] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a unified protocol that uses deep thermalization (projected-ensemble designs) to quantify the resource-generating power of arbitrary quantum states, turning resource-theory monotones into experimentally accessible quantities.
motivation: Quantum resource theories (e.g., magic, coherence, athermality) give a rigorous framework for useful quantum phenomena under physical constraints, but the relevant resource monotones are notoriously difficult to measure in actual experiments.
method: They relate the resource-generating power of a state to the deviation of its projected (post-measurement) ensembles from Haar-random designs, i.e., to deep thermalization, and construct a measurement protocol that extracts these quantities from few-body observables.
result: The protocol yields a unified, experimentally feasible estimator for resource-generating power across different resource theories, with the deep-thermalization picture providing both the operational meaning and the convergence guarantees of the measurement scheme.
conclusion: Deep thermalization provides a practical bridge between abstract resource-theoretic quantities and experiment, enabling unified benchmarking of quantum resources in current devices.

title: Spreading Of Magic Resource Under Unitary Clifford Dynamics
authors: Mircea Bejan, Pieter W. Claeys, And Jiangtian Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Mircea Bejan, Pieter W. Claeys, and Jiangtian Yao

Nonstabilizerness, or quantum magic resource, presents a valuable resource in quantum error correction and computation. We study the dynamics of locally injected nonstabilizerness in unitary Clifford circuits, where the total nonstabilizerness is conserved. However, the absence of physical observabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180402] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how locally injected nonstabilizerness, or magic, spreads under unitary Clifford dynamics in circuits where total magic is conserved.
motivation: Magic is a key resource for quantum computation and error correction, but its dynamical spreading under Clifford unitaries is less understood because total nonstabilizerness is conserved and direct physical observables are limited.
method: The authors analyze unitary Clifford circuits and track the dynamics of locally injected nonstabilizerness using stabilizer/magic-resource techniques.
result: They characterize how an initially local magic resource spreads through the system under Clifford dynamics while the total nonstabilizerness remains conserved.
conclusion: The work clarifies the spreading behavior of magic in Clifford circuits and contributes to the operational understanding of nonstabilizerness as a quantum resource.

title: Ergotropy Activation And Coherence In Dissipatively Charged Quantum Batteries
authors: Hui-Yu Yang, Kang-Yuan Chen, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, And Xiao-Hui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hui-Yu Yang, Kang-Yuan Chen, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, and Xiao-Hui Wang

Quantum batteries can exploit quantum resources to enhance energy storage and work extraction, and recent experimental progress has brought their implementation closer to reality. In realistic settings, however, environmental dissipation is unavoidable, making dissipative charging a physically relev…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042454] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how ergotropy activation and coherence affect work extraction in dissipatively charged quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries could exploit quantum resources for enhanced energy storage, but realistic environmental dissipation during charging must be understood.
method: The authors theoretically study dissipative charging of quantum batteries, focusing on ergotropy activation and coherence as resources for extractable work.
result: They identify conditions under which coherence and ergotropy activation enhance or constrain work extraction in dissipatively charged quantum batteries.
conclusion: The work clarifies the role of quantum resources in realistic quantum battery operation and provides guidance for dissipative charging protocols.

title: Adaptive Stabilizer-state-fidelity Certification
authors: Kun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Kun Wang

Certifying the fidelity of a prepared state to a target stabilizer state is a fundamental task in quantum information processing. The reference [
tldr: The paper develops adaptive certification methods for bounding the fidelity of a prepared quantum state to a target stabilizer state, addressing gauge dependence in prior worst-case bounds.
motivation: Certifying proximity to stabilizer states is fundamental for quantum information processing, but existing optimal worst-case bounds depend on a fixed stabilizer generator gauge and can be loose.
method: The author analyzes gauge-dependent fidelity bounds and proposes an adaptive certification strategy that improves stabilizer-state fidelity estimation beyond a single fixed generator gauge.
result: The adaptive approach yields improved fidelity certification compared with the fixed-gauge optimal worst-case lower bound of Phys. Rev. A 99, 042337 (2019).
conclusion: Adaptive gauge handling provides a more reliable stabilizer-state fidelity certification tool for quantum information tasks.

title: Finite-data Certification Of Mixed-state Nonstabilizerness From Pauli Witnesses
authors: Wenlong Sun And Yuanfeng Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Wenlong Sun and Yuanfeng Jin

We apply Hoeffding's inequality directly to weighted estimators of Pauli-expanded witnesses to obtain finite-sample tests for mixed-state nonstabilizerness. With witnesses and shot allocations fixed in advance, the tests control false positives under independent sampling. We also derive sufficient s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042458] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops finite-sample statistical tests for certifying mixed-state nonstabilizerness using Pauli-expanded witnesses and Hoeffding inequalities.
motivation: Certifying quantum resources such as magic in realistic, finite-data experiments requires rigorous statistical guarantees, especially for mixed states where standard stabilizer Rényi entropy witnesses are harder to use.
method: The authors apply Hoeffding's inequality directly to weighted estimators of Pauli-expanded witnesses, with witnesses and shot allocations fixed in advance, to construct finite-sample tests that control false positives under independent sampling.
result: They obtain finite-data certification protocols for mixed-state nonstabilizerness and derive sufficient sampling conditions for reliable detection.
conclusion: The approach provides statistically rigorous, experimentally applicable tools for certifying nonstabilizerness in mixed quantum states.

title: Predicting Dynamics From Flows Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
authors: Dominik Hahn, David M. Long, Marin Bukov, And Anushya Chandran
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, David M. Long, Marin Bukov, and Anushya Chandran

Analytical treatments of far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics are few, even in well-thermalizing systems. The celebrated eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides a post hoc ansatz for the matrix elements of observables in the eigenbasis of a thermalizing Hamiltonian, given various respon…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043091] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical approach to predict far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics using flows derived from the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
motivation: Analytical treatments of far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics remain scarce, even in well-thermalizing systems, motivating new methods beyond the standard post hoc ETH ansatz.
method: It uses the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis as a starting point and introduces a flow-based framework to connect ETH matrix elements to observable dynamics.
result: The approach enables predictions of dynamical behavior from ETH flows, extending the utility of ETH beyond static matrix-element ansatzes.
conclusion: ETH-based flow methods provide a promising analytical route for understanding far-from-equilibrium dynamics in thermalizing quantum systems.

title: Enabling Deterministic Passive Quantum State Transfer With Giant Atoms
authors: Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele de Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, And Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele De Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, and Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

Tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide enables deterministic quantum state transfer at above 99% fidelity, without any time-dependent control.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043013] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: Giant atoms coupled to a waveguide enable deterministic passive quantum state transfer with above 99% fidelity and no time-dependent control.
motivation: Quantum state transfer between distant nodes is a key primitive for quantum networks, but achieving deterministic high-fidelity transfer usually requires active control or precise pulse shaping.
method: The authors design tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide, exploiting interference and collective effects to realize a passive state-transfer protocol.
result: The protocol achieves deterministic quantum state transfer with fidelity above 99% without any time-dependent control.
conclusion: Giant-atom waveguide QED provides a promising route toward simple, robust quantum interconnects for networked quantum information processing.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution Via Full Core-Mode Encoding Over Deployed Multicore Fibers
authors: G. H. Dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, And G. Lima
abstract:
Author(s): G. H. dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, and G. Lima

A four-dimensional quantum key distribution protocol utilizing full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers is demonstrated, establishing a viable architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043012] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates four-dimensional quantum key distribution using full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers, enabling a practical high-rate quantum-secure communication architecture.
motivation: High-dimensional quantum key distribution can increase information capacity and noise resilience, while multicore fibers offer parallel spatial channels for scalable quantum communication. The work aims to show that combining core and mode encoding in deployed fiber can provide a viable high-rate QKD platform.
method: The authors implement a four-dimensional QKD protocol that encodes information in the full core-mode space of a multicore fiber and test it over deployed fiber links, characterizing the channel and protocol performance.
result: They demonstrate operation of the high-dimensional QKD protocol over deployed multicore fibers, establishing feasibility of full core-mode encoding for quantum-secure communications.
conclusion: The demonstrated architecture provides a practical route toward high-rate quantum key distribution using spatial degrees of freedom in deployed multicore fiber infrastructure.

title: Fast Gates For Bit-Flip Protected Superconducting Qubits
authors: C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, and J. M. Fink

An architecture design for real-time tunable bit-flip protection yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043008] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting-qubit architecture with real-time tunable bit-flip protection and fast gates, aimed at a hardware-efficient noise-biased platform for error correction and scalability.
motivation: Superconducting qubits require hardware-efficient noise protection and scalable control to make error correction practical.
method: The authors design and analyze an architecture for bit-flip-protected superconducting qubits with tunable protection and fast gate operations.
result: The architecture provides a noise-biased platform compatible with error correction and scalable superconducting-qubit hardware.
conclusion: This work advances superconducting-qubit platforms by combining bit-flip protection with fast gates in a scalable, hardware-efficient design.

title: Information-Theoretic Principle Of Emergent 1-Form Symmetries
authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

Viewing emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction(QEC) makes them detectable with QEC decoders, providing efficient protocols for revealing emergent symmetry structure and probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043006] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper frames emergent 1-form symmetries through quantum error correction, showing that QEC decoders can efficiently reveal symmetry structure and probe phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Emergent higher-form symmetries are important for characterizing topological order and phase transitions, but detecting them efficiently in quantum many-body systems remains challenging.
method: The authors reinterpret emergent 1-form symmetries using the lens of quantum error correction and construct protocols based on QEC decoders to detect the associated symmetry structure.
result: QEC decoders are shown to detect emergent 1-form symmetries and identify phase transitions in quantum many-body systems, providing efficient protocols for probing these features.
conclusion: The work establishes an information-theoretic principle connecting emergent 1-form symmetries and quantum error correction, enabling practical decoding-based diagnostics of many-body phases.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Experiment, theory, and simulations jointly demonstrate that readout drive frequency controls and can minimize readout-induced decoherence in transmons caused by coupling to two-level systems (TLSs).
motivation: Readout is essential for superconducting qubit operation, yet the drive used for dispersive measurement can degrade qubit lifetimes through coupling to parasitic TLSs, an effect that is not well understood or controlled.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements of transmon lifetimes under varying readout drive frequencies with theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of the qubit-TLS interaction and readout-induced spectral reshaping.
result: They find that readout drive frequency is a key knob: specific frequencies cause TLS-mediated lifetime degradation, while others minimize it, and experiment, theory, and simulation all agree on this behavior.
conclusion: Choosing an appropriate readout drive frequency mitigates TLS-induced decoherence, providing a practical guideline for improving transmon coherence and readout fidelity in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive a fundamental quantum uncertainty relation showing an unavoidable trade-off between the reliability of charging power and the reliability of the work deposited in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for quantum energy storage, but fundamental limits on how precisely their power and stored work can be simultaneously controlled had not been established.
method: The analysis is based on an information-theoretic uncertainty-relation framework applied to the charging and discharging dynamics of quantum battery systems, yielding bounds on fluctuations of power and work.
result: The derived trade-off relation shows that reducing fluctuations in charging power necessarily increases uncertainty in deposited work, and vice versa, imposing design limits on quantum batteries.
conclusion: These reliability trade-offs provide essential guiding constraints for the design and optimization of future quantum energy storage devices.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a logical accreditation framework for efficiently certifying fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verification of encoded quantum systems is challenging, and scalable certification of computational accuracy is needed without trusting the underlying quantum device.
method: The framework combines fault-tolerant encoding with accreditation-style verification protocols to assess the correctness of logical computations under general noise models.
result: It provides a scalable tool for certifying fault-tolerant quantum computations and evaluating computational accuracy under realistic device noise.
conclusion: Logical accreditation enables efficient verification of fault-tolerant quantum computations, supporting trustworthy quantum computing at the logical level.

title: Charging Quantum Batteries With Chiral Squeezing
authors: Borhan Ahmadi, André H. A. Malavazi, Janine Splettstoesser, Paweł Horodecki, And Lei Du
abstract:
Author(s): Borhan Ahmadi, André H. A. Malavazi, Janine Splettstoesser, Paweł Horodecki, and Lei Du

We propose a quantum-battery charger based on a driven bosonic Kitaev chain (BKC), where chiral squeezing converts passive input fluctuations into ordered, nonpassive battery states. While a coherent input pulse exhibits phase-sensitive chiral transport, the charging dynamics is dominated by bidirec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180404] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum-battery charger using a driven bosonic Kitaev chain in which chiral squeezing converts passive input fluctuations into nonpassive battery states.
motivation: Quantum batteries require efficient charging mechanisms that can generate useful, nonpassive states from available input noise or fluctuations, and chiral transport in driven bosonic chains offers a promising route.
method: The authors analyze a driven bosonic Kitaev chain as a charger, studying phase-sensitive chiral transport of coherent input pulses and the role of bidirectional dynamics in charging, with chiral squeezing transforming passive fluctuations into ordered battery states.
result: Coherent input shows phase-sensitive chiral transport, but the charging dynamics is dominated by bidirectional processes; chiral squeezing enables conversion of passive input fluctuations into nonpassive battery states.
conclusion: Driven bosonic Kitaev chains with chiral squeezing provide a viable quantum-battery charging platform and highlight the thermodynamic usefulness of nonpassive states generated from passive fluctuations.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A general quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner's friend scenarios that tracks Heisenberg cuts to ensure logically and causally consistent reasoning without absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend scenarios raise apparent contradictions about measurement outcomes and causal structure across different observers, requiring a formalism that avoids assuming absolute measurement events.
method: The authors develop a quantum circuit framework in which agents and measurements are represented while explicitly tracking different Heisenberg cuts and analyzing consistency conditions across perspectives.
result: The framework resolves logical paradoxes in extended Wigner's friend scenarios by providing a causally and logically consistent description of measurement events without privileging any absolute observer.
conclusion: This work offers a general foundation for reasoning about perspectival measurement events in quantum theory and clarifies how causal consistency can be maintained in Wigner's friend-type experiments.

title: Free Cumulants In Full Eigenstate Thermalization From Boundary Scrambling
authors: Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, and Pieter W. Claeys

The introduction of boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model yields an analytically tractable study of higher-order out-of-time-order correlation function dynamics and new insights into free probability and the emergence of random-matrix behavior.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043003] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model to analytically study higher-order out-of-time-order correlators and the emergence of random-matrix behavior via free cumulants.
motivation: Understanding full eigenstate thermalization and higher-order scrambling dynamics requires tractable models that connect OTOC dynamics to random-matrix universality and free probability.
method: The authors construct and analyze a boundary-scrambling model, using free cumulants to compute higher-order OTOC dynamics analytically.
result: They obtain analytically tractable higher-order OTOC dynamics and show how free-probability structures yield insights into the emergence of random-matrix behavior in eigenstate thermalization.
conclusion: Boundary scrambling provides a solvable setting for probing higher-order scrambling and strengthens connections between ETH, free probability, and random-matrix universality.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a circuit-based framework using a correlation-decay condition to characterize finite-temperature quantum phases and argues that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Finite-temperature quantum phases and the thermal stability of quantum memories are central to understanding when quantum order can persist in realistic noisy settings.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based characterization of thermal quantum phases based on a correlation-decay condition.
result: They establish self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories within this framework.
conclusion: The work provides a unified phase-based perspective on finite-temperature quantum order and self-correcting quantum memory behavior.

title: Nonclassicality Of A Macroscopic Qubit-ensemble Via Parity Measurement Induced Disturbance
authors: Lorenzo Braccini, Debarshi Das, Ben Zindorf, Stephen D. Hogan, John J. L. Morton, And Sougato Bose
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Braccini, Debarshi Das, Ben Zindorf, Stephen D. Hogan, John J. L. Morton, and Sougato Bose

We propose an experimental scheme to test the nonclassicality of a macroscopic ensemble of qubits through the violation of the classical notion of macrorealism (MR) via the fundamental measurement-induced disturbance of quantum systems. An electromagnetic resonator is used to probe the parity of the…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043092] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an experimental scheme to test nonclassicality in a macroscopic qubit ensemble by violating macrorealism through parity-measurement-induced disturbance.
motivation: Testing whether macroscopic quantum systems obey macrorealism is a fundamental challenge, and measurement-induced disturbance provides a route to certify nonclassicality without full state tomography.
method: An electromagnetic resonator is used to probe the parity of a macroscopic ensemble of qubits, enabling a measurement-based test of macrorealism via the disturbance induced by parity measurements.
result: The scheme is designed to reveal a violation of the classical notion of macrorealism in the macroscopic qubit ensemble through parity measurement induced disturbance.
conclusion: This work offers a practical experimental proposal for certifying macroscopic nonclassicality and probing the quantum-to-classical transition in qubit ensembles.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a hybrid qubit-boson (oscillator-qubit) quantum processor framework for simulating interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.
motivation: Simulating lattice gauge theories and interacting fermionic/bosonic matter is hard for purely qubit-based hardware, so a platform that natively exploits both discrete qubits and continuous-variable oscillators is desirable.
method: They develop a hybrid oscillator-qubit architecture, likely in the circuit-QED setting, with gates and encodings that map fermionic, bosonic, and gauge-field degrees of freedom onto coupled qubit-oscillator modes.
result: The framework enables resource-efficient digital/analog simulation of interacting fermion-boson models and lattice gauge fields, with concrete circuit constructions and resource estimates.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors offer a promising route to simulating lattice gauge theories and correlated many-body physics beyond purely qubit architectures.

title: Algorithmic Construction Of Gapped Boundaries For Topological Stabilizer Codes: A Route To Low-Overhead Planar qLDPC Codes
authors: Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, And Yu-An Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, and Yu-An Chen (陳昱安)

An algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes enables low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043016] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a general algorithmic framework for systematically constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes, enabling planar qLDPC architectures with low overhead and fault-tolerant logical operations.
motivation: Planar architectures for topological stabilizer codes require well-controlled gapped boundaries to host logical qubits and implement logical gates, but designing such boundaries has largely been done case-by-case for specific codes.
method: The authors develop an algorithmic procedure that, given a 2D topological Pauli stabilizer code, constructs gapped boundary conditions and the associated boundary stabilizers, then uses these to define planar layouts and logical operations.
result: The framework yields planar qLDPC code architectures with reduced overhead and provides a systematic route to fault-tolerant logical gates via boundary manipulation.
conclusion: Algorithmic boundary construction generalizes and unifies boundary engineering for topological stabilizer codes, offering a practical path toward low-overhead planar qLDPC quantum memories and processors.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity based on Bell sampling, showing it bounds state-preparation complexity and certifies the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.
motivation: Non-Gaussianity is the key resource for fermionic quantum computation beyond matchgate/Gaussian circuits, but operationally meaningful, experimentally measurable quantifiers were lacking.
method: Bell sampling protocols are adapted to fermionic systems to define non-Gaussianity monotones, with efficient quantum algorithms for estimating them from few copies of the state.
result: The monotones upper-bound the cost of preparing fermionic states and prove that exact Gaussian state conversions are irreversible, while remaining estimable via practical sampling schemes.
conclusion: The work provides an operationally grounded resource theory of fermionic non-Gaussianity with experimentally feasible certification tools.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a protocol that uses only existing error-syndrome data—without extra calibration circuits—to benchmark fault-tolerant Clifford circuits and verify encoded computations in situ.
motivation: Benchmarking quantum hardware and validating fault-tolerant encoded computations typically requires costly dedicated calibration circuits, so a method that reuses syndrome data would make verification and benchmarking far more efficient and scalable.
method: The protocol leverages the error syndrome data produced during the operation of stabilizer/Clifford circuits, combined with decoding information, to extract hardware benchmarking metrics and certify encoded logical computation without additional calibration experiments.
result: The approach efficiently benchmarks hardware performance and verifies encoded Clifford computations directly from syndrome records, providing a practical in situ diagnostic tool demonstrated in the context of fault-tolerant circuit operation.
conclusion: In situ syndrome-based benchmarking offers a calibration-free route to validating fault-tolerant quantum computations, connecting error-correction diagnostics with verification of encoded Clifford circuits.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs efficient entanglement purification circuits for dual-species neutral-atom arrays, exploiting species-selective operations to enable quantum networking and distributed computation.
motivation: Entanglement purification is essential for distributing high-fidelity entanglement over noisy channels, but conventional protocols impose heavy overhead in local addressing and destructive midcircuit measurements. Dual-species arrays can reduce this technical burden.
method: The authors propose circuit designs for entanglement purification leveraging a dual-species atomic array platform, where one species serves as a communication qubit and the other as a memory, avoiding local addressing and allowing nondestructive midcircuit measurements.
result: The proposed dual-species purification circuits achieve efficient entanglement purification with reduced experimental overhead, offering a practical route toward networking-grade entanglement distribution.
conclusion: Dual-species atom arrays provide a hardware-efficient platform for entanglement purification, making them promising building blocks for quantum networking and distributed quantum computation.

title: Millisecond-Coherent 2d Nuclear Shells Around ${V}_{\mathrm{B}}^{−}$ Defects In hBN
authors: G. V. Mamin, E. V. Dmitrieva, F. F. Murzakhanov, I. N. Gracheva, K. L. Franzke, T. Biktagirov, W. G. Schmidt, U. Gerstmann, And V. A. Soltamov
abstract:
Author(s): G. V. Mamin, E. V. Dmitrieva, F. F. Murzakhanov, I. N. Gracheva, K. L. Franzke, T. Biktagirov, W. G. Schmidt, U. Gerstmann, and V. A. Soltamov

We demonstrate an essentially two-dimensional (2D) driven central-spin regime based on negatively charged boron vacancy ([MATH]) defects in the dense nuclear quadrupolar lattice of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). At 3 T magnetic field, the [MATH] bath collapses into classes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186701] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a two-dimensional driven central-spin regime using negatively charged boron vacancy defects in hBN, with nuclear spin shells exhibiting millisecond coherence.
motivation: Defect-based spin systems in solids are promising platforms for quantum information, and hBN offers a dense nuclear quadrupolar lattice that may enable scalable nuclear-spin quantum memories or registers.
method: The authors use negatively charged boron vacancy defects in hBN under a 3 T magnetic field and analyze the central-spin dynamics of the surrounding nuclear bath, identifying shell-structured nuclear spin classes.
result: They observe an essentially 2D central-spin regime and millisecond-scale coherence of the nuclear shells around the defect.
conclusion: These findings establish hBN boron-vacancy defects as a viable hybrid quantum platform for coherent nuclear-spin control and potential quantum memory applications.

title: Lower Bounding The Secret Key Capacity Of Bosonic Gaussian Channels Via Optimal Gaussian Measurements
authors: Giuseppe Ortolano, Stefano Pirandola, And Leonardo Banchi
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Ortolano, Stefano Pirandola, and Leonardo Banchi

We find the maximum rate achievable in the private communication over a bosonic quantum channel with a fully Gaussian protocol based on optimal single-mode Gaussian measurements. This rate establishes a lower bound on the secret rate capacity of the channel. We focus on the class of phase-insensitiv…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042464] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a lower bound on the secret key capacity of bosonic Gaussian channels using optimal single-mode Gaussian measurements within fully Gaussian protocols.
motivation: Secret key capacity of bosonic Gaussian channels is difficult to characterize exactly, so computable lower bounds based on practical Gaussian protocols are valuable for quantum communication theory.
method: The authors optimize Gaussian protocols with single-mode Gaussian measurements to find the maximum private communication rate achievable over phase-insensitive bosonic Gaussian channels.
result: They obtain a new lower bound on the secret key capacity for this channel class, corresponding to the best rate attainable by the considered Gaussian measurement strategies.
conclusion: The work provides improved capacity benchmarks for Gaussian quantum channels and clarifies the performance limits of Gaussian measurement-based key distribution protocols.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems can permanently retain memory of their initial state and early dynamics, revealing ergodicity breaking beyond conventional quantum scarring.
motivation: Classical ergodic systems are expected to forget initial conditions, but quantum systems can evade thermalization in ways not fully captured by existing scarring mechanisms.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for quantum dynamics that identifies and characterizes persistent initial-state memory, termed 'quantum birthmarks', in systems that break ergodicity.
result: They show that quantum systems can retain a lasting imprint of their initial state and early-time evolution, defying classical ergodic expectations and extending ergodicity breaking beyond known scarring phenomena.
conclusion: These findings establish a broader class of quantum ergodicity breaking with observable memory effects, with implications for quantum thermalization and the foundations of quantum statistical mechanics.

title: Photon Pairs, Squeezed Light, And The Quantum Wave-mixing Effect In A Cascaded Qubit System
authors: R. D. Ivanovskikh, W. V. Pogosov, A. A. Elistratov, S. V. Remizov, A. Yu. Dmitriev, T. R. Sabirov, A. V. Vasenin, S. A. Gunin, And O. V. Astafiev
abstract:
Author(s): R. D. Ivanovskikh, W. V. Pogosov, A. A. Elistratov, S. V. Remizov, A. Yu. Dmitriev, T. R. Sabirov, A. V. Vasenin, S. A. Gunin, and O. V. Astafiev

We develop a theoretical description of quantum wave mixing (QWM) in a cascaded waveguide-QED system of two superconducting qubits, where the probe is driven by an external coherent tone and by the resonance fluorescence of a strongly driven source qubit. Starting from the field correlation function…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043741] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of quantum wave mixing in a cascaded waveguide-QED system of two superconducting qubits driven by a coherent probe and resonance fluorescence.
motivation: To understand photon-pair generation, squeezed light, and quantum wave-mixing effects in cascaded superconducting-qubit waveguide-QED architectures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical description starting from field correlation functions for a two-qubit cascaded system with a strongly driven source qubit.
result: The analysis characterizes quantum wave mixing and photon-pair/squeezed-light emission arising from the interplay of coherent driving and resonance fluorescence in the cascaded qubit setup.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for quantum wave mixing in superconducting waveguide-QED systems, relevant to hybrid quantum platform characterization and quantum optical control.

title: Charging Efficiency Bursts In A Quantum Battery With Cyclic Indefinite Causal Order
authors: Po-Rong Lai, Hsien-Chao Jan, Jhen-Dong Lin, And Yueh-Nan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Po-Rong Lai, Hsien-Chao Jan, Jhen-Dong Lin, and Yueh-Nan Chen

Enhancement of quantum battery performance is a popular subject in quantum thermodynamics. An interesting phenomenon is the quick charging effect [
tldr: The paper studies how a cyclic indefinite causal order, realized via a quantum switch/superposition of trajectories, can produce bursts of enhanced charging efficiency in a quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a promising platform in quantum thermodynamics, and recent work showed that superposing trajectories ('quick charging') can boost charging power; the authors ask whether cyclic indefinite causal order can further enhance and structure this advantage.
method: They model a quantum battery charged through an interferometric superposition of causal orders arranged in a cyclic configuration, and evaluate charging efficiency/power as a function of the control and cycle parameters, likely within an open-system or unitary charging framework.
result: Cyclic indefinite causal order yields pronounced non-monotonic 'bursts' of charging efficiency, outperforming definite-order charging schemes over identifiable parameter regimes tied to the interference of causal trajectories.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order is established as a usable resource for improving quantum battery performance and for engineering structured, burst-like charging dynamics, motivating further study of causal-order effects in thermodynamic tasks.

title: Phase-space Representations Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Enrico Bozzetto And Jonte R. Hance
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Bozzetto and Jonte R. Hance

We connect the structure theorem for quasiprobability representations to quantum error correction. For a code space invariant under a subgroup of an extended Weyl-Heisenberg group, the Brif-Mann construction gives a semifunctorial representation whenever its kernel satisfies the Stratonovich-Weyl ax…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043076] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper connects the structure theorem for quasiprobability representations to quantum error-correcting codes via the Brif-Mann construction for code spaces invariant under an extended Weyl-Heisenberg subgroup.
motivation: It aims to understand how phase-space and quasiprobability representation methods can describe quantum error-correcting code spaces.
method: The authors use the structure theorem for quasiprobability representations and the Stratonovich-Weyl axioms to determine when the Brif-Mann construction yields a semifunctorial representation.
result: For a code space invariant under a subgroup of an extended Weyl-Heisenberg group, the Brif-Mann construction gives a semifunctorial representation whenever its kernel satisfies the Stratonovich-Weyl axioms.
conclusion: This establishes a link between quantum error correction and phase-space representation theory, showing that group-invariant code spaces admit quasiprobability descriptions under suitable kernel conditions.

title: Entropy Transport Through A Superfluid Quantum Point Contact: A Keldysh Field-theory Approach
authors: Davide Bertolusso, C. J. Bolech, And Thierry Giamarchi
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Bertolusso, C. J. Bolech, and Thierry Giamarchi

We study the matter and entropy transport between two ultracold neutral Fermi-gas reservoirs linked by a quantum point contact under a chemical-potential gradient. We describe the two leads with a BCS mean-field model and derive the current-bias characteristics for both particle and entropy transpor…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043066] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies particle and entropy transport between two ultracold Fermi-gas reservoirs coupled by a quantum point contact under a chemical-potential gradient.
motivation: Understanding entropy flow in mesoscopic quantum transport is important for non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and for characterizing dissipation and information flow in strongly correlated quantum systems.
