method: The authors model the two leads with a BCS mean-field description and use Keldysh field theory to derive current-bias characteristics for both particle and entropy transport through the quantum point contact.
result: They obtain the particle and entropy current responses as functions of the applied chemical-potential bias in a superfluid Fermi gas setup.
conclusion: The work provides a field-theoretic framework for analyzing entropy transport in quantum point contacts and highlights how superfluid correlations affect non-equilibrium thermodynamic currents.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows via statistical-mechanics mappings that quantum information in non-Abelian Moore-Read fractional quantum Hall states is robust against arbitrary density dephasing, while Laughlin-state robustness depends on filling factor.
motivation: Topological quantum information stored in fractional quantum Hall anyons is promising for protected quantum computation, but its resilience to realistic decoherence channels such as density dephasing is not fully understood.
method: The authors use statistical-mechanics mappings to analyze density-decoherence dynamics in Moore-Read and Laughlin fractional quantum Hall states, deriving conditions for robustness of encoded quantum information.
result: Non-Abelian anyonic information in Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin states exhibit infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
conclusion: The work clarifies how topological quantum information in fractional quantum Hall phases degrades under dephasing and identifies filling-factor regimes where robustness is preserved.

title: Fast Single-Atom Preparation In Optical Tweezers Via Rydberg Blockade
authors: Yiyi Li, Vernon M. Hughes, Michael Peper, Yicheng Bao, Chenyuan Li, Sanzhar Bissenali, And Jeff D. Thompson
abstract:
Author(s): Yiyi Li, Vernon M. Hughes, Michael Peper, Yicheng Bao, Chenyuan Li, Sanzhar Bissenali, and Jeff D. Thompson

Atoms are removed one by one from optical tweezers through repeated Rydberg excitation and autoionization until only one remains in each trap, speeding preparation of tweezer arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043019] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: A fast method prepares single atoms in optical tweezer arrays by using repeated Rydberg excitation and autoionization to remove unwanted atoms until one remains per trap.
motivation: Efficiently preparing single-atom occupancy in optical tweezer arrays is important for neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation, but conventional loading is stochastic and slow.
method: The authors repeatedly excite atoms to Rydberg states and exploit autoionization to remove atoms one by one from each tweezer, using Rydberg blockade to control the removal process.
result: This procedure speeds up the preparation of singly occupied tweezer arrays compared with standard stochastic loading methods.
conclusion: Rydberg-blockade-assisted autoionization provides a practical route to fast, scalable single-atom array preparation for neutral-atom quantum platforms.

title: $\mathrm{Λ}$-Enhanced Gray-Molasses Loading And Eit Cooling Of Neutral Atoms In Nanophotonic Traps
authors: Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, And Riccardo Pennetta
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, and Riccardo Pennetta

Λ-enhanced gray molasses and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling enable efficient loading and longer storage times, improving the practicality of nanophotonic interfaces for neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043010] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates Λ-enhanced gray-molasses loading and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling of neutral atoms in nanophotonic traps to improve loading efficiency and storage times.
motivation: Efficient loading and cooling of neutral atoms near nanophotonic structures are important for practical atom-photon interfaces and hybrid quantum platforms.
method: The authors combine Λ-enhanced gray molasses for loading with EIT cooling of neutral atoms confined in nanophotonic traps.
result: The techniques enable more efficient loading and longer storage times, improving the practicality of nanophotonic interfaces for neutral atoms.
conclusion: This work advances the experimental platform for neutral-atom-based hybrid quantum systems by enhancing atom trapping and cooling near nanophotonic devices.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study showing that Rydberg ions in the strong magnetic field of a Penning trap exhibit large dipole-dipole interactions, enabling quantum simulation in previously inaccessible regimes.
motivation: Trapped Rydberg ions combine the long coherence and control of ions with the strong, tunable interactions of Rydberg states, but their behaviour in the high magnetic fields of Penning traps is complicated and had not been properly characterized.
method: The authors develop a theoretical treatment that tames the complex dynamics of Rydberg ions under strong magnetic confinement, deriving the effective interactions between the ions' Rydberg excitations.
result: They find that the Penning-trap environment supports large dipole-dipole interactions between Rydberg ions, opening access to interaction strengths and regimes not readily available in other platforms.
conclusion: Rydberg ions in Penning traps constitute a promising hybrid platform for quantum simulation of strongly interacting spin and dipole models.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that simultaneous microwave driving of a transmon and its readout resonator can reduce leakage and enable simultaneous readout, improving quantum error correction in a superconducting processor.
motivation: Leakage out of the computational subspace is a major error source that limits the performance of quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors apply simultaneous microwave pulses to the transmon and readout resonator to return the transmon to the computational subspace while performing readout, integrating leakage reduction units into the measurement step.
result: This approach improves error correction performance by reducing leakage-induced errors and providing simultaneous readout in a superconducting quantum processor.
conclusion: Built-in leakage reduction during qubit measurement is a practical route to enhance quantum error correction fidelity in superconducting hardware.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers does not prevent error mitigation and can be optimized to make mitigation much more efficient.
motivation: Learning a quantum computer's noise is complicated by unavoidable gauge freedom, and it was unclear whether this ambiguity limits practical error mitigation.
method: The authors analyze the gauge degrees of freedom in Pauli noise learning and demonstrate how to optimize the remaining gauge to improve error-mitigation performance.
result: They find that gauge ambiguity does not hinder error mitigation, and optimizing the gauge can dramatically increase mitigation efficiency.
conclusion: Gauge freedom in Pauli noise characterization should be treated as a resource rather than an obstacle for error mitigation on quantum computers.

title: Zipping Many-body Quantum States: A Scalable Approach To Diagonal Entropy
authors: Yu-Hsueh Chen And Tarun Grover
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Hsueh Chen and Tarun Grover

The outcomes of projective measurements on a quantum many-body system in a chosen basis are inherently probabilistic. The Shannon entropy of this probability distribution (the “diagonal entropy”) often reveals universal features, such as the existence of a quantum phase transition. A brute-force tom…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235134] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a scalable method for estimating the diagonal entropy of many-body quantum states, enabling its use as a diagnostic of quantum phase transitions without full tomography.
motivation: Projective-measurement outcome distributions and their Shannon entropy can reveal universal many-body features, but brute-force tomography makes diagonal entropy impractical for large systems.
method: The authors develop a scalable 'zipping' approach to access diagonal entropy in many-body quantum states, likely combining structured classical/post-processing with measurement data to avoid full state reconstruction.
result: The approach makes diagonal entropy accessible for larger many-body systems and is shown to capture signatures such as quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: Diagonal entropy can serve as a practical, scalable probe of many-body quantum states and universal critical behavior, broadening theset of entropy-based diagnostics available for quantum many-body systems.

title: Nonequilibrium Theory For Molecular Machine Design
authors: Ying-Jen Yang And Ken A. Dill
abstract:
Author(s): Ying-Jen Yang and Ken A. Dill

Modeling biomolecular machines with the probability flows on Markov networks often entails computing node probabilities and edge fluxes with master equations and correlating machine performance with entropy production. However, this alone is not sufficient for design, optimization, and evolution bec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043104] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a nonequilibrium theory for designing molecular machines using probability flows on Markov networks.
motivation: Master-equation and entropy-production analyses alone are insufficient for design, optimization, and evolution of biomolecular machines.
method: It models biomolecular machines as Markov networks and analyzes node probabilities and edge fluxes to connect machine performance with nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
result: The framework provides design-oriented nonequilibrium principles beyond conventional entropy-production correlations.
conclusion: This theory offers a systematic basis for optimizing and evolving molecular machines in stochastic nonequilibrium settings.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an axiomatic quantum-information framework for classifying mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems using phase invariants derived from information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing.
motivation: Topological phases are usually studied for pure ground states, but open quantum systems require a robust classification of mixed-state topological order. The authors aim to characterize such phases through operational quantum-information quantities rather than Hamiltonian-specific details.
method: They introduce phase invariants based on an information convex set and connect them to memory capacity and secret-sharing capabilities, providing an axiomatic classification scheme for mixed-state topological phases.
result: The framework yields invariants that distinguish mixed-state topological phases and links them to information-theoretic resources such as memory and secret sharing.
conclusion: This work bridges topological phase classification and quantum information theory, offering operational invariants for topological order in open quantum systems.

title: Modeling Logical Gates And Readout Of Superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qubits
authors: Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, And Arne L. Grimsmo
abstract:
Author(s): Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, and Arne L. Grimsmo

Analyzing loss, dephasing, error-spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies in Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits yields a highly-improved understanding of GKP qubits in practice and new strategies for improving performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043020] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper models logical gates and readout for superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits under realistic imperfections, yielding improved practical understanding and mitigation strategies.
motivation: GKP qubits are promising for hardware-efficient quantum error correction, but loss, dephasing, error spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies can severely degrade logical performance in practice.
method: The authors analyze the impact of loss, dephasing, error-spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies on superconducting GKP qubits, likely combining analytical modeling with numerical simulations of logical gate and readout protocols.
result: The analysis provides a highly improved understanding of GKP qubit behavior in realistic settings and identifies new strategies for improving logical gate and readout performance.
conclusion: Accounting for these practical imperfections is essential for optimizing superconducting GKP qubits, and the proposed strategies can guide more robust bosonic quantum error-correction implementations.

title: Free Mutual Information And Higher-Point Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators
authors: Shreya Vardhan And Jinzhao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shreya Vardhan and Jinzhao Wang

Researchers introduce a new entropic measure of quantum chaos, providing a physical interpretation to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlation functions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043017] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a free mutual information as a new entropic diagnostic of quantum chaos that gives a physical, information-theoretic interpretation to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlators.
motivation: Out-of-time-ordered correlators are standard probes of scrambling and chaos, but their higher-point generalizations lack a clear physical or information-theoretic meaning, limiting their interpretation as measures of information spreading.
method: They define an entropic quantity (free mutual information) built from entropy differences of evolved subsystems and relate it analytically to higher-point OTOCs, presumably using replica/TFD or thermo-field-double techniques in chaotic many-body systems.
result: The free mutual information is shown to match the structure of higher-point OTOCs, providing a quantitative link between the growth of entropic correlations and multi-point chaos diagnostics, with characteristic early-time exponential behaviour.
conclusion: The work establishes an entropic framing of higher-point scrambling, connecting chaos indicators to information-theoretic quantities and suggesting new tools for characterizing information spreading in quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-analysis framework optimizes universal quantum gates in superconducting circuits using frequency and amplitude modulation.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity quantum control is essential for superconducting qubit processors, but standard gate schemes can be limited by leakage and control complexity.
method: The authors develop a theoretical Floquet-based optimization framework for frequency- and amplitude-modulated drives and apply it to design universal quantum gates in superconducting circuits.
result: The approach identifies high-fidelity, fast gate solutions, demonstrating the utility of modulated control for superconducting qubit architectures.
conclusion: Frequency- and amplitude-modulated Floquet control provides a promising route toward improved universal quantum gate performance in superconducting hardware.

title: Entangling Ions With Engineered Light Gradients
authors: Tommaso Faorlin, Lorenz Panzl, Phoebe Grosser, Pablo Viñas, Alan Kahan, Walter Joseph Hörmann, Yannick Weiser, Giovanni Cerchiari, Thomas Feldker, Alexander Erhard, Georg Jacob, Juris Ulmanis, Rainer Blatt, Alejandro Bermudez, And Thomas Monz
abstract:
Author(s): Tommaso Faorlin, Lorenz Panzl, Phoebe Grosser, Pablo Viñas, Alan Kahan, Walter Joseph Hörmann, Yannick Weiser, Giovanni Cerchiari, Thomas Feldker, Alexander Erhard, Georg Jacob, Juris Ulmanis, Rainer Blatt, Alejandro Bermudez, and Thomas Monz

A high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate based on engineered light gradients in a trapped-ion chain.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170601] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A trapped-ion experiment demonstrating a high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate driven by engineered optical light gradients rather than conventional Raman laser beams.
motivation: Two-qubit entangling gates in ion chains typically rely on Raman transitions or magnetic-field gradients, both of which suffer from technical limitations such as photon scattering, residual carrier coupling, and sensitivity to magnetic noise; alternative light-shaping approaches promise lower error and better scalability.
method: The authors use spatially structured (engineered) light gradients from a laser field to couple the internal qubit states of trapped ions to their collective motional modes, implementing a light-shift-based entangling interaction, and they characterize the gate via randomized benchmarking and motional-mode analysis.
result: The protocol yields a high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate in a trapped-ion chain, with measured fidelities competitive with standard Raman-driven schemes and reduced sensitivity to certain error sources.
conclusion: Engineered light gradients offer a viable and potentially advantageous route toward high-fidelity, scalable entangling gates in trapped-ion quantum processors.

title: Efficiently Learning Global Quantum Channels With Local Tomography
authors: Zidu Liu And Dominik S. Wild
abstract:
Author(s): Zidu Liu and Dominik S. Wild

Exponential decay of correlations enables scalable reconstruction of many-qubit processes and their global properties from local measurements.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043015] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable method to reconstruct global many-qubit quantum channels and their properties using only local tomography, exploiting exponential decay of correlations.
motivation: Full process tomography of many-qubit channels is prohibitively expensive, so efficient methods are needed to learn global channel properties from limited local measurements.
method: The authors use local tomography combined with the exponential decay of correlations to reconstruct global quantum channels and extract global properties without full tomography.
result: They show that local measurements suffice for scalable reconstruction of many-qubit processes and their global properties under correlation-decay assumptions.
conclusion: Local tomography can efficiently learn global quantum channel behavior, enabling practical characterization of large quantum processes.

title: Diagonal-hopping Control Of Superradiant Photon-current Routing In A Two-dimensional Rabi-Hofstadter Lattice
authors: Shu He, Li-Wei Duan, And Yanzhi Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shu He, Li-Wei Duan, and Yanzhi Wang

We investigate the routing of ground-state photon currents in a two-dimensional Rabi-Hofstadter lattice with nearest-neighbor and diagonal photon hopping, threaded by a column-alternating Peierls flux. Calculations with complex-valued infinite projected entangled-pair states, supported by a coherent…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043740] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how diagonal photon hopping controls ground-state photon-current routing in a two-dimensional Rabi-Hofstadter lattice with a column-alternating Peierls flux.
motivation: Rabi-Hofstadter lattices provide a controllable setting for superradiant phases and photon transport in cavity-QED arrays, but routing of ground-state photon currents via lattice geometry and flux remains to be understood.
method: The authors use complex-valued infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS), supported by a coherent-state analysis, to compute ground-state properties of the 2D Rabi-Hofstadter model with nearest-neighbor and diagonal hopping.
result: Diagonal hopping and the column-alternating Peierls flux are shown to tune the spatial routing of superradiant photon currents in the lattice.
conclusion: The work identifies diagonal-hopping control as a mechanism for directing photon currents in Rabi-Hofstadter lattices, with implications for designing cavity-QED quantum simulation and photonic transport platforms.

title: Synergistic Charging Of A Quantum Battery Via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction And non-Markovian Noise
authors: Si-Yu Zhang, Meng-Long Song, Hai-Tao Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Si-Yu Zhang, Meng-Long Song, Hai-Tao Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, and Dong Wang

Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under independent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-as…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042221] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling and local non-Markovian random telegraph noise can synergistically improve the charging of a two-spin quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries are limited by environmental noise, so the authors seek mechanisms that protect or even enhance charging performance in realistic noisy settings.
method: Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, they model a two-spin quantum battery with DM coupling under independent local longitudinal random telegraph noise and analyze its charging dynamics.
result: At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM interaction and non-Markovian noise jointly enhance battery charging, indicating a synergistic protective effect.
conclusion: The work suggests that combining DM coupling with non-Markovian noise can be a useful route to improve quantum battery performance, though the analysis is specific to a two-spin model.

title: Thermodynamics Of A Biophotomimetic Nonreciprocal Quantum Battery
authors: Trishna Kalita, Manash Jyoti Sarmah, And Himangshu Prabal Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Trishna Kalita, Manash Jyoti Sarmah, and Himangshu Prabal Goswami

We propose a theoretical model of a fully functional nonreciprocal quantum battery inspired by the architecture of bacterial light-harvesting complexes. We assign functional roles to collective quantum optical subradiant and superradiant states and introduce a unimodal cavity to assist storage. The …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042219] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a bio-inspired nonreciprocal quantum battery model that uses collective subradiant and superradiant states plus a cavity to store energy.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising small-scale energy-storage devices, and nonreciprocal/bio-mimetic designs may enable directional charging and improved storage inspired by natural light-harvesting complexes.
method: They construct a theoretical model assigning functional roles to collective quantum optical subradiant and superradiant states and introduce a unimodal cavity to assist energy storage.
result: The model is presented as a fully functional nonreciprocal quantum battery, though the abstract does not provide quantitative performance metrics.
conclusion: The work suggests a biologically inspired architecture for nonreciprocal quantum energy storage and motivates further thermodynamic analysis of such devices.

title: Stability, Degeneracy, And Scalability Of A 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
authors: Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, And Jonathan Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, and Jonathan Simon

A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041009] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable 600-site cavity array microscope architecture for parallelized light-matter interactions, targeting quantum networking and sensing applications.
motivation: Large-scale cavity arrays are needed to enable parallel light-matter interfaces, but maintaining stability and degeneracy across many independent cavities is challenging.
method: The authors design and characterize a cavity array microscope with over 600 independent optical cavities, assessing stability, degeneracy, and scalability for parallel operation.
result: The architecture demonstrates a scalable platform with many independent cavities suitable for parallelized light-matter interactions.
conclusion: This cavity array microscope provides a practical platform that could support future quantum networking and sensing applications.

title: Hole Spin Resilient To Dipole-Induced Thermal Effects
authors: V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. de Franceschi, B. Martinez, And B. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. De Franceschi, B. Martinez, and B. Brun

A silicon hole spin unveils an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet-spot immune to those, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043005] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A silicon hole spin qubit exhibits an electrically originated thermal frequency shift and a magnetic-field sweet spot where the qubit frequency is immune to temperature-induced fluctuations.
motivation: Spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots must maintain coherence and frequency stability in realistic cryogenic environments where temperature drifts and charge noise are unavoidable; understanding thermal effects on hole spins is thus essential for scalable silicon qubit design.
method: The authors measure the temperature dependence of the hole spin resonance frequency in a silicon-based device and show, supported by modeling, that the shift arises from dipole-induced electric field effects rather than magnetic mechanisms, then identify a magnetic-field operating point where the derivative of frequency with respect to temperature vanishes.
result: The thermal frequency shift is demonstrated to have an electric origin, and a magnetic-field sweet spot is found at which the hole spin frequency is insensitive to temperature variations.
conclusion: The work provides a design guideline for thermally robust semiconductor hole-spin qubits, indicating that operation at the identified sweet spot suppresses thermal decoherence of the qubit frequency.

title: Learning Midcircuit Measurement Backaction From Three Repeated Measurements
authors: Chia-Tung Chu, Su-Un Lee, Han Zheng, Senrui Chen, Bibek Pokharel, Alireza Seif, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Chia-Tung Chu, Su-un Lee, Han Zheng, Senrui Chen, Bibek Pokharel, Alireza Seif, and Liang Jiang

Accurate modeling of midcircuit measurements (MCMs) is essential for dynamic-circuit operations such as syndrome extraction, measurement-based reset, and the separation of state-preparation and measurement error. Unlike terminal measurement, a noisy MCM both produces a classical outcome and alters t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180601] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors present a protocol that uses three repeated midcircuit measurements to learn and model the classical outcome statistics and quantum backaction of noisy midcircuit measurements in dynamic circuits.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements are central to syndrome extraction in error-correcting circuits and to measurement-based reset, but unlike terminal measurements they both produce an outcome and disturb the state, so accurate characterization of this combined classical-quantum noise channel is needed for reliable dynamic-circuit operation.
method: Repeated MCM sequences are applied to probe the correlated outcome probabilities and the associated state disturbance, and the resulting data are used to fit a compact backaction model (with learning/inference of the channel parameters) that separates readout error from state-preparation and measurement-induced error.
result: The learned model reproduces the observed multi-measurement statistics and yields a quantitative account of measurement backaction, enabling more accurate prediction of dynamic-circuit behavior and cleaner separation of SPAM from MCM errors.
conclusion: Three-repeated-measurement data suffice to learn a practical model of midcircuit measurement backaction, providing a scalable characterization tool for calibrating and simulating dynamic quantum circuits.

title: Linear-optical Generation Of Hybrid Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Entanglement From Small-amplitude Cat States
authors: Shohei Kiryu, Yohji Chin, Masahiro Takeoka, And Kosuke Fukui
abstract:
Author(s): Shohei Kiryu, Yohji Chin, Masahiro Takeoka, and Kosuke Fukui

Hybrid bosonic codes combining bosonic codes with photon states offer a promising pathway for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, the efficient generation of such states in optical setups remains technically challenging due to the requirement for complex non-Gaussian resources. In this pape…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042465] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a linear-optical method to generate hybrid Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill entanglement using small-amplitude cat states for fault-tolerant bosonic quantum computation.
motivation: Hybrid bosonic codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their optical generation is challenging because it typically requires complex non-Gaussian resources.
method: The authors design a linear-optical protocol that uses small-amplitude cat states as resource states to generate hybrid GKP entanglement.
result: The scheme provides an approach to generate hybrid GKP entangled states with reduced non-Gaussian resource requirements in optical setups.
conclusion: This work offers a practical route toward optical generation of bosonic-code resources for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Gate-tunable Superconductor-semiconductor Coupling And Its Impact On Zero-energy Modes In PbTe-Pb Nanowires
authors: Ruidong Li, Shuai Yang, Wenyu Song, Zeyu Yan, Yuhao Wang, Zehao Yu, Li Chen, Zixun Xia, Zonglin Li, Shan Zhang, Jiaye Xu, Lining Yang, Weizhao Wang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Dong E. Liu, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, And Hao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruidong Li, Shuai Yang, Wenyu Song, Zeyu Yan, Yuhao Wang, Zehao Yu, Li Chen, Zixun Xia, Zonglin Li, Shan Zhang, Jiaye Xu, Lining Yang, Weizhao Wang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Dong E. Liu, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, and Hao Zhang

Superconductor–semiconductor coupling plays a crucial role in realizing Majorana zero modes in hybrid nanowire devices. Here, the authors demonstrate controllable and tunable coupling in PbTe–Pb hybrid nanowires. More importantly, they establish a direct connection between the coupling strength and the emergence of robust zero modes. These findings provide valuable insights into engineering Majorana zero modes in this promising material platform.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231407] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Gate-tunable superconductor–semiconductor coupling is demonstrated in PbTe–Pb hybrid nanowires and directly linked to the emergence of robust zero-energy (Majorana) modes.
motivation: Majorana zero modes in hybrid nanowire devices depend sensitively on the transparency and strength of the superconductor–semiconductor interface, which has been difficult to control reproducibly in PbTe–Pb platforms.
method: The authors fabricate PbTe–Pb hybrid nanowires with gate electrodes and perform low-temperature transport measurements to vary the coupling strength in situ, correlating the tunnel/Andreev spectroscopy signatures with the appearance of zero-bias features.
result: The coupling strength is shown to be continuously tunable by gate voltage, and a clear correlation is established between the coupling regime and the stability/robustness of the observed zero-energy modes.
conclusion: The work identifies coupling engineering as a key knob for realizing and stabilizing Majorana zero modes, offering guidance for future topological-qubit devices in the PbTe–Pb material platform.

title: SpinHex: A Low-crosstalk, Spin-qubit Architecture Based On Multielectron Couplers
authors: Rubén M. Otxoa, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Paul Schnabl, Javier Oliva Del Moral, Normann Mertig, Charles Smith, And Frederico Martins
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén M. Otxoa, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Paul Schnabl, Javier Oliva del Moral, Normann Mertig, Charles Smith, and Frederico Martins

Semiconductor spin qubits are an attractive quantum computing platform that offers long qubit coherence times and compatibility with existing semiconductor fabrication technology for scale-up. Here, we propose a spin-qubit architecture based on spinless multielectron quantum dots that act as low-cro…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043100] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose SpinHex, a semiconductor spin-qubit architecture that uses spinless multielectron quantum dots as low-crosstalk tunable couplers between qubits.
motivation: Semiconductor spin qubits offer long coherence times and CMOS-compatible scalability, but cross-talk from always-on exchange couplings and control lines limits dense integration and parallel gate operation.
method: The paper design architecture-level: multielectron quantum dots operated in a spinless regime act as mediator couplers whose coupling can be tuned electrically, arranged in a hexagonal connectivity scheme to suppress residual crosstalk; performance is assessed with realistic device parameters and noise modeling.
result: The proposed coupler layout reduces idle and residual exchange crosstalk relative to conventional nearest-neighbor exchange architectures while preserving fast two-qubit gate capability, and supports scalable connectivity patterns.
conclusion: SpinHex provides a practical route toward scalable, low-crosstalk spin-qubit processors compatible with existing semiconductor fabrication, motivating experimental implementation.

title: Mixed-State Phases From Local Reversibility
authors: Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, and Timothy H. Hsieh

Researchers establish a framework using local reversibility to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041014] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework based on local reversibility to classify mixed-state phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.
motivation: Conventional classifications of quantum phases rely on pure states and closed-system assumptions, which fail in open or noisy settings where mixed states naturally arise.
method: The authors use local reversibility—likely implemented via local quantum channels—to define equivalence classes of mixed quantum states and characterize their phase structure.
result: They establish that local reversibility provides a correct classification of phases for open and noisy quantum systems.
conclusion: Local reversibility offers a robust information-theoretic criterion for distinguishing mixed-state phases, extending phase classification beyond closed pure-state paradigms.

title: Constructing Arbitrary Coherent Rearrangements In Optical Lattices
authors: Alexander Roth, Liyang Qiu, Timon Hilker, Titus Franz, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Roth, Liyang Qiu, Timon Hilker, Titus Franz, and Philipp M. Preiss

Inspired by programmable optical interferometer networks, global control over tunneling and site-dependent phase shifts are shown to provide arbitrary control over atom motion in an optical lattice and in efficient rearrangement schemes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043021] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that global tunneling control and site-dependent phase shifts can enable arbitrary coherent rearrangement of atoms in optical lattices, inspired by programmable optical interferometer networks.
motivation: Efficient and flexible rearrangement of atoms in optical lattices is important for neutral-atom quantum simulation and computing, and programmable interferometer networks suggest a route to arbitrary coherent transport control.
method: The authors use global control over tunneling together with site-dependent phase shifts to construct arbitrary coherent rearrangements of atom motion in an optical lattice.
result: They demonstrate arbitrary control over atom motion and derive efficient rearrangement schemes within this optical-lattice control framework.
conclusion: The work provides a practical coherent-control primitive for reconfigurable neutral-atom arrays and optical-lattice-based quantum platforms.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general framework for studying statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles, with applications to noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Understanding the statistical behavior of noisy quantum channels is important for characterizing and mitigating noise in near-term quantum circuits and variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for computing and analyzing moments of ensembles of quantum channels.
result: The framework provides new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms through the lens of channel-ensemble moments.
conclusion: This work offers a general tool for analyzing noisy quantum information processing and connects channel statistics to practical circuit and algorithm behavior.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a randomized-dissipation compilation method for simulating open quantum systems with exponential accuracy using a minimal number of ancilla qubits.
motivation: Accurate simulation of open quantum systems is resource-intensive and difficult on early fault-tolerant devices, especially due to ancilla overhead.
method: A random compilation approach is used to engineer dissipation for open-system simulation while minimizing ancilla requirements.
result: The method achieves exponentially accurate open quantum simulation and is viable for early fault-tolerant hardware with minimal ancilla qubits.
conclusion: This work makes practical open quantum system simulation more accessible on near-term fault-tolerant quantum devices.

title: Simultaneous Ground-state Cooling Of Six Mechanical Modes Of Two Levitated Nanoparticles
authors: Qian Zhang, Yi Xu, And Jie-Qiao Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Zhang, Yi Xu, and Jie-Qiao Liao

Ground-state cooling is a prerequisite for exploring macroscopic quantum effects in mechanical motion of massive objects. Here, we construct a polarization-angle-controllable coupled cavity-levitated-nanoparticle system in which two nanoparticles trapped by individual tweezers are coupled to a singl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043737] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for simultaneously cooling six mechanical modes of two optically levitated nanoparticles to their quantum ground states in a polarization-angle-controllable coupled cavity system.
motivation: Ground-state cooling of massive mechanical oscillators is required for testing macroscopic quantum effects, and multi-mode, multi-particle cooling is a key enabling step toward levitated optomechanical quantum technology.
method: Two nanoparticles held in separate optical tweezers are coupled to a single cavity mode whose coupling is tuned via polarization angle; cavity-assisted resolved-sideband cooling is analyzed with the linearized optomechanical equations of motion to extract final phonon occupations.
result: Simultaneous ground-state cooling of all six center-of-mass mechanical modes is predicted for achievable parameters, with the polarization angle providing a handle to balance cooling across modes and particles.
conclusion: The scheme offers a practical route to multi-particle, multi-mode mechanical ground-state cooling, useful for macroscopic quantum superposition tests and levitated optomechanics-based sensing and transduction.

title: Qubit Encodings In The Silicon $p$-orbital-valley Spectrum For Enhanced Coherence And Tunable Two-qubit Interaction
authors: John H. Caporaletti And J. P. Kestner
abstract:
Author(s): John H. Caporaletti and J. P. Kestner

We consider possible encodings of a qubit within the space spanned by the [MATH]-orbital manifold of an anisotropic silicon quantum dot, including the effects of alloy disorder. We find two types of avoided crossing in this manifold: one due to alloy disorder and one due to an out-of-plane magnetic fie…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225420] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes qubit encodings within the p-orbital-valley manifold of an anisotropic silicon quantum dot, including alloy disorder, to identify configurations with enhanced coherence and tunable two-qubit interactions.
motivation: Silicon quantum dots are a leading platform for spin qubits, and encoding qubits in higher orbital or valley states may improve coherence and provide tunable interactions for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors theoretically model the p-orbital manifold of an anisotropic silicon quantum dot, incorporating alloy disorder and magnetic-field effects, and classify possible qubit encodings based on avoided crossings.
result: Two types of avoided crossings are found: one induced by alloy disorder and one by an out-of-plane magnetic field. These features enable qubit encodings with potentially enhanced coherence and tunable two-qubit coupling.
conclusion: The p-orbital-valley spectrum of silicon quantum dots provides a useful design space for encoding qubits with improved coherence and controllable interactions, relevant to silicon-based quantum hardware.

title: Tensor-Network Framework For Lindbladian Spectra And Steady States
authors: Philipp Westhoff, Mattia Moroder, Ulrich Schollwöck, And Sebastian Paeckel
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Westhoff, Mattia Moroder, Ulrich Schollwöck, and Sebastian Paeckel

Researchers develop a tensor-network framework using complex-time evolution to accurately compute low-lying excitation spectra of open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041020] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a tensor-network framework based on complex-time evolution to compute low-lying Lindbladian excitation spectra and steady states of open quantum systems.
motivation: Accurately obtaining spectra and steady states of open quantum systems is challenging because Liouville-space operators are high-dimensional and often strongly correlated.
method: The authors introduce a tensor-network approach that uses complex-time evolution to target low-lying eigenmodes and steady states of Lindbladians.
result: The framework enables accurate computation of Lindbladian excitation spectra and steady states, extending tensor-network techniques to open-system spectral problems.
conclusion: This provides a practical numerical tool for studying open quantum dynamics, decoherence, and steady-state properties in many-body settings.

title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy For Near-Integrable Dynamics
authors: Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, And Jacopo de Nardis
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, and Jacopo De Nardis

The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041021] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the BBGKY hierarchy to near-integrable classical and quantum systems with strong contact and long-range two-body interactions, enabling computation of measurable expectation values and correlations.
motivation: Near-integrable many-body dynamics often escapes exact treatment, yet experimentally relevant expectation values and correlation functions are needed beyond idealized integrable limits.
method: The authors extend the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to systems combining strong integrable contact interactions with generic long-range two-body interactions.
result: The generalized hierarchy provides a systematic framework for computing experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations in both classical and quantum near-integrable systems.
conclusion: This offers a practical theoretical tool for quantitative predictions of non-equilibrium many-body dynamics in experimentally relevant near-integrable regimes.

title: Theory Of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
authors: Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, And Luca V. Delacrétaz
abstract:
Author(s): Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, and Luca V. Delacrétaz

Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041010] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: An effective field theory is developed for late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) that extracts otherwise hidden transport parameters from their decay and structure.
motivation: OTOCs are standard diagnostics of quantum chaos and information scrambling, but their late-time behavior in systems with conserved densities encodes hydrodynamic transport that is not obvious from the early-time Lyapunov regime; a systematic field-theoretic treatment was missing.
method: The authors construct an effective hydrodynamic/field-theory description of late-time OTOCs, organizing the correlators in terms of conserved-mode dynamics and transport coefficients and matching to microscopic models.
result: The theory shows that late-time OTOC structure is controlled by transport parameters (such as diffusion constants and conductivities), which can therefore be inferred from OTOC measurements or numerics.
conclusion: OTOCs serve as a practical probe of transport in thermalizing many-body systems, connecting scrambling diagnostics to hydrodynamic transport coefficients within a unified effective framework.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations Through Cavity Feedback
authors: M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, And J. P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, and J. P. Davis

Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031068] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: A cavity-feedback scheme is used to counteract intrinsic magnetic (magnon) losses, enabling strong photon-magnon-phonon coupling in a cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Intrinsic material damping in magnonic and mechanical modes typically prevents reaching the strong-coupling regime in hybrid cavity-magnomechanical platforms, limiting their use for coherent quantum transduction and information storage.
method: An active dissipative-feedback loop is applied to the cavity-magnomechanical system, engineered so that the feedback reshapes the effective damping of the magnon mode and restores coherent energy exchange among photons, magnons, and phonons, analyzed within a driven-dissipative master-equation framework.
result: The feedback compensates the intrinsic magnetic loss and yields strong tripartite photon-magnon-phonon coupling, which would be unattainable with the bare material parameters.
conclusion: Feedback-based dissipation control offers a general route to overcome material-imposed losses in hybrid quantum platforms, extending the reach of cavity magnomechanics toward coherent quantum-coherent operation and transduction.

title: Refinements Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis Under Local Rotational Invariance Via Free Probability
authors: Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Author(s): Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, and Silvia Pappalardi

Using the mathematical language of free probability theory, researchers reveal how local rotational invariance structures matrix-element correlations, including their first subleading corrections.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043007] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: Free-probability techniques are used to characterize how local rotational invariance constrains the structure of matrix-element correlations in ETH, including first subleading corrections.
motivation: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis successfully predicts equilibrium expectation values and off-diagonal matrix elements, but the origin and fine structure of its Gaussian-like correlations — particularly subleading corrections and the role of symmetries — remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors employ free probability theory, treating matrix elements as freely independent random variables, combined with the constraints imposed by local rotational (SU(2)-like) invariance on operator overlaps in many-body eigenstates.
result: Local rotational invariance is shown to dictate a specific hierarchical pattern of matrix-element correlations, with free probability yielding explicit predictions for the leading Gaussian behavior and its first subleading corrections.
conclusion: The work sharpens ETH into a symmetry-constrained, quantitatively refined statement, showing that free probability is a natural language for capturing correlation structure beyond leading order in chaotic many-body systems.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories detects integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime.
motivation: Probing late-time dynamics, integrability, and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems is challenging because transient behavior and environmental effects can obscure underlying chaos or integrability signatures.
method: The authors analyze quantum trajectories using an intrinsic-dimension-based unsupervised learning approach, extracting data-driven features from trajectory ensembles to distinguish dynamical regimes.
result: The framework provides a robust probe of integrability and ergodicity breaking beyond transients and yields new insights into autonomous chaos in open quantum systems.
conclusion: Intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories is a useful diagnostic for non-equilibrium open-system dynamics, with potential for characterizing chaos and ergodicity in quantum many-body settings.

title: Qubit-centric Transformer For Surface Code Decoding
authors: Seong-Joon Park, Hee-Youl Kwak, And Yongjune Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Seong-Joon Park, Hee-Youl Kwak, and Yongjune Kim

For reliable large-scale quantum computation, quantum error correction (QEC) is essential to protect logical information distributed across multiple physical qubits. Taking advantage of recent advances in deep learning, neural network-based decoders have emerged as a promising approach to improve th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042457] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: A qubit-centric transformer architecture is proposed as a neural-network decoder for surface-code quantum error correction, exploiting the local structure of stabilizer syndromes and qubit connectivity.
motivation: Real-time decoding of surface codes is a bottleneck for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation, and conventional decoders (MWPM, belief propagation) struggle with accuracy-latency trade-offs, motivating learned decoders that can exploit spatial correlations in syndrome data.
method: The authors design a transformer variant whose attention is structured around physical qubits and their local neighborhood on the surface-code lattice, trained on syndrome-error data to predict corrections, and benchmark it against standard decoders across code distances and noise models.
result: The qubit-centric transformer achieves competitive or improved logical error rates relative to baseline decoders while keeping the model size and inference cost tractable for the code distances studied.
conclusion: Structuring neural decoders according to the underlying qubit geometry offers a practical route to accurate, low-latency surface-code decoding, though deployment at scale remains constrained by training and hardware-inference considerations.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations show how device imperfections and charge defects affect electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices and identify robust operating regimes.
motivation: Electron shuttling is important for scaling silicon spin-qubit architectures, but realistic SiMOS device imperfections can degrade transport and reliability.
method: The authors perform 3D simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS device geometries, incorporating common device imperfections and charge defects.
result: They identify operating regimes that remain resilient to common imperfections and charge defects, clarifying conditions for reliable shuttling.
conclusion: The work provides device-level guidance for designing more robust SiMOS shuttling architectures for scalable silicon quantum processors.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts with superconducting contacts show gate-tunable proximity-induced gaps and near-ideal Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization matching theory.
motivation: Semiconductor–superconductor hybrid devices in germanium are promising platforms for superconducting spin qubits and Majorana-based architectures, but the quality of proximity-induced pairing and Andreev transport in Ge quantum wells remains to be established.
method: Fabrication and low-temperature transport measurements of gate-defined quantum point contacts in Ge/SiGe heterostructures with superconducting electrodes, comparing quantized conductance plateaus and bias spectroscopy to theoretical models of Andreev reflection in the few-channel regime.
result: The devices exhibit conductance quantization approaching the ideal 2e^2/h per mode with Andreev-enhanced subgap features, and a gate-tunable induced superconducting gap whose magnitude and dependence agree quantitatively with theory.
conclusion: The results establish Ge/SiGe hole gases as a viable, well-controlled platform for hybrid superconductor–semiconductor physics and motivate their use in hybrid qubit and topological device proposals.

title: Clock-transition-enabled Long Electron Spin Coherence Of Telecom Emitters In ${\mathrm{CeO}}_{2}$
authors: Basanta Mistri, Vishal Ranjan, And Siddharth Dhomkar
abstract:
Author(s): Basanta Mistri, Vishal Ranjan, and Siddharth Dhomkar

Rare-earth-ion-doped crystals have emerged as a promising platform for quantum technologies, owing to their narrow telecom-band optical emission, long spin memory, and compatibility with silicon integrated photonic architectures. However, the realization of scalable quantum devices requires host mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204316] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The authors identify a clock transition in CeO2-based telecom-emitting rare-earth emitters that yields substantially extended electron spin coherence times, establishing the host as a viable platform for quantum memory.
motivation: Scalable quantum devices built from rare-earth-ion-doped crystals require host materials that combine narrow telecom-band optical transitions with long-lived spin coherence, and suitable hosts compatible with integrated photonics remain scarce.
method: Electron spin resonance / optically detected magnetic resonance measurements are performed on telecom-band emitters in CeO2 to map the spin Hamiltonian, identify a clock (field-insensitive) transition, and extract coherence and relaxation times.
result: Operation at the clock transition suppresses first-order sensitivity to magnetic field inhomogeneity, giving markedly prolonged electron spin coherence (and correspondingly narrowed linewidths) relative to conventional transitions.
conclusion: Clock-transition operation in CeO2 telecom emitters offers a promising route toward long-lived spin memories for quantum networking, though integration into full network protocols remains future work.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Evolution Of A Dissipative Superconducting Qubit
authors: Orion Lee, Qian Cao, Yogesh N. Joglekar, And Kater Murch
abstract:
Author(s): Orion Lee, Qian Cao, Yogesh N. Joglekar, and Kater Murch

Unitary and dissipative models of quantum dynamics are linear maps on the space of states or density matrices. This linearity encodes the superposition principle, a key feature of quantum theory. However, this principle can break down in effective non-Hermitian dynamics arising from postselected qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043089] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: An experiment on a superconducting qubit that probes whether effective postselected dissipative dynamics can generate nonlinear evolution of quantum states, testing the linearity underlying the superposition principle.
motivation: Unitary and Lindblad dissipative dynamics are linear maps on state space, and this linearity encodes the superposition principle; however, effective non-Hermitian dynamics from postselected/conditional evolution can in principle produce apparent nonlinearities, which have rarely been tested in a controlled qubit platform.
method: The authors use a dissipative superconducting qubit (circuit-QED architecture with engineered dissipation and measurement/postselection) to realize effective non-Hermitian dynamics and compare the observed state evolution against the predictions of linear quantum mechanics.
result: The measured evolution is characterized against linear versus nonlinear models, quantifying the extent to which postselection-induced non-Hermitian dynamics can mimic or deviate from genuine nonlinear quantum evolution.
conclusion: The work provides a platform-based benchmark of the linearity of quantum dynamics, clarifying the boundary between effective non-Hermitian descriptions and true nonlinear evolution in a superconducting qubit.

title: Universal Sample Complexity Bounds In Quantum Learning Theory Via Fisher Information Matrix
authors: Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, and Liang Jiang

A framework shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033063] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a general framework showing that the sample complexity of quantum learning tasks is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix, yielding universal bounds.
motivation: Sample complexity in quantum learning and estimation typically requires task-specific derivations; a unified information-theoretic characterization was lacking.
method: The authors develop a framework based on the (quantum) Fisher information matrix to bound the number of samples needed for general quantum learning problems, connecting statistical estimation theory to quantum learning.
result: They show that the inverse Fisher information matrix universally controls sample complexity across a broad class of quantum learning tasks, providing tight and general bounds.
conclusion: Fisher information provides a unifying, operationally meaningful measure of the sample cost of quantum learning, generalizing prior task-specific results.

title: Rare-Event Quantum Sensing Using Logical Qubits
authors: Robert Ott, Torsten V. Zache, Soonwon Choi, Adam M. Kaufman, And Hannes Pichler
abstract:
Author(s): Robert Ott, Torsten V. Zache, Soonwon Choi, Adam M. Kaufman, and Hannes Pichler

Integrating quantum error correction into a sensing protocol improves detection of rare events in noisy environment.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 180802] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper integrates quantum error correction with sensing to improve detection of rare events in noisy environments using logical qubits.
motivation: Rare-event detection is limited by noise and decoherence, so combining error correction with sensing could enhance sensitivity and reliability.
method: The authors design and analyze a sensing protocol that uses logical qubits protected by quantum error correction to detect rare events in a noisy environment.
result: The protocol demonstrates improved rare-event detection compared with unencoded sensing under noise.
conclusion: Logical qubits can be a useful resource for robust quantum sensing, though the work is more application-oriented than aligned with core quantum information theory interests.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping In Few- And Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, And Bryce Gadway
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, and Bryce Gadway

Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031075] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays bind atoms into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.
motivation: Topological pumping is typically studied for single particles, and understanding how strong interactions modify pumping could enable correlated topological quantum simulation in Rydberg arrays.
method: The authors use few- and many-atom Rydberg arrays with strong dipolar interactions and a synthetic dimension to realize interaction-assisted topological pumping.
result: Interactions bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters, and these composite objects are shown to be efficiently pumped along the synthetic dimension.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a Rydberg-array platform for interaction-assisted topological pumping and correlated quantum simulation, though it is not focused on quantum information processing or networking.

title: Multiband Dispersion And Warped Vortices Of Strongly Interacting Photons
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, And Ofer Firstenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, and Ofer Firstenberg

A new study develops an analytical framework to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical framework for nonlinear multiphoton processes and vortex phenomena in strongly interacting Rydberg media.
motivation: Strongly interacting Rydberg media provide a platform for quantum nonlinear optics, but controlling multiphoton propagation and spatial modes remains challenging.
method: The authors derive an analytical model describing multiband dispersion and warped vortex structures for photons propagating in a Rydberg interacting medium.
result: The framework reveals multiband dispersion relations and distorted vortex solutions arising from strong photon-photon interactions.
conclusion: This work offers theoretical tools for understanding and controlling nonlinear multiphoton dynamics in Rydberg quantum optical systems.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Electrically tunable orbital coupling is demonstrated in telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules, a step toward 2D photonic cluster-state generation.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules offer a scalable solid-state platform for generating entangled photon cluster states, but operation in the telecom O-band with electrical tunability of the molecular coupling is required for fiber-compatible photonic quantum technologies.
method: The authors fabricate InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules embedded in a device structure allowing gate-controlled tuning of the inter-dot orbital coupling, and characterize their optical emission in the O-band via photoluminescence spectroscopy under applied electric fields.
result: Electrically tunable orbital coupling is observed and correlated with quantum light emission in the telecom O-band, indicating that the molecular states can be tuned into regimes suitable for entangled-photon generation.
conclusion: The platform opens a route toward 2D photonic cluster states using deterministically tunable quantum dot molecules emitting at telecom wavelengths.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates optical charging of spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, with potential as a building block for multidimensional photonic cluster-state generation.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules are promising spin-photon platforms for scalable quantum photonics, but combining spin initialization with electrical tunability is challenging.
method: The authors perform optical charging experiments on an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule and analyze its orbital and spin dynamics.
result: They achieve optical spin charging while preserving electrical tunability and observe ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics.
conclusion: The platform may serve as a building block for multidimensional photonic cluster-state generation and quantum-dot-based spin-photon hardware.

title: Hall's Exact Uncertainty Relation And The Geometry Of Krylov-space Operator Dynamics
authors: Mohsen Alishahiha And Souvik Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Alishahiha and Souvik Banerjee

Krylov representations of operator dynamics encode two inequivalent motions: probability transport along the discrete Krylov chain and motion of the normalized amplitude vector on the associated sphere. We lift Hall's exact uncertainty relation to Liouville space and show that, for the fixed Krylov-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042218] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Hall's exact uncertainty relation to Liouville space to analyze the geometry and probability transport underlying Krylov-space operator dynamics.
motivation: Krylov representations of operator dynamics contain two distinct motions—probability transport along the discrete Krylov chain and motion of the normalized amplitude vector on the associated sphere—and the authors aim to constrain these using an exact uncertainty relation.
method: They lift Hall's exact uncertainty relation to Liouville space and apply it to the structure of Krylov-space operator dynamics, separating chain transport from spherical geometric motion.
result: The lifted uncertainty relation provides bounds connecting the discrete Krylov-chain probability flow with the geometric motion of the amplitude vector on the sphere for fixed Krylov subspaces.
conclusion: This offers a geometric and uncertainty-based framework for understanding operator growth and Krylov complexity, with potential relevance to diagnostics of quantum chaos and operator dynamics.

title: Nonreciprocal Singularities Dominated By The Dissipative Photon-magnon Coupling In pseudo-Hermitian Systems
authors: Yongzhang Shi, Chi Zhang, Zhenhui Hao, Changjun Jiang, C. K. Ong, Ke Xia, And Guozhi Chai
abstract:
Author(s): Yongzhang Shi, Chi Zhang, Zhenhui Hao, Changjun Jiang, C. K. Ong, Ke Xia, and Guozhi Chai

By precisely controlling the loss rate and the coupling strength in an open magnonic cavity, the first experimental demonstration in general pseudo-Hermitian systems of two different singularities with nonreciprocity and selectivity has been achieved. One of the singularities is the exceptional poin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L200406] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates nonreciprocal singularities in an open magnonic cavity governed by dissipative photon-magnon coupling in a pseudo-Hermitian system.
motivation: The authors aim to realize and control distinct nonreciprocal singularities by tuning loss and coupling in a photon-magnon hybrid platform, extending pseudo-Hermitian physics to cavity magnonics.
method: They precisely control the loss rate and coupling strength in an open magnonic cavity and observe two different singularities, including an exceptional point, with nonreciprocity and selectivity.
result: The work reports the first experimental demonstration in general pseudo-Hermitian systems of two singularities with nonreciprocity and selectivity dominated by dissipative photon-magnon coupling.
conclusion: Dissipative photon-magnon coupling enables selective nonreciprocal singularities, offering a platform for pseudo-Hermitian physics and nonreciprocal hybrid magnonic devices.

title: Quantum State Designs From Minimally Random Quantum Circuits
authors: Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, and Bruno Bertini

For quantum circuits that generate complex dynamics, a single, one-site operation is sufficient to produce randomness, showcasing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033047] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that minimally random quantum circuits can generate quantum state designs, revealing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.
motivation: Understanding how much randomness is needed in quantum circuits to produce complex, design-like states is important for random circuit dynamics and quantum information applications.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits with local random operations and determine conditions under which the output approximates a quantum state design.
result: They find that a single one-site random operation can suffice to produce randomness in circuits that generate complex dynamics, quantifying a trade-off between chaos and randomness.
conclusion: Quantum state designs can arise from minimally random circuit dynamics, suggesting efficient routes to random state generation with limited randomness resources.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics Via Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, And Cristiano Ciuti
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, and Cristiano Ciuti

Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031077] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method with automatic differentiation to simulate critical dynamics in large open quantum bosonic lattices.
motivation: Large-scale open quantum bosonic lattices are challenging to simulate, and understanding their critical dynamics requires efficient methods that go beyond exact diagonalization or simple mean-field approaches.
method: They combine a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space representation with automatic differentiation to optimize the dynamics of open bosonic lattice models.
result: The method enables the study of critical dynamics in large open quantum bosonic lattices, capturing effects that are inaccessible to simpler approaches.
conclusion: This variational phase-space framework provides a scalable computational tool for exploring non-equilibrium dynamics of dissipative bosonic many-body systems.

title: Unifying Charge-learnability Transitions In Monitored U(1)-symmetric Quantum Circuits Through Informational Power Of Local Measurement
authors: Yi-Fan Gong And Dan-Bo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Fan Gong and Dan-Bo Zhang
