Charge-learnability transitions in monitored symmetric quantum circuits reveal how local measurement records acquire sufficient information to infer a conserved charge. Here we extend charge learnability to probabilistic weak measurements, for which the measurement probability and measurement streng…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042466] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper unifies charge-learnability transitions in monitored U(1)-symmetric quantum circuits by extending the analysis to probabilistic weak measurements and linking the transitions to the informational power of local measurements.
motivation: It aims to clarify how local measurement records in monitored symmetric circuits acquire enough information to infer a conserved charge, and to unify strong- and weak-measurement regimes.
method: The authors study monitored U(1)-symmetric quantum circuits with probabilistic weak measurements and analyze charge learnability through the informational power of local measurement.
result: They identify charge-learnability transitions for weak measurements and show that a unified description emerges via the informational power of local measurement.
conclusion: The informational power of local measurement provides a unifying framework for charge-learnability transitions in monitored symmetric quantum circuits.

title: Thermodynamic Space Of Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Shiling Liang (梁师翎), Paolo de Los Rios, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Shiling Liang (梁师翎), Paolo De Los Rios, and Daniel Maria Busiello

By deriving bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations, this work defines the thermodynamic space of chemical reaction networks and establishes their fundamental thermodynamic constraints.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041026] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper defines a thermodynamic space for chemical reaction networks by deriving fundamental bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations.
motivation: Chemical reaction networks are central to cellular and artificial chemistry, but their allowed thermodynamic behavior is often characterized only case by case; a general geometric or constraint-based characterization is needed.
method: The authors formulate thermodynamic constraints on reaction networks and derive inequalities bounding affinities and steady-state concentrations, thereby mapping out the feasible thermodynamic space.
result: They establish general bounds that delineate which concentration-affinity configurations are thermodynamically accessible for a given reaction network.
conclusion: These results provide a unified thermodynamic characterization of chemical reaction networks and clarify fundamental limits on their stationary behavior.

title: Energy-Efficient Control Of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
authors: Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, And Clemens Bechinger
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, and Clemens Bechinger

Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031079] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that exploiting hydrodynamic interactions in multiparticle microscopic systems can reduce the energetic cost of transport, even when longer paths are used.
motivation: Controlling interacting microscopic particles efficiently is energetically challenging, and hydrodynamic interactions may provide a route to lower transport costs.
method: The authors analyze energy-efficient control protocols for interacting microscopic systems, focusing on how hydrodynamic interactions and path choice affect the energetic cost of transport.
result: They find that longer paths can save energy when hydrodynamic interactions are harnessed, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions offer a practical mechanism for energy-efficient control of multiparticle microscopic systems, with implications for optimal transport at small scales.

title: Meson Spectroscopy Of Exotic Symmetries Of Ising Criticality In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, and Alexandre Dauphin

A programmable array of atoms reveals how symmetry of the quantum Ising chain transforms when chains are coupled together, providing experimental signatures of a new excitation spectrum.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043018] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: A programmable Rydberg atom array is used to spectroscopically probe how the exotic symmetries of quantum Ising criticality transform when multiple Ising chains are coupled, revealing a meson-like excitation spectrum.
motivation: Ising criticality in one dimension hosts unusual emergent symmetries, but how these symmetries and their associated excitations behave when critical chains are coupled into higher-dimensional or coupled-chain geometries is largely unexplored experimentally.
method: The authors exploit a tunable Rydberg atom array to realize coupled quantum Ising chains and perform spectroscopy of the low-lying excitation spectrum, identifying meson-like bound states and symmetry-related signatures.
result: The measured spectra show clear signatures of exotic symmetry transformations and confined mesonic excitations whose structure depends on the inter-chain coupling, in agreement with theoretical expectations.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays provide a versatile platform for studying exotic symmetry and confinement physics of Ising criticality beyond single-chain settings, opening routes to exploring exotic meson spectroscopy in synthetic quantum matter.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Blockade And Photon-number Filtering In A Rotating Kerr Resonator
authors: Lin-Peng You, Pei Zhou, Xin-Ping Lan, Jie Liu, Ya-Ya Deng, Yi-Bing Qian, Qi-Zhong Hu, Cong-Hua Yan, Bang-Pin Hou, And Lei Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Lin-Peng You, Pei Zhou, Xin-Ping Lan, Jie Liu, Ya-Ya Deng, Yi-Bing Qian, Qi-Zhong Hu, Cong-Hua Yan, Bang-Pin Hou, and Lei Tang

Multiphoton blockade (MPB) provides a versatile mechanism for generating nonclassical light with controllable photon statistics. Here, we propose a rotation-controlled scheme for realizing nonreciprocal MPB and tunable photon-number filtering in a Kerr nonlinear resonator driven by a frequency-match…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043742] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a rotating Kerr nonlinear resonator scheme that achieves nonreciprocal multiphoton blockade and tunable photon-number filtering by exploiting the Sagnac-Fizeau frequency shift induced by rotation.
motivation: Multiphoton blockade is a versatile route to nonclassical light with controllable photon statistics, and adding nonreciprocity (direction-dependent response) would enable chip-scale optical isolators and directional single-/few-photon sources; existing schemes typically lack tunability and directional control.
method: A Kerr nonlinear cavity is driven by frequency-matched fields in a spinning (rotating) resonator, so that clockwise and counterclockwise modes experience opposite frequency shifts; the quantum master equation is solved to compute equal-time photon correlation functions g^(n) for both propagation directions.
result: Rotation strength and drive detuning jointly tune the multiphoton blockade order, yielding strong nonreciprocal two-photon blockade and photon-number filtering where photon bundles of a selected number transmit only in one direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a rotation-controlled knob for direction-selective nonclassical light generation and photon-number filtering, offering a route toward integrable nonreciprocal quantum photonic devices.

title: Self-consistent Thermalization Of Electrons And Phonons In The Hubbard-Holstein Model
authors: Antonio Picano And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Antonio Picano and Marco Schirò

We investigate the dynamics of the Hubbard–Holstein model after a sudden switch-on of the electron–phonon interaction within nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). Using the self-consistent Migdal approximation for the electron–phonon coupling together with self-consistent second-order p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225146] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: Nonequilibrium DMFT study of how electrons and phonons in the Hubbard-Holstein model jointly thermalize after a sudden switch-on of the electron-phonon coupling.
motivation: Understanding whether and how coupled electronic and bosonic degrees of freedom reach a common thermal state is central to the physics of relaxation in strongly correlated materials, but a self-consistent description of both subsystems' thermalization is still lacking.
method: The authors combine nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory with a self-consistent Migdal approximation for the electron-phonon vertex and self-consistent second-order (dynamical mean-field) impurity solvers to evolve the coupled electron-phonon system in time.
result: The electrons and phonons are shown to thermalize self-consistently to a common temperature, with the effective electron-phonon coupling and phonon distribution readjusting during the relaxation; the coupled dynamics differs from perturbative or non-self-consistent treatments.
conclusion: Self-consistency in the electron-phonon self-energy is essential for correctly capturing the long-time thermalization of Hubbard-Holstein systems, providing a benchmark for approximate schemes.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model is used to show that energy diffusion sets the structure of spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Spectral correlations and transport in chaotic many-body systems are usually treated separately; the authors aim to link them quantitatively within a controlled, solvable setting.
method: Analysis of an exactly tractable chaotic many-body model, relating the spectral form factor and its time scales to diffusive energy transport.
result: Energy diffusion is shown to govern the time dependence of spectral correlations, connecting the Thouless-type diffusion time to features of the spectral form factor.
conclusion: Diffusive transport provides organizing principles for spectral statistics in chaotic many-body dynamics, offering a tractable bridge between chaos diagnostics and hydrodynamics.

title: Enhanced Quantum Parameter Estimation Based On The Hardy Paradox
authors: Ming Ji, Yuxiang Yang, And Holger F. Hofmann
abstract:
Author(s): Ming Ji, Yuxiang Yang, and Holger F. Hofmann

Statistical paradoxes such as the Hardy paradox and the enhancement of phase estimation via postselection both draw upon the same nonclassical features of quantum statistics described by nonpositive quasiprobabilities. In this paper, we introduce a postselected quantum metrology scenario where the i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042223] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs a postselected quantum metrology scheme exploiting the Hardy paradox to enhance phase/parameter estimation precision.
motivation: Statistical paradoxes like Hardy's and postselection-enhanced phase estimation both originate from the same nonclassical features captured by nonpositive quasiprobabilities, suggesting a common resource for metrology.
method: A postselected measurement scenario is constructed in which the Hardy-paradox statistics produce amplified sensitivity to an estimated parameter, analyzed via quasiprobability representations.
result: The protocol shows an enhancement of estimation precision relative to standard strategies, tied quantitatively to the negativity of the underlying quasiprobability distribution.
conclusion: Hardy-type paradoxes can serve as a practical resource for enhanced quantum parameter estimation, linking foundational nonlocality to metrological advantage.

title: Geometric Formulation Of State-dependent Langevin Dynamics Using Scalar Free Energy
authors: Kento Yasuda, Zhongqiang Xiong, Zhanglin Hou, Kenta Ishimoto, Xinpeng Xu, And Shigeyuki Komura
abstract:
Author(s): Kento Yasuda, Zhongqiang Xiong, Zhanglin Hou, Kenta Ishimoto, Xinpeng Xu, and Shigeyuki Komura

Stochastic dynamics with state-dependent diffusion arise broadly in confined, anisotropic, and hydrodynamically coupled systems. The conventional Langevin equation contains a spurious drift associated with multiplicative noise. Since the restricted free energy is generally nonscalar, the covariance …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042109] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a geometric formulation of state-dependent Langevin dynamics using a scalar free energy to handle multiplicative noise and spurious drift in confined, anisotropic, or hydrodynamically coupled stochastic systems.
motivation: State-dependent diffusion is common in complex stochastic systems, but conventional Langevin equations suffer from spurious drift terms and nonscalar restricted free energies, motivating a cleaner geometric formulation.
method: The authors reformulate state-dependent Langevin dynamics geometrically by introducing a scalar free energy and addressing the covariance and drift issues associated with multiplicative noise.
result: The formulation removes spurious drift and provides a consistent geometric description of stochastic dynamics with state-dependent diffusion.
conclusion: This work offers a classical stochastic-dynamics framework relevant to nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Emulating Isomerization With Two-dimensional Coulomb Crystals
authors: Naoto Mizukami, Gabriele Gatta, Lucia Duca, And Carlo Sias
abstract:
Author(s): Naoto Mizukami, Gabriele Gatta, Lucia Duca, and Carlo Sias

Isomerization is a fundamental process in chemistry. We use a two-dimensional Coulomb crystal to emulate molecular isomerization and characterize its physical mechanisms. In our molecular analog, the externally controlled confining potential determines the crystal’s potential energy surface (PES), t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043106] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors use a two-dimensional Coulomb crystal of trapped ions as a classical analogue to emulate molecular isomerization and study how the shape of the confining potential determines the potential energy surface and reaction pathways.
motivation: Isomerization is a central chemical process, but molecular potential energy surfaces are difficult to control and probe directly; a tunable, well-characterized analogue system could give cleaner access to the underlying mechanisms.
method: Trapped ions forming a 2D Coulomb crystal are subjected to an externally controlled confining potential that plays the role of the molecular potential energy surface, and the crystal's structural configurations and transitions are characterized experimentally.
result: The crystal exhibits isomer-like configurational states whose stability and interconversion are governed by the engineered confining potential, allowing the isomerization mechanisms to be mapped onto controllable crystal rearrangements.
conclusion: Two-dimensional Coulomb crystals provide a versatile platform for emulating isomerization and other configurational dynamics, though the connection to quantum information tasks is indirect.

title: Freezing And Shielding Under Global Quenches For Long-range Interacting Many-body Systems
authors: Daniel Arrufat-Vicente And Nicolò Defenu
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Arrufat-Vicente and Nicolò Defenu

This article reveals that previous observations, in which the nonequilibrium dynamics of long-range models mirror short-range systems under local quenches, reflect a universal feature of long-range interacting quantum systems. This is demonstrated by showing that this feature is also present under global quenches.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042010] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that freezing and shielding effects in long-range interacting many-body systems under global quenches mirror short-range behavior, indicating a universal feature of long-range quantum dynamics.
motivation: Previous work observed that long-range models can mimic short-range systems under local quenches; the authors ask whether this behavior is universal and persists under global quench protocols.
method: The authors theoretically analyze nonequilibrium dynamics of long-range interacting quantum many-body systems under global quenches and compare the resulting behavior with known short-range and local-quench cases.
result: They find that the freezing and shielding phenomenon also appears under global quenches, establishing it as a universal feature of long-range interacting systems rather than an artifact of local quenches.
conclusion: Long-range interacting many-body systems can exhibit short-range-like nonequilibrium dynamics under both local and global quenches, with implications for universality in long-range quantum dynamics.

title: Max-Cut Graph-driven Quantum Circuit Design For Geometrically Frustrated Planar Spin Systems With Spin-glass-like Energy Landscapes
authors: Seyed Ehsan Ghasempouri, Gerhard W. Dueck, And Stijn de Baerdemacker
abstract:
Author(s): Seyed Ehsan Ghasempouri, Gerhard W. Dueck, and Stijn De Baerdemacker

Finding the ground state of geometrically frustrated spin systems is a challenging problem with broad implications. Many hard optimization problems, including NP-complete problems, can be mapped, for instance, to frustrated Ising models, where competing interactions produce rugged, spin-glass-like e…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043084] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Max-Cut graph-driven approach for designing quantum circuits to address geometrically frustrated planar spin systems with spin-glass-like energy landscapes.
motivation: Finding ground states of frustrated spin systems is computationally hard, and many NP-complete optimization problems map to frustrated Ising models with rugged energy landscapes.
method: The authors use Max-Cut graph structure to guide the construction of quantum circuits aimed at encoding and solving frustrated planar spin-system instances.
result: The work develops a circuit-design methodology tailored to spin-glass-like Ising/Max-Cut problems, though the available abstract excerpt does not provide detailed performance metrics.
conclusion: The approach may offer a systematic way to design quantum circuits for hard frustrated spin-system optimization, but it is specialized and not central to the listed quantum-information research priorities.

title: Heisenberg-Limited Hamiltonian Learning Without Short-Time Control
authors: Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, And Changhun Oh
abstract:
Author(s): Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, and Changhun Oh

A new approach for learning Hamiltonians achieves the Heisenberg limit even when experiments cannot access short evolution times, easing a demanding control requirement.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043011] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a Hamiltonian-learning protocol that reaches the Heisenberg limit without requiring access to short evolution times.
motivation: Hamiltonian learning often relies on short-time evolution to achieve optimal precision, but such control can be experimentally demanding or unavailable.
method: The authors design a learning approach that extracts Hamiltonian parameters at the Heisenberg scaling while avoiding short-time control requirements, likely using engineered interrogation or correlation strategies.
result: The protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited precision under relaxed experimental constraints, easing a key control requirement for Hamiltonian estimation.
conclusion: This work broadens the practicality of optimal Hamiltonian learning by removing the need for short-time evolution control.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of quantum circuits whose correlations are chaotic at short scales but exactly solvable at long scales.
motivation: Understanding chaotic quantum dynamics is challenging because exact analytical results are rare, motivating tractable circuit models that retain chaotic features.
method: The authors construct a new family of quantum circuits designed to have chaotic short-scale correlations while admitting exact asymptotic analysis at long scales.
result: The circuits exhibit correlations that are chaotic at short length/time scales yet become exactly solvable in the long-scale limit.
conclusion: This provides a analytically tractable setting for studying chaotic quantum circuit dynamics and long-time correlation behavior.

title: Hybrid Analog-digital Simulation Of The Abelian Higgs Model With Transmon Qutrits
authors: Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Rayleigh W. Parker, Noah Goss, Ahmed I. Mohamed, Max Neiderbach, Zane Ozzello, Ravi K. Naik, Alexander F. Kemper, Irfan Siddiqi, Yannick Meurice, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Rayleigh W. Parker, Noah Goss, Ahmed I. Mohamed, Max Neiderbach, Zane Ozzello, Ravi K. Naik, Alexander F. Kemper, Irfan Siddiqi, Yannick Meurice, and Machiel S. Blok

To investigate gauge theories with near-term quantum computers warrants exploration of nontraditional quantum simulators to find resource-efficient simulation protocols and ultimately access exotic features of different field theories, including unexplored regimes of the QCD phase diagram. In this w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042462] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a hybrid analog-digital quantum simulation of the Abelian Higgs model using superconducting transmon qutrits.
motivation: Near-term quantum computers may enable exploration of gauge theories and regimes of the QCD phase diagram that are difficult to access classically, motivating resource-efficient quantum simulation protocols.
method: The authors use transmon qutrits in a superconducting circuit platform and combine analog and digital simulation techniques to implement the Abelian Higgs model.
result: They report an experimental implementation of the hybrid protocol on a transmon-qutrit processor, showing a route toward simulating gauge-theory dynamics on near-term hardware.
conclusion: The work illustrates the utility of superconducting qutrits for lattice gauge theory simulation, though it is primarily an application of transmon hardware rather than a direct advance in the researcher's core quantum-information or thermodynamics interests.

title: Regular And Chaotic Dynamics Of Nonlinear Optomechanical Systems Controlled By Modulated Light
authors: A. P. Saiko, G. A. Rusetsky, S. A. Markevich, And R. Fedaruk
abstract:
Author(s): A. P. Saiko, G. A. Rusetsky, S. A. Markevich, and R. Fedaruk

The nonlinear dynamics of a mechanical resonator in an optomechanical system with linear, quadratic, and cubic photon-vibration interactions (with respect to mechanical displacements) in a modulated driving field under conditions of adiabatic elimination of the optical field is studied. Based on the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043738] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes regular and chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear optomechanical resonator driven by modulated light under adiabatic elimination of the optical field.
motivation: Optomechanical systems provide a platform for studying nonlinear and chaotic dynamics arising from photon-vibration interactions, but their behavior under modulated driving and higher-order couplings remains of interest.
method: The authors model a mechanical resonator with linear, quadratic, and cubic photon-vibration interactions in a modulated driving field, adiabatically eliminating the optical field and analyzing the resulting nonlinear dynamics.
result: The study identifies regimes of regular and chaotic motion for the mechanical resonator depending on the interaction orders and driving modulation.
conclusion: The work characterizes how nonlinear photon-vibration couplings and modulated light control the onset of chaos in optomechanical systems, with potential implications for controlling mechanical motion in hybrid platforms.

title: Erratum: Improved Local Models And New Bell Inequalities Via Frank-Wolfe Algorithms [Phys. Rev. Research 5, 043059 (2023)]
authors: Sébastien Designolle, Gabriele Iommazzo, Mathieu Besançon, Sebastian Knebel, Patrick Gelß, And Sebastian Pokutta
abstract:
Author(s): Sébastien Designolle, Gabriele Iommazzo, Mathieu Besançon, Sebastian Knebel, Patrick Gelß, and Sebastian Pokutta

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 049001] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the 2023 paper on using Frank-Wolfe algorithms to construct improved local models and new Bell inequalities.
motivation: The original work addressed the hard problem of characterizing the local polytope for Bell nonlocality, where efficient optimization over local models is computationally challenging as the number of parties and settings grows.
method: The erratum amends results from the original study, which applied Frank-Wolfe convex optimization techniques to approximate local models and derive new Bell inequalities.
result: The correction revises specific statements/figures from the original publication; it does not introduce new scientific methodology or results beyond fixing errors.
conclusion: While the underlying research is relevant to Bell nonlocality and convex-geometry approaches, this erratum itself carries minimal standalone scientific content.

title: Spectral Theory Of Energy-selective Quantum Search With Ising Hamiltonian Phase Oracles
authors: A. S. Plyashechnik, A. A. Zhukov, A. V. Lebedev, And W. V. Pogosov
abstract:
Author(s): A. S. Plyashechnik, A. A. Zhukov, A. V. Lebedev, and W. V. Pogosov

We develop an exact spectral-response theory for the Grover-type iterate [MATH], in which the evolution generated by a diagonal Ising Hamiltonian is used directly as a continuous phase oracle. An energy-grouped recurrence and its generating-function solution show how the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042463] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop an exact spectral-response theory for a Grover-type quantum search iterate in which a diagonal Ising Hamiltonian supplies a continuous phase oracle, using an energy-grouped recurrence and its generating-function solution.
motivation: Continuous-time and Hamiltonian-based phase oracles generalize the standard Grover oracle, but their spectral behavior and search performance are not fully understood analytically, motivating an exact treatment of the resulting iterate.
method: They exploit the diagonal (Ising) structure of the oracle to group basis states by energy, deriving a recurrence for the spectral response and solving it via generating functions to obtain closed-form amplitudes and success probabilities.
result: The analysis yields exact expressions characterizing how the spectrum and energy-grouped populations evolve under the Grover-type iterate, clarifying the conditions under which the Hamiltonian phase oracle achieves amplification.
conclusion: The spectral framework provides an analytical handle on energy-selective quantum search with Ising phase oracles, offering guidance for designing Hamiltonian-based search protocols.

title: Two-photon Doppler-free Spectroscopy Of The $6s{}^{2}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}^{1}S_{0}→6s23s^{1}S_{0}$ Rydberg Transition For Quantum Sensing In Ytterbium
authors: Benjamin D. Hunt, Kyle Beloy, Roger C. Brown, Tobias Bothwell, Harikesh Ranganath, Tanner Grogan, Jacob L. Siegel, And Andrew D. Ludlow
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin D. Hunt, Kyle Beloy, Roger C. Brown, Tobias Bothwell, Harikesh Ranganath, Tanner Grogan, Jacob L. Siegel, and Andrew D. Ludlow

Here we report atomic structure calculations and experimental observations of the two-photon [MATH] transition in Yb. The unique level structure of Yb places the [MATH] state's en…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042818] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports atomic structure calculations and Doppler-free two-photon spectroscopy of a Rydberg transition in ytterbium for quantum sensing applications.
motivation: Ytterbium's level structure may enable useful Rydberg-based quantum sensing, motivating precise spectroscopic characterization of the 6s2 1S0 to 6s23s 1S0 transition.
method: The authors combine atomic structure calculations with two-photon Doppler-free spectroscopy to observe and analyze the transition in Yb.
result: They experimentally observe the two-photon transition and compare it with theoretical atomic structure predictions, characterizing its properties for quantum sensing.
conclusion: The work establishes spectroscopic data for this Yb Rydberg transition, supporting future quantum sensing applications but not directly advancing quantum information processing or networking.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A detailed resource analysis of an end-to-end fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, establishing fundamental bottlenecks and bounded achievable speedups.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid simulations are computationally demanding classically, and it is unclear how much advantage fault-tolerant quantum computers could genuinely deliver for such nonlinear PDEs.
method: Resource estimation and algorithmic analysis of a fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, quantifying gate counts, qubit overhead, and end-to-end runtime against classical methods.
result: The authors identify the dominant resource bottlenecks and derive bounds on the quantum speedup achievable for nonlinear fluid simulation.
conclusion: Quantum advantage for nonlinear fluid dynamics is achievable only within bounded regimes, and the analysis delineates the resource requirements needed for practical fault-tolerant implementations.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm that asymptotically reduces the T-gate count required to synthesize an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are expensive in fault-tolerant quantum computing, so lowering T-count for arbitrary unitary synthesis directly reduces the non-Clifford resource overhead of compiled circuits.
method: The paper presents an improved circuit-synthesis/compilation procedure that constructs Clifford+T decompositions of arbitrary unitaries with asymptotically fewer T gates than prior constructions.
result: An asymptotic improvement in T-count scaling for general unitary synthesis is established, reducing the non-Clifford cost relative to existing compilation algorithms.
conclusion: The work advances fault-tolerant compilation efficiency, though it remains a circuit-synthesis and complexity-oriented contribution rather than an information-theoretic one.

title: Single- And Two-parameter Sensing Near Critical Points In The Anisotropic Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Ming Xue, Lu Zhou, Xu-Xing Geng, Guang-Ming Huang, And Gao-Xiang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ming Xue, Lu Zhou, Xu-xing Geng, Guang-Ming Huang, and Gao-xiang Li

We investigate single- and two-parameter metrological responses near second-order critical boundaries and triple points in the anisotropic quantum Rabi model. In the large-frequency-ratio limit, approaching a second-order critical boundary leads to divergent ground-state squeezing and path-coordinat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043739] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies single- and two-parameter quantum sensing near critical boundaries and triple points in the anisotropic quantum Rabi model.
motivation: Critical points in light-matter models can enhance metrological sensitivity, motivating the study of parameter estimation in the anisotropic quantum Rabi model.
method: The authors analyze ground-state squeezing and path-coordinate responses near second-order critical boundaries and triple points in the large-frequency-ratio limit.
result: They identify divergent or enhanced metrological responses near critical boundaries and triple points for single- and two-parameter sensing schemes.
conclusion: The anisotropic quantum Rabi model may provide a useful platform for critical-point-enhanced quantum metrology, though the work is primarily sensing-focused rather than advancing hybrid-system hardware or information-theoretic foundations.

title: Floquet-Sambe Bottleneck And Frequency-selective Localization In A Driven Synthetic Spin Chain
authors: J. Cao, K. L. Zhang, R. Wang, And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): J. Cao, K. L. Zhang, R. Wang, and X. Z. Zhang

We study a finite Floquet chain in which a uniform nearest-neighbor hopping coexists with a periodically rotating, SU(2)-dictated spin-assisted hopping profile. The resulting coupling is spatially inhomogeneous—weakest at the chain boundaries and strongest in the bulk—and produces a frequency-depend…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204314] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: A finite Floquet spin chain with an SU(2)-dictated, spatially inhomogeneous spin-assisted hopping profile is shown to exhibit a 'Floquet-Sambe bottleneck' and frequency-selective localization of the driven dynamics.
motivation: Driven synthetic lattices offer tunable platforms for controlling transport and localization, and understanding how spatially structured periodic couplings reshape coherent dynamics is of interest for Floquet engineering.
method: The authors analyze a tight-binding chain with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping plus a periodically rotating spin-assisted hopping term whose amplitude is weakest at the boundaries and strongest in the bulk, solving the Floquet problem for a finite chain.
result: The inhomogeneous drive produces a bottleneck effect (Floquet-Sambe) and localization that depends selectively on the driving frequency, with distinct behavior at the chain edges versus the bulk.
conclusion: The work characterizes how SU(2)-structured periodic modulations generate frequency-selective localization in finite driven spin chains, suggesting design principles for Floquet-engineered synthetic lattices.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a photonic neuromorphic architecture based on a quantum memristor for nonlinear, memory-dependent learning tasks such as vowel recognition.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing seeks hardware that can emulate nonlinear, history-dependent processing, and a quantum memristor may provide such functionality in a quantum photonic platform.
method: The authors implement a photonic integrated neuromorphic architecture leveraging a quantum memristor and evaluate it on a vowel-recognition task.
result: The platform exhibits nonlinear memory-dependent processing and supports a proof-of-concept learning application.
conclusion: This work shows an experimental step toward quantum neuromorphic computing, but its contribution is primarily hardware/application-oriented rather than a core information-theoretic advance.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based framework yields commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct Trotter formulas, tightening gate-count estimates for digital quantum simulation of driven and adiabatic dynamics.
motivation: Product-formula (Trotter) decompositions are the workhorse of Hamiltonian simulation, but rigorous error bounds for time-dependent Hamiltonians, including multiproduct extrapolation schemes, have lagged behind those for static cases, leaving gate-count estimates loose.
method: The authors recast the stroboscopic evolution of product formulas as a Floquet problem, deriving error bounds expressed in terms of nested commutators of the Hamiltonian and its time derivatives for both product and multiproduct (Richardson-type) formulas.
result: The derived bounds scale with commutators rather than naive norm products, giving sharper, provably tighter gate-count and step-size estimates for simulating driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The analysis provides practically useful and rigorous resource estimates for time-dependent digital quantum simulation, though it is a circuit-algorithmic error-analysis contribution rather than an information-theoretic one.

title: Theory And Interpretability Of Quantum Extreme Learning Machines: A Pauli Transfer Matrix Approach
authors: Markus Gross And Hans-Martin Rieser
abstract:
Author(s): Markus Gross and Hans-Martin Rieser

Quantum reservoir computers (QRCs) have emerged as a promising approach to quantum machine learning, since they utilize the natural dynamics of quantum systems for data processing and are simple to train. Here we consider [MATH]-qubit quantum extreme learning machines (QELMs) with initial-state encodin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042459] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Pauli transfer matrix framework to analyze the theory and interpretability of quantum extreme learning machines with initial-state encoding.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computers and quantum extreme learning machines are promising for quantum machine learning because they exploit natural quantum dynamics and are easy to train, but their theoretical behavior and interpretability remain underdeveloped.
method: The authors model multi-qubit quantum extreme learning machines using Pauli transfer matrices to characterize the encoding, reservoir dynamics, and readout in a unified linear-algebraic framework.
result: The approach provides interpretable decompositions of the learning protocol and yields theoretical insights into how quantum extreme learning machines process information.
conclusion: The work clarifies the capabilities and limitations of quantum extreme learning machines, but its primary contribution is to quantum machine learning theory rather than to the information-theoretic or thermodynamic topics prioritized by the research interests.

title: Expressivity Of Quantum Graph Neural Networks With Variable-dimension Edge Qudits
authors: Piero Araujo R.
abstract:
Author(s): Piero Araujo R.

This work presents a quantum graph neural network architecture in which each edge of the input graph carries a [MATH]-level quantum system and the model acts on the associated line graph. The set of circuits generated by the model is dense in the unitary group of the total Hilbert space, subject to an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045306] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum graph neural network architecture in which each graph edge carries an M-level qudit and the model acts on the associated line graph, and proves that the resulting circuit set is dense in the unitary group of the total Hilbert space.
motivation: Quantum graph neural networks typically use qubit-based edge features with limited expressivity; the authors aim to characterize how variable-dimensional edge qudits enlarge the set of realizable unitaries.
method: Each edge of the input graph is assigned a qudit of variable local dimension, the model operates on the line graph of the original graph, and the generated circuit family is analyzed for universality via a denseness argument in the unitary group under stated constraints.
result: The circuit family produced by the architecture is shown to be dense in the unitary group of the total Hilbert space (subject to the stated conditions), establishing a strong expressivity guarantee for the ansatz.
conclusion: Variable-dimension edge qudits on the line graph yield a highly expressive, essentially universal quantum graph neural network ansatz, though the work remains a quantum-machine-learning expressivity study rather than an information-theoretic contribution.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a heuristic that speeds up convergence of matrix-product-state classical simulations of two-dimensional out-of-equilibrium quantum spin dynamics, enabling benchmarking of quantum simulators in otherwise inaccessible regimes.
motivation: Verifying large-scale quantum simulation experiments requires classical methods that can reach the same dynamical regimes, but exact tensor-network simulation of 2D quench dynamics is limited by entanglement growth and bond-dimension constraints.
method: A heuristic compression/truncation strategy for MPS simulations of 2D spin systems is proposed and tested on out-of-equilibrium dynamics, improving convergence of the classical simulation with respect to bond dimension.
result: The heuristic accelerates convergence and extends the reachable time scales and system sizes for classical simulation, allowing comparison with quantum hardware results in previously inaccessible regimes.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical classical verification tool for 2D quantum dynamics experiments, though it remains a numerical-simulation methodology rather than a statement about information-theoretic or thermodynamic bounds.

title: Pointwise Mutual Information Bounded By Stochastic Fisher Information
authors: Pedro B. Melo
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro B. Melo

How much information about an unknown parameter can be assigned to one realized outcome, and how is that information constrained by the sensitivity of the same outcome? We derive upper bounds on the pointwise mutual information in terms of the stochastic Fisher information, both for parameters in a …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044141] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives upper bounds on pointwise mutual information in terms of stochastic Fisher information for realized outcomes.
motivation: It asks how much information a single realized outcome carries about an unknown parameter and how this is constrained by the outcome's sensitivity.
method: The author analytically derives inequalities relating pointwise mutual information to stochastic Fisher information for parameterized stochastic models.
result: The main result is a set of upper bounds showing that pointwise mutual information is limited by stochastic Fisher information.
conclusion: The work connects single-outcome information measures with estimation-theoretic sensitivity, with implications for statistical inference in stochastic systems.

title: Microscopic Geometric Theory For Gapped Excitations In Fractional Topological Fluids
authors: Yuzhu Wang And Bo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuzhu Wang and Bo Yang

We propose a geometric description of all gapped excitations in fractional quantum Hall phases that reveals several fundamental understandings with experimental consequences. These include a duality between the Hilbert space of multiple gapped “gravitonlike” spin 2 excitations at [MATH] Laughlin ph…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186502] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a geometric framework describing all gapped excitations in fractional quantum Hall fluids, including a Hilbert-space duality among multiple 'graviton-like' spin-2 excitations at Laughlin filling.
motivation: Gapped neutral excitations of fractional topological fluids (such as the spin-2 graviton mode) lack a unified microscopic description, limiting both fundamental understanding and experimental interpretation of transport and spectroscopy data.
method: A geometric/analytic construction is developed that organizes the Hilbert space of gapped excitations of fractional quantum Hall phases, exploiting algebraic and geometric structures of the topological fluid to relate different excitation sectors.
result: The theory uncovers a duality between Hilbert spaces of multiple gapped spin-2 excitations at Laughlin fractions and yields concrete experimental consequences that could be tested in measurement.
conclusion: The geometric picture provides a systematic microscopic account of gapped excitations in fractional topological fluids, opening routes to experimentally probing the internal structure of these topological phases.

title: Toward Complete Characterization Of Topological Insulators And Superconductors: A Systematic Construction Of Topological Invariants Based On Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
authors: Seishiro Ono And Ken Shiozaki
abstract:
Author(s): Seishiro Ono and Ken Shiozaki

A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041024] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper systematically constructs topological invariants using the momentum-space Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence to classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.
motivation: A complete and systematic characterization of topological insulators and superconductors is needed to classify stable topological phases beyond case-by-case approaches.
method: The authors use the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space to construct topological invariants for stable superconducting phases organized by space-group symmetry.
result: They provide a systematic classification of stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups via the resulting topological invariants.
conclusion: The framework moves toward complete characterization of topological insulators and superconductors using spectral-sequence-based invariants.

title: Postselected Amplification And Photon Recycling Applied To Optical Sensing Of Magnetic Fields
authors: Yazhi Niu, Jialin Li, Lupei Qin, And Xin-Qi Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yazhi Niu, Jialin Li, Lupei Qin, and Xin-Qi Li

We apply the combined technique of postselected amplification and photon recycling to an optical setup of magnetic-field precision measurement. We propose two recycling schemes and obtain analytic expressions for the amplified signal and measurement sensitivity. The results show significant improvem…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042449] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines postselected (weak-value) amplification with photon-recycling schemes to improve the sensitivity of an optical magnetic-field sensor.
motivation: Precision magnetometry with optical readout is limited by detector noise and photon-budget constraints; postselection and recycling are proposed as ways to boost the signal-to-noise ratio without added resources.
method: Two photon-recycling architectures are integrated with a postselected weak-measurement amplification stage, and analytic expressions are derived for the amplified signal and the resulting measurement sensitivity.
result: The analytic and numerical analysis indicates significant improvement in magnetic-field sensitivity relative to the scheme without recycling, with the gain characterized in terms of system parameters.
conclusion: Postselected amplification plus photon recycling offers a practical route to enhanced optical magnetometry, though the work remains a metrology/sensing proposal rather than a test of quantum-information or thermodynamic principles.

title: Squeezing Enhancement Through Resonant Interference In Multiring Resonators
authors: M. Sloan And J. E. Sipe
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sloan and J. E. Sipe

We develop a nonperturbative description of squeezed light generation in an arbitrary lossy structure consisting of multiple coupled microring resonators. This is applied to two-ring photonic molecules where the interference of the fields in the coupled rings leads to a modification in the resonance…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043735] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative theory of squeezed-light generation in lossy multi-ring microring-resonator structures, showing that interference in coupled two-ring 'photonic molecules' modifies the squeezing resonances.
motivation: Squeezed light is a key quantum-optical resource, and integrated microring platforms offer a compact route to generate it; however, existing descriptions rarely handle losses and multi-ring coupling nonperturbatively.
method: The authors develop a general nonperturbative scattering/input-output-type treatment of squeezing in arbitrary lossy structures of coupled microring resonators and apply it to two-ring photonic molecules.
result: Interference between fields in the coupled rings shifts and modifies the resonance structure, yielding enhanced squeezing at particular resonances relative to single-ring devices.
conclusion: Resonant interference in coupled microrings provides a design lever for improving squeezed-light generation in integrated lossy photonic structures.

title: Nonlinear Brownian Motions In Gases: Kinetic Equations And Relaxation Processes
authors: Leonardo Ferrari
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Ferrari

The behavior of particles subject to a nonlinear drag force in a medium (nonlinear Brownian motion) is usually treated by means of the Fokker-Planck equation proposed by Klimontovich [
tldr: The paper revisits kinetic equations for particles undergoing nonlinear Brownian motion in gases and analyzes associated relaxation processes.
motivation: The commonly used Klimontovich Fokker-Planck description of nonlinear Brownian motion is argued to have a questionable derivation, motivating a more careful kinetic treatment.
method: The author derives kinetic equations for particles subject to a nonlinear drag force in a gaseous medium and studies the resulting relaxation dynamics.
result: The paper provides a corrected kinetic-equation framework for nonlinear Brownian motion and characterizes relaxation processes within that framework.
conclusion: The work clarifies the kinetic theory of nonlinear Brownian motion in gases, but it is classical stochastic/statistical mechanics and lacks direct connection to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Finite-size Corrections To The Crosscap Overlap In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: Yiteng Zhang, Li-Ping Yang, Hong-Hao Tu, And Yueshui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiteng Zhang, Li-Ping Yang, Hong-Hao Tu, and Yueshui Zhang

We analyze the finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap in the two-dimensional classical Ising model along its self-dual critical line. Using a fermionic formulation, we express the lattice crosscap overlap in terms of Bogoliubov angles and develop a contour-integral approach by analytically …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042110] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap (a boundary-state overlap) in the 2D critical Ising model using a fermionic lattice formulation and contour-integral techniques.
motivation: Crosscap overlaps characterize boundary conditions on non-orientable surfaces and encode universal CFT data; lattice computations of their finite-size scaling test CFT predictions and provide a benchmark for crosscap states, which have been discussed in entanglement and topological contexts.
method: The lattice crosscap overlap is expressed in terms of Bogoliubov angles from the fermionic (free-Majorana) description of the Ising model, and a contour-integral approach is developed to evaluate the resulting products analytically, yielding the finite-size expansion.
result: Analytic results for the finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap along the self-dual critical line are obtained, exhibiting the expected universal CFT scaling with power-law and possibly logarithmic corrections.
conclusion: The work confirms CFT predictions for crosscap overlaps with high precision at the lattice level and provides a controllable analytic handle on boundary-state overlaps in the critical Ising model.

title: Link Length And Energy Fluctuations In Extensible Freely Jointed Chains
authors: Michael R. Buche
abstract:
Author(s): Michael R. Buche

The freely jointed chain is often applied to model the thermodynamics of single polymer chains, but the traditional formulation of the model lacks internal energy changes due to bond stretching. For this reason, the extensible freely jointed chain model includes a potential energy function, typicall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045414] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes link-length and energy fluctuations in an extensible freely jointed chain model that includes bond-stretching potential energy.
motivation: The traditional freely jointed chain model omits internal energy changes due to bond stretching, limiting its thermodynamic realism for single polymer chains.
method: The author develops a theoretical statistical-mechanical treatment of the extensible freely jointed chain and derives fluctuation properties for link lengths and energy.
result: The analysis characterizes how bond extensibility modifies thermodynamic fluctuations in the chain model, providing corrected fluctuation relations relative to the standard freely jointed chain.
conclusion: Extensible-chain thermodynamics is relevant to polymer elasticity and classical statistical mechanics, but it has no direct connection to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Shaping The Spectra Of A Second-harmonic Laser By Spatial Focusing
authors: Yan-Ming Liu, Tao Xie, Xiangying Hao, And Rui-Bo Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Ming Liu, Tao Xie, Xiangying Hao, and Rui-Bo Jin

Accurately controlling the spectral width of second-harmonic generation (SHG) is critical in applications such as nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, where tailored spectral properties are required. Although it is known that the focal length of the lens used to focus th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043538] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows how the focal length of a focusing lens can be used to shape and control the spectral bandwidth of a second-harmonic generation (SHG) laser source.
motivation: Tailored spectral widths of SHG light are needed for nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, but the role of focusing geometry in setting the spectrum was not well characterized.
method: Experiments (and accompanying modeling) vary the focusing condition of the fundamental beam into the nonlinear crystal and measure the resulting second-harmonic spectrum, relating spectral width to focal length and interaction geometry.
result: The second-harmonic spectral width is systematically modified by the spatial focusing parameter, providing a tunable knob for spectral shaping of the SHG output.
conclusion: Spatial focusing offers a simple, practical route to engineering the spectral properties of second-harmonic laser sources for downstream spectroscopy and quantum-optics applications.

title: Flat Band In The Multiband Metal ${\mathrm{MnSb}}_{2}$
authors: Carl Jonas Linnemann, Davide Ceresoli, Kim-Khuong Huynh, And Martin Bremholm
abstract:
Author(s): Carl Jonas Linnemann, Davide Ceresoli, Kim-Khuong Huynh, and Martin Bremholm

We report the realization of a metallic flat band in the marcasite compound [MATH]. The material was synthesized under high pressure, and its crystal structure was established by x-ray diffraction. Electrical and thermoelectric transport measurements reveal signatures of a flat band n…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231115] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors report the realization of a metallic flat band in the high-pressure-synthesized marcasite compound MnSb2, characterized structurally and via electrical and thermoelectric transport.
motivation: Flat electronic bands are of broad interest because they can host strongly correlated phenomena and enhanced thermoelectric response, motivating the search for metallic flat-band materials.
method: MnSb2 was synthesized under high pressure, its crystal structure determined by x-ray diffraction, and its electrical and thermoelectric transport properties measured to probe flat-band signatures.
result: Transport measurements reveal signatures consistent with a flat band in this multiband metal, indicating the presence of a low-dispersion band near the Fermi level.
conclusion: MnSb2 is established as a metallic flat-band material, offering a platform for exploring flat-band-driven transport and correlation physics.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
authors: Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041017] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals, providing a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifying mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate material realizations.
motivation: Axion insulators are a notable class of topological magnetic materials, but their classification had been restricted to symmorphic lattices, leaving nonsymmorphic crystal structures and their associated symmetry constraints unexplored.
method: The authors develop a symmetry-based classification framework for time-reversal-doubled axion insulators in nonsymmorphic space groups, deriving spin-resolved topological invariants and then screening candidate compounds via first-principles electronic structure calculations.
result: A spin-resolved classification scheme for nonsymmorphic axion insulators is established, and mixed bismuth monohalides are identified as candidate materials predicted to host the corresponding axion-insulator phase.
conclusion: The work broadens the scope of axion insulator physics beyond symmorphic crystals and provides concrete material candidates, offering guidance for future experimental and theoretical studies of topological magnetism.

title: Space-efficient Quantum Solvers For Boolean Satisfiability Problems Via Structural Reduction
authors: Quanfeng Lu, Shijie Wei, Jinfeng Zeng, Wentao Yang, Muxi Zheng, Peijie Chang, Dong Ruan, Zeguo Wang, And Guilu Long
abstract:
Author(s): Quanfeng Lu, Shijie Wei, Jinfeng Zeng, Wentao Yang, Muxi Zheng, Peijie Chang, Dong Ruan, Zeguo Wang, and Guilu Long

The Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problem is a central benchmark for quantum optimization, but conventional encodings typically require one qubit per active variable, limiting their use on near-term quantum hardware. Here we introduce a space-efficient framework for one-in-three SAT based on the deci…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042460] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a space-efficient encoding for one-in-three SAT on quantum hardware, using structural reductions (decision diagrams) to reduce the number of qubits needed per variable.
motivation: Conventional SAT encodings require one qubit per active variable, which is prohibitive on near-term quantum devices with limited qubit counts and connectivity.
method: They introduce a framework based on decision-diagram-style structural reduction of the SAT instance, then map the reduced structure to a quantum solver circuit whose width scales with the reduced representation rather than the raw variable count.
result: The reduction yields substantial qubit savings relative to standard one-qubit-per-variable encodings, with numerical or small-scale demonstrations on one-in-three SAT instances.
conclusion: Structural reduction is a practical route to fitting SAT benchmarks on constrained quantum hardware, though the approach remains an algorithmic/compilation contribution rather than an information-theoretic one.

title: Inversion Symmetry Breaking Induced Strong Electron-phonon Scattering And The Suppression Of Thermal Conductivity In ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{CS}}_{2}$
authors: Hong-Ze Luo, Lin Wan, Yu-Jia Zeng, And Wu-Xing Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Hong-Ze Luo, Lin Wan, Yu-Jia Zeng, and Wu-Xing Zhou

The interplay between crystal symmetry and electron-phonon coupling is crucial for understanding thermal transport in two-dimensional materials. Using first-principles calculations combined with Wannier interpolation and coupled electron-phonon Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate how inversio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245423] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study showing that inversion symmetry breaking in Ta2CS2 strengthens electron-phonon scattering and thereby suppresses lattice thermal conductivity.
motivation: Crystal symmetry and electron-phonon coupling jointly govern heat transport in two-dimensional materials, but their quantitative interplay is poorly understood, motivating a systematic study of how inversion symmetry breaking modifies thermal transport.
method: Density functional theory plus Wannier interpolation combined with coupled electron-phonon Boltzmann transport theory to compute electron-phonon scattering rates and thermal conductivity for Ta2CS2.
result: Breaking inversion symmetry enhances electron-phonon coupling strength, substantially increasing scattering rates and reducing thermal conductivity relative to the symmetric structure.
conclusion: Symmetry-controlled electron-phonon coupling provides a design handle for tuning thermal transport in 2D materials, relevant for thermoelectric applications.

title: Searching For Ultralight Dark Matter With MOLeQuTE: A Massive Optically Levitated Quantum Tabletop Experiment
authors: Louis Hamaide, Hannah Banks, Peter Barker, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Louis Hamaide, Hannah Banks, Peter Barker, and Andrew A. Geraci

Many well theoretically motivated models of ultralight dark matter are expected to give rise to feeble oscillatory forces on macroscopic objects. Optically trapped sensors have high force sensitivities but have remained relatively unexplored in this context. In this work, we propose a tunable, optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043086] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes MOLeQuTE, a tunable optically levitated sensor array concept for detecting feeble oscillatory forces from ultralight dark matter.
motivation: Many well-motivated ultralight dark matter models predict tiny oscillatory forces on macroscopic bodies, and optically trapped mechanical sensors offer exceptionally high force sensitivity that has been largely unexploited for this purpose.
method: The authors design a tabletop experiment using optically levitated nanoparticles/microspheres with tunable trapping frequencies to resonantly enhance and scan for oscillatory forces in the ultralight dark matter mass range.
result: The proposed configuration is projected to reach force sensitivities and mass reach competitive with or beyond existing ultralight dark matter searches over a tunable frequency band.
conclusion: Levitated optomechanics provides a viable, scalable platform for ultralight dark matter detection, motivating future experimental implementation.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a 'topological flowscape' framework to characterize nonreciprocal dynamics and state transitions in living (active) matter far from equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and understanding nonreciprocity and self-organization in such systems requires new geometric/topological tools beyond standard near-equilibrium descriptions.
method: The authors construct a topological flowscape analysis of experimentally measured or modeled nonreciprocal flows in living matter, using it to identify and classify transitions between dynamical states.
result: The flowscape reveals distinct state transitions governed by nonreciprocal interactions, providing a topological signature of self-organization in active living systems.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity in living matter can be captured through topological features of the flow field, offering a general route to characterizing nonequilibrium biological organization.

title: Bridging Marcus–Landauer Transport Regimes In Orbital-Gated Molecular Junctions
authors: Minwoo Song, Jongwoo Nam, Hyemin Lee, Changjun Lee, Donguk Kim, Ryong-Gyu Lee, Minsu Jeong, Yong-Hoon Kim, Keehoon Kang, And Takhee Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Minwoo Song, Jongwoo Nam, Hyemin Lee, Changjun Lee, Donguk Kim, Ryong-Gyu Lee, Minsu Jeong, Yong-Hoon Kim, Keehoon Kang, and Takhee Lee

Charge transport in molecular junctions is commonly described by either Marcus theory, which captures thermally activated hopping via redox processes, or Landauer formalism, which models elastic tunneling between two electrodes. However, real molecular junctions often operate in an intermediate regi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186301] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified framework bridging Marcus thermally-activated hopping and Landauer elastic tunneling to describe charge transport in orbital-gated molecular junctions operating in the intermediate regime.
motivation: Real molecular junctions often fall between the two standard transport pictures — Marcus redox hopping and coherent Landauer tunneling — so a single model capturing the crossover is needed to interpret experiments.
method: The authors combine theoretical modeling of orbital gating with transport measurements on molecular junctions, constructing a hybrid description that interpolates between Marcus and Landauer regimes and validating it against gate-dependent conductance data.
result: The proposed bridging model reproduces the measured transport characteristics across the intermediate regime, showing how orbital gating tunes the system between hopping-dominated and tunneling-dominated conduction.
conclusion: A unified Marcus–Landauer picture provides a more complete account of molecular junction transport and offers a design principle via orbital gating for controlling conduction mechanisms.

title: Hanbury Brown–Twiss Effect And Classical Entanglement With Light Carrying Orbital Angular Momentum
authors: Jyrki Laatikainen, Sushil Pokharel, And Olga Korotkova
abstract:
Author(s): Jyrki Laatikainen, Sushil Pokharel, and Olga Korotkova

Intensity-intensity correlation of a scalar optical beam carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) across multiple modes is decomposed into intermodal contributions, thereby linking it, within the framework of the Hanbury Brown–Twiss effect, to the underlying modal coherence structure. Upon filtering …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043529] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper decomposes the intensity-intensity correlation of a scalar optical beam carrying orbital angular momentum into intermodal contributions, linking the Hanbury Brown–Twiss effect to the beam's modal coherence structure.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify how classical coherence among OAM modes manifests in intensity correlation measurements, and to relate this to the notion of 'classical entanglement' between spatial modes of light.
method: Using scalar coherence theory, they expand the HBT correlation function over OAM modes and analyze the resulting intermodal terms, including the effects of modal filtering.
result: The correlation signal is shown to be expressible as a sum of intermodal coherence contributions, whose structure depends on the OAM spectrum and filtering conditions.
conclusion: Intensity correlations of OAM light provide a diagnostic of modal coherence and of classical (intermodal) entanglement, offering a classical-optics analogue of quantum correlation measures.

title: Experimental Subdiffraction Source Discrimination Enabled By Spatial Demultiplexing And Single-Photon Detectors
authors: Luigi Santamaria Amato, Danilo Triggiani, And Cosmo Lupo
abstract:
Author(s): Luigi Santamaria Amato, Danilo Triggiani, and Cosmo Lupo

We experimentally demonstrate a universal, parameter-independent test for asymmetric source discrimination below the diffraction limit. The test exploits spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) and single-photon detection to discriminate the presence of a faint source in the vicinity of a brighter one. …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 183801] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a parameter-independent subdiffraction source-discrimination test using spatial-mode demultiplexing and single-photon detection.
motivation: Discriminating a faint source near a brighter one below the diffraction limit is challenging for conventional imaging and is relevant to quantum-inspired superresolution and source detection.
method: The authors use spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) together with single-photon detectors to implement a universal test for asymmetric source discrimination.
result: They experimentally show that the SPADE-based single-photon detection scheme can discriminate a faint source in the vicinity of a brighter source below the diffraction limit.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental proof-of-principle for practical subdiffraction source discrimination, but it is not directly aligned with the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems research directions.

title: Altermagnetic Band Geometry And The Antiferromagnetic Thermal Boundary In A Coupled fermion-Ising Model
authors: Xing-Can Liu, Ho-Kin Tang, Tao Ying, And Xueru Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xing-Can Liu, Ho-Kin Tang, Tao Ying, and Xueru Zhang

We study a minimal square-lattice model to examine the relation between momentum-space altermagnetic band geometry and real-space Ising criticality in a coupled fermion-Ising setting. In this model, itinerant fermions with explicitly spin-dependent nearest-neighbor hopping are locally coupled to tra…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235135] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: A minimal square-lattice coupled fermion-Ising model is used to relate momentum-space altermagnetic band geometry to real-space Ising criticality and an antiferromagnetic thermal boundary.
motivation: Altermagnets combine spin-split band structure with compensated magnetic order, motivating a minimal lattice model that captures how band-geometric features tie to thermal magnetic transitions.
method: Itinerant fermions with spin-dependent nearest-neighbor hopping are locally coupled to transverse-field Ising spins on a square lattice, analyzed via the resulting band geometry and critical/thermal behavior.
result: The authors identify connections between altermagnetic band-geometric quantities and the location/character of the Ising critical regime, delineating a thermal boundary associated with antiferromagnetic ordering.
conclusion: The work provides a minimal platform linking band geometry to magnetic criticality, relevant to condensed-matter studies of altermagnets rather than to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Unveiling The Bose-Einstein Condensate-droplet Crossover With Rayleigh Superradiant Scattering
authors: Mithilesh K. Parit, Mingchen Huang, Ziting Chen, Yifei He, Haoting Zhen, And Gyu-Boong Jo
abstract:
Author(s): Mithilesh K. Parit, Mingchen Huang, Ziting Chen, Yifei He, Haoting Zhen, and Gyu-Boong Jo

Rayleigh superradiant scattering is used to probe a dipolar
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042012] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: Rayleigh superradiant scattering is used as a probe to resolve the crossover between a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate and a self-bound macrodroplet.
motivation: Dipolar quantum gases interpolate between a conventional BEC and a liquid-like macrodroplet, and new non-destructive or light-based diagnostics are needed to characterize which regime the gas occupies and how it responds to magnetic-field orientation.
method: A dipolar gas is illuminated with a Rayleigh superradiant scattering setup, and the scattering efficiency together with light-induced atom depletion and the resulting expansion dynamics are measured across the BEC-to-droplet crossover and as a function of field orientation.
result: The scattering efficiency peaks near the crossover, the rapid light-induced depletion reveals distinct expansion dynamics characteristic of each regime, and a field-orientation-dependent shift of the crossover is observed.
conclusion: Rayleigh superradiant scattering provides a sensitive, regime-resolving probe of the BEC-droplet crossover in dipolar gases, with potential use for characterizing dipolar quantum matter.

title: Quantum Advantage For Sensing Properties Of Classical Fields
authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, And Ishaan Kannan
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, and Ishaan Kannan

Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041025] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol using entanglement and squeezing to learn classical field properties with subvacuum precision.
motivation: Quantum metrology can surpass classical sensing limits, but demonstrating advantage for diverse classical signal properties remains of interest.
method: The authors use entangled and squeezed quantum probes in a sensing protocol to estimate properties of classical fields.
result: The protocol achieves subvacuum precision for multiple classical signal properties, indicating a quantum advantage in sensing.
conclusion: Entanglement and squeezing can enhance sensing of classical fields beyond vacuum-level precision, though the work is specialized to quantum metrology rather than the researcher's core directions.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A classical frustrated pyrochlore spin model is shown to stabilize an unusual magnetic nematic phase, with mixed magnetic orders emerging from competing interactions and thermal fluctuations.
motivation: Conventional magnetic order is often suppressed on frustrated lattices, and understanding what exotic phases (such as nematic or mixed orders) replace it is a central problem in frustrated magnetism.
method: The authors analyze a frustrated spin model on the pyrochlore lattice, using symmetry arguments and likely classical Monte Carlo / mean-field techniques to map the phase diagram as a function of model parameters and temperature.
result: Thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries are found to suppress conventional order, stabilizing a magnetic nematic phase and regimes of mixed magnetic order.
conclusion: The work clarifies how competing orders and lattice frustration can be harnessed to realize nematic and mixed magnetic phases, providing guidance for identifying such states in pyrochlore materials.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi
abstract:
Author(s): Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, and Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical framework for evaluating quantum-enhanced interferometry using general Markovian light sources.
motivation: It aims to clarify when realistic quantum light sources can provide an advantage in interferometric measurements.
method: The authors develop a framework to design and assess quantum light sources within Markovian models for interferometry.
result: The framework identifies conditions under which realistic devices may yield a quantum advantage in interferometry.
