conclusion: The work provides guidance for evaluating quantum light sources in interferometric applications, though it lies outside the primary research directions.

title: Invariant Energy Subspaces In Quantum-optical High-harmonic Generation: An Information-theoretic Approach
authors: Philipp Stammer
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Stammer

Energy conservation is ubiquitous in the understanding of the process of high-harmonic generation. Yet a complete quantum-optical description of the photon-number-resolved structure implied by exact energy conservation remained elusive. Here, we solve this problem by introducing an information-theor…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043736] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces invariant energy subspaces and an information-theoretic framework to describe photon-number-resolved quantum-optical high-harmonic generation under exact energy conservation.
motivation: A complete quantum-optical description of the photon-number-resolved structure implied by exact energy conservation in high-harmonic generation had remained elusive.
method: It constructs an information-theoretic approach based on invariant energy subspaces to partition and analyze the quantum-optical photon-number structure of high-harmonic generation.
result: The framework resolves the photon-number-resolved structure associated with exact energy conservation in quantum-optical high-harmonic generation.
conclusion: The work provides a new information-theoretic perspective on high-harmonic generation, but it is not directly aligned with the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems research directions.

title: Optical Vortex Generation By Magnons With Spin-orbit-coupled Light
authors: Ryusuke Hisatomi, Alto Osada, Kotaro Taga, Haruka Komiyama, Takuya Takahashi, Shutaro Karube, Yoichi Shiota, And Teruo Ono
abstract:
Author(s): Ryusuke Hisatomi, Alto Osada, Kotaro Taga, Haruka Komiyama, Takuya Takahashi, Shutaro Karube, Yoichi Shiota, and Teruo Ono

Light possesses both spin and orbital angular momentum. In spatially inhomogeneous optical fields, which are characterized by a finite distribution of wave vectors in [MATH] space, these properties undergo spontaneous coupling, referred to as optical spin-orbit coupling. The study of the coupling has r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043062] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that magnons in a magnetic film can imprint orbital angular momentum onto light via spin-orbit coupling of light, generating optical vortices.
motivation: Optical spin-orbit coupling in spatially inhomogeneous fields is well studied, but whether collective spin excitations (magnons) can mediate transfer of angular momentum between spin and orbital degrees of freedom of light was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the coupling between magnon modes and structured optical fields with a broad wave-vector distribution, and derive/measure the resulting conversion of spin angular momentum into orbital angular momentum of the transmitted light.
result: Magnon excitation is found to generate optical vortices, i.e., light carrying well-defined orbital angular momentum, controlled by the magnon mode and the inhomogeneous wave-vector distribution.
conclusion: Magnon-mediated spin-orbit coupling of light provides a route to compact, tunable sources of structured light, with potential use in magnon-photon hybrid platforms.

title: Experimental Observation Of Erratic Non-Hermitian Skin Effect In Phononic Crystals
authors: Yujian Yuan, Jie Liu, He Gao, Jiamin Guo, Zhongming Gu, And Jie Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yujian Yuan, Jie Liu, He Gao, Jiamin Guo, Zhongming Gu, and Jie Zhu

The erratic non-Hermitian skin effect (ENHSE), emerging from the interplay between disorder and locally nonreciprocal yet globally reciprocal couplings, has reshaped the conventional bulk-boundary correspondence through its disorder-dependent localization properties. Here, we experimentally observe …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186602] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: An experimental demonstration of the erratic non-Hermitian skin effect in classical phononic crystals, showing disorder-dependent localization that breaks conventional bulk-boundary correspondence.
motivation: The non-Hermitian skin effect challenges standard bulk-boundary correspondence, and the recently proposed 'erratic' variant arising from the interplay of disorder with locally nonreciprocal but globally reciprocal couplings has so far lacked experimental verification.
method: Acoustic/phononic crystal lattices are engineered with locally nonreciprocal yet globally reciprocal couplings and controlled disorder, and the resulting mode localization is mapped experimentally via spatially resolved acoustic measurements.
result: The experiment observes disorder-dependent, erratic localization of eigenmodes consistent with predictions for the ENHSE, confirming the breakdown of conventional bulk-boundary correspondence in this regime.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental observation of the erratic non-Hermitian skin effect, establishing phononic crystals as a platform for studying disorder-driven non-Hermitian topological phenomena.

title: Directional Quantum Walks Of Two Bosons On The Hatano-Nelson Lattice
authors: Sk Anisur, Kartik Singh, And Sayan Choudhury
abstract:
Author(s): Sk Anisur, Kartik Singh, and Sayan Choudhury

We theoretically investigate the interplay of interactions and non-Hermiticity in the dynamics of two bosons on the one-dimensional Hatano-Nelson lattice with nonreciprocal tunneling. We find that the nonreciprocity in the tunneling leads to the formation of an asymmetric density cone during the tim…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043313] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: This work theoretically studies two interacting bosons undergoing directional quantum walks on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson lattice with nonreciprocal tunneling.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how interactions and non-Hermitian nonreciprocity jointly affect quantum walk dynamics, particularly the emergence of asymmetric density propagation.
method: They analyze the time evolution of two bosons on a Hatano-Nelson lattice, incorporating on-site interactions and asymmetric tunneling, likely via exact diagonalization or numerical propagation.
result: The nonreciprocal tunneling produces an asymmetric density cone, and interactions modify the walk dynamics in ways tied to the non-Hermitian skin effect and bosonic bunching.
conclusion: The study clarifies interaction-induced effects in non-Hermitian quantum walks and suggests Hatano-Nelson lattices as platforms for directional boson transport.

title: $p$-wave Magnet Driven Field-free Josephson Diode Effect
authors: Lovy Sharma, Bimal Ghimire, And Manisha Thakurathi
abstract:
Author(s): Lovy Sharma, Bimal Ghimire, and Manisha Thakurathi

Recently, the superconducting diode effect, characterized by unequal critical currents in opposite directions, has been observed experimentally and predicted theoretically in models of bulk superconductors and Josephson junctions. In this work, we construct a Josephson junction using a recently disc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204510] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Josephson junction built on a p-wave magnet that exhibits a field-free superconducting diode effect, i.e. unequal critical currents in opposite directions without an applied magnetic field.
motivation: The superconducting diode effect has so far required an external magnetic field or complex heterostructures; finding intrinsic, field-free mechanisms is desirable for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors construct a theoretical Josephson junction model incorporating a recently described p-wave magnet as the barrier/weak link and compute the current-phase relation and critical currents in both directions.
result: They find a nonzero diode efficiency in zero applied field, arising from the momentum-dependent spin polarization of the p-wave magnet that breaks the required symmetries.
conclusion: p-wave magnets offer a viable route to intrinsic, field-free Josephson diodes, with potential use in superconducting logic and memory.

title: Electric Field Controlled Nonlinear Anomalous Nernst Effect In Two-dimensional Time-reversal Symmetric Systems
authors: Ying-Li Wu And Xiao-Qin Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying-Li Wu and Xiao-Qin Yu

Here, the authors demonstrate that an applied direct electric field lifts the symmetry constraint on the nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect, enabling this effect in time-reversal symmetric 2D systems with crystallographic symmetries beyond a single mirror symmetry. They propose an alternating temperature gradient, rather than a steady one, as a driving force, allowing experimental detection via second-harmonic measurements. This finding broadens the material platform for quantum-geometry-induced transverse thermoelectric effects and provides an alternative route for thermoelectric energy harvesting.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245425] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A direct electric field lifts the symmetry constraint on the nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect, enabling it in time-reversal symmetric 2D crystals with more general crystallographic symmetries and detectable via second-harmonic thermoelectric measurements.
motivation: The nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect (NANEs) is a quantum-geometry-driven transverse thermoelectric response, but its observation has been restricted to time-reversal broken or single-mirror-symmetry systems, limiting the material platforms available.
method: The authors analyze symmetry constraints on the nonlinear anomalous Nernst coefficient in 2D time-reversal symmetric systems, show that an applied DC electric field breaks the relevant constraint, and propose an alternating temperature gradient with second-harmonic lock-in detection for measurement.
result: Applying a DC electric field allows a nonzero NANEs in time-reversal symmetric 2D systems with crystallographic symmetries beyond a single mirror, and the alternating-temperature-gradient scheme yields a measurable second-harmonic signal.
conclusion: The work broadens the class of materials exhibiting quantum-geometry-induced transverse thermoelectric effects and offers an alternative route toward thermoelectric energy harvesting.

title: U(2) Chern-Simons-Ginzburg-Landau Theory Of Fractional Quantum Hall Hierarchies
authors: Taegon Lee, Gil Young Cho, And Donghae Seo
abstract:
Author(s): Taegon Lee, Gil Young Cho, and Donghae Seo

We construct effective [MATH] Chern-Simons-Ginzburg-Landau theories for Abelian and non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall hierarchies that had previously been described only through categorical data or trial wave functions. Our framework captures both Abelian hierarchy states built on half-fi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231116] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors construct effective U(2) Chern-Simons-Ginzburg-Landau field theories describing Abelian and non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall hierarchy states that were previously characterized only by categorical data or trial wave functions.
motivation: Fractional quantum Hall hierarchies, especially non-Abelian ones, have lacked a unified effective-field-theory description, being accessible only through abstract categorical data or microscopic trial wave functions.
method: They build U(2) Chern-Simons-Ginzburg-Landau effective theories that capture both Abelian hierarchy states built on half-filled composite-fermion levels and non-Abelian hierarchy states.
result: The framework reproduces the known hierarchy structure and provides an explicit field-theoretic representation of states previously described only by categorical or wave-function data.
conclusion: The U(2) CSGL approach offers a systematic effective description of FQH hierarchies, bridging categorical/trial-wave-function constructions and Landau-Ginzburg-type field theory.

title: Tackling The Sign Problem In The Doped Hubbard Model With Normalizing Flows
authors: Dominic Schuh, Lena Funcke, Janik Kreit, Thomas Luu, And Simran Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Dominic Schuh, Lena Funcke, Janik Kreit, Thomas Luu, and Simran Singh

The Hubbard model at finite chemical potential is a cornerstone for understanding doped correlated systems, but simulations are severely limited by the sign problem. In the auxiliary-field formulation, the spin basis mitigates the sign problem, yet severe ergodicity issues have limited its use. We e…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231117] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Normalizing flows are used to mitigate the sign problem and ergodicity issues in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the doped Hubbard model.
motivation: Finite-chemical-potential Hubbard model simulations are severely limited by the fermionic sign problem, and although the spin basis reduces signs, it introduces severe ergodicity problems that restrict practical use.
method: The authors employ normalizing-flow-based machine-learning approaches to improve sampling and overcome ergodicity limitations in the auxiliary-field formulation of the Hubbard model.
result: The proposed approach enables simulations at finite doping that were previously inaccessible, alleviating both sign and ergodicity problems in the spin-basis auxiliary-field formulation.
conclusion: Normalizing flows provide a viable route to studying doped correlated electron systems with quantum Monte Carlo, extending the reach of sign-problem-limited simulations.

title: Exploring Entropic Orders: High-temperature Continuous Symmetry Breaking And Topological Order
authors: Po-Shen Hsin And Ryohei Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Po-Shen Hsin and Ryohei Kobayashi

High temperature is usually expected to destroy order: as the Gibbs state approaches the infinite-temperature limit, it becomes an equal-weight ensemble over all states and the system is generically disordered. Recent works showed that entropic order can violate this expectation through coupling to …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214112] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores entropic orders that can survive at high temperature, including continuous symmetry breaking and topological order.
motivation: High temperature is normally expected to destroy order, but recent work suggests entropic effects can stabilize ordered phases even near the infinite-temperature limit.
method: The authors use theoretical statistical-mechanical/field-theoretic analysis of Gibbs states and coupling mechanisms to identify conditions under which entropic order persists.
result: They find mechanisms by which high-temperature continuous symmetry breaking and topological order can emerge through entropic ordering.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of finite-temperature order beyond conventional expectations, but it lies primarily in condensed-matter/statistical physics rather than the targeted quantum-information or information-thermodynamics directions.

title: Nondiffusive Phonon Transport In Complex Diamond Microstructures And Nanostructures
authors: Kai Zhang, Wanying Liu, Yunting Zhu, Weiyi Lin, And Yangyu Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Zhang, Wanying Liu, Yunting Zhu, Weiyi Lin, and Yangyu Guo

The ultrahigh thermal conductivity of diamond, relevant to the momentum-conserving phonon normal process, holds exceptional promise for advanced micro/nanoscale thermal management. However, efficient modeling of collective phonon transport in complex three-dimensional diamond structures remains chal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225424] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops efficient modeling of collective (nondiffusive, momentum-conserving) phonon transport in complex three-dimensional diamond micro- and nanostructures to predict ultrahigh thermal conductivity for micro/nanoscale thermal management.
motivation: Diamond's extremely high thermal conductivity, tied to momentum-conserving normal phonon processes, is attractive for advanced thermal management, but modeling collective phonon transport in complex 3D geometries is computationally challenging.
method: The authors build a simulation framework for phonon transport in complex diamond structures, capturing nondiffusive/collective effects beyond simple Fourier or diffusive Boltzmann treatments, and apply it to realistic 3D micro/nanostructures.
result: The model reproduces and predicts enhanced, geometry-dependent thermal transport in complex diamond architectures where collective phonon effects dominate over purely diffusive behavior.
conclusion: Efficient modeling of collective phonon transport enables rational design of diamond-based micro/nanoscale thermal management structures.

title: Defect-nucleated Charge Density Wave In Monolayer $1H\text{−}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: Fangjun Cheng, Xinyu Liu, Matthew Toole, James Mckenzie, Nileema Sharma, Kota Yoshimura, Yi-Ting Hsu, Badih Assaf, And Xiaolong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Fangjun Cheng, Xinyu Liu, Matthew Toole, James McKenzie, Nileema Sharma, Kota Yoshimura, Yi-Ting Hsu, Badih Assaf, and Xiaolong Liu

Reduced dimensionality is generally expected to enhance charge density wave (CDW) order. However, experimental results in monolayer [MATH] appear conflicting: while optical measurements reveal CDW signatures up to 145 K on oxide substrates, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) studies …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245424] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that substrate-oxide defects nucleate charge density wave order in monolayer 1H-NbSe2, reconciling conflicting reports of CDW transition temperatures across substrates.
motivation: Reduced dimensionality should enhance charge density wave order, yet optical measurements on oxide substrates report CDW signatures up to 145 K while STM studies find much weaker or absent order; the origin of this discrepancy is unclear.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to image monolayer 1H-NbSe2 on different substrates, correlating CDW domain formation with the presence of substrate-induced disorder and individual defects.
result: CDW order in the monolayer is found to be nucleated by defects rather than being a homogeneous bulk-like transition, explaining the substrate-dependent and spatially inhomogeneous CDW signatures observed in prior optical versus STM experiments.
conclusion: Disorder and substrate-induced defects play a decisive role in stabilizing charge density wave order in monolayer NbSe2, so apparent conflicts between optical and local probes are reconciled by inhomogeneous, defect-nucleated CDW domains.

title: Coexistence Of Magnon-induced Optical Vortex And Gaussian Beam Scattering Assisted By Rotational Umklapp Process
authors: Ryusuke Hisatomi, Kotaro Taga, Hisakazu Matsuki, Shutaro Karube, Yoichi Shiota, And Teruo Ono
abstract:
Author(s): Ryusuke Hisatomi, Kotaro Taga, Hisakazu Matsuki, Shutaro Karube, Yoichi Shiota, and Teruo Ono

The exploitation of crystal-lattice symmetries to engineer angular momentum transfer between structured light and magnons marks a novel frontier for optomagnonic research. In Brillouin light scattering, when focused light propagates parallel to an external magnetic field and interacts with ferromagn…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194428] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: Brillouin light scattering of focused light parallel to a magnetic field in a ferromagnet can simultaneously produce a magnon-induced optical vortex and a scattered Gaussian beam via a rotational Umklapp process.
motivation: Optomagnonics aims to exploit crystal-lattice symmetries to control angular momentum exchange between structured light and magnons, a largely unexplored route for manipulating optical orbital angular momentum.
method: Angle- and polarization-resolved Brillouin light-scattering experiments on a magnetized ferromagnet, analyzed in terms of rotational Umklapp processes that relax the angular-momentum matching conditions.
result: Two coexisting scattering channels are observed: one generating an optical vortex carrying orbital angular momentum from magnon absorption/emission, and one yielding a Gaussian beam, both enabled by the Umklapp-assisted angular momentum transfer.
conclusion: The rotational Umklapp mechanism provides a symmetry-based handle for engineering vortex beams with magnons, opening directions for optomagnonic angular-momentum control.

title: Scattering Zones In Quantum Speckle Propagation
authors: Shaurya Aarav, S. A. Wadood, And Jason W. Fleischer
abstract:
Author(s): Shaurya Aarav, S. A. Wadood, and Jason W. Fleischer

Quantum speckles exhibit significantly richer behavior than their classical counterparts due to their higher dimensionality. A simple example is the far-field speckle pattern in one-dimensional (1D) light scattering: Classical light forms 1D speckles defined by the numerical aperture, whereas biphot…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043113] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how quantum speckle patterns in one-dimensional light scattering differ from classical speckles, revealing additional structure and scattering zones due to biphoton correlations.
motivation: Quantum speckles are expected to show richer behavior than classical speckles because of higher dimensionality and quantum correlations, motivating a systematic comparison in a simple 1D scattering geometry.
method: The authors analyze far-field speckle patterns formed by classical light versus biphoton quantum light in 1D scattering, characterizing the resulting spatial structure and identifying distinct scattering zones.
result: Quantum speckles exhibit behavior beyond the numerical-aperture-defined classical speckle size, with biphoton correlations producing additional far-field features and zones not present classically.
conclusion: The work clarifies how quantum correlations shape speckle propagation and may inform quantum optical scattering and imaging, but it does not directly address the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems priorities.

title: Large Time-step Discretization Of Adiabatic Quantum Dynamics
authors: Dong An, Pedro C. S. Costa, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Dong An, Pedro C. S. Costa, and Dominic W. Berry

Adiabatic quantum computing is a general framework for preparing eigenstates of Hamiltonians on quantum devices. However, its digital implementation requires an efficient Hamiltonian simulation subroutine, which may introduce extra computational overhead or complicated quantum control logic. In this…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043098] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a large time-step discretization method for efficiently simulating adiabatic quantum dynamics in digital quantum implementations.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum computing requires Hamiltonian simulation for digital implementation, but standard methods can introduce substantial computational overhead and complicated control logic.
method: The authors propose and analyze a discretization scheme that allows larger time steps when simulating adiabatic quantum dynamics, reducing simulation cost while maintaining accuracy.
result: The method is shown to improve the efficiency of digital adiabatic quantum dynamics simulation by relaxing time-step constraints.
conclusion: Large time-step discretization offers a practical route to more efficient digital simulation of adiabatic quantum protocols.

title: Floquet Generation Of Hybrid-order Topology And ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$-like Bipolar Localization
authors: Koustav Roy, Latu Kalita, B. Tanatar, And Saurabh Basu
abstract:
Author(s): Koustav Roy, Latu Kalita, B. Tanatar, and Saurabh Basu

Periodic driving offers a powerful tool to engineer topological phases and even induce phase transitions that are inaccessible in static settings. In this work, we demonstrate that a suitable driving protocol applied to the Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes model, a canonical quadrupolar insulator with a $…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043094] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-driving protocol applied to the Benalcazar-Berdevig-Hughes quadrupolar insulator generates hybrid-order (mixed first- and second-order) topology along with Z2-like bipolar localization of corner/edge modes.
motivation: Periodic driving can access topological phases and transitions that have no static counterpart, so the authors ask whether driving a canonical quadrupolar higher-order insulator can produce new hybrid-order topological phases and qualitatively new localization patterns.
method: The authors drive the BBH model with a suitable time-periodic protocol, obtain an effective Floquet Hamiltonian, and analyze its quasienergy spectrum, bulk topological invariants, and boundary (corner/edge) mode structure to identify the hybrid-order phase and the associated bipolar localization.
result: The driven BBH model realizes a hybrid-order topological phase in which both first-order edge and second-order corner modes coexist, accompanied by a Z2-like bipolar localization pattern that is absent in the static model.
conclusion: Floquet engineering of the BBH model offers a route to hybrid-order topology and to controlling localization of topological states, extending higher-order band topology beyond static quadrupolar insulators.

title: Penning Trap Single-photon Counter For Axion Detection
authors: Jack A. Devlin, Marko L. Wojtkowiak, Shreyak R. Banhatti, He Zhang, Jiacheng Shi, Toren S. Dofher, Jonathan M. H. Gosling, Michael R. Tarbutt, And Richard C. Thompson
abstract:
Author(s): Jack A. Devlin, Marko L. Wojtkowiak, Shreyak R. Banhatti, He Zhang, Jiacheng Shi, Toren S. Dofher, Jonathan M. H. Gosling, Michael R. Tarbutt, and Richard C. Thompson

Discovering the microscopic composition of dark matter is one of the most important open problems in physics today. Axions are a leading candidate to be dark matter; however, a search of the full range of all likely axion masses is hampered by the standard quantum noise limit. This makes haloscope s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043082] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Penning-trap-based single-photon counter to circumvent the standard quantum noise limit in axion haloscope searches for dark matter.
motivation: Axions are a leading dark matter candidate, but conventional haloscope searches over the full plausible mass range are slowed by the standard quantum limit of noise in linear microwave amplifiers.
method: The authors develop a single-photon counting scheme based on a trapped electron/particle in a Penning trap coupled to a microwave cavity, characterized theoretically and with proof-of-principle measurements of its noise and detection performance.
result: The device demonstrates photon-counting sensitivity that can evade the added noise of phase-insensitive amplification, potentially accelerating axion scans by removing the standard quantum limit bottleneck.
conclusion: Penning-trap single-photon counters offer a viable quantum-noise-limited-free detection route for next-generation axion haloscopes, though the work is aimed at dark-matter detection rather than quantum information processing.

title: Probing The Ground State Of The Antiferromagnetic Heisenberg Model On The Kagome Lattice Using Geometrically Informed Variational Quantum Eigensolver
authors: Abdellah Tounsi, Nacer Eddine Belaloui, Abdelmouheymen Rabah Khamadja, Takei Eddine Fadi Lalaoui, Mohamed Messaoud Louamri, David E. Bernal Neira, And Mohamed Taha Rouabah
abstract:
Author(s): Abdellah Tounsi, Nacer Eddine Belaloui, Abdelmouheymen Rabah Khamadja, Takei Eddine Fadi Lalaoui, Mohamed Messaoud Louamri, David E. Bernal Neira, and Mohamed Taha Rouabah

This work investigates the nature of the ground state of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on fundamental kagome cells, a triangle and a star, using the variational quantum eigensolver algorithm on real quantum hardware. We demonstrate that the ground-state preparation is achievable using a sha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043080] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a geometrically informed variational quantum eigensolver on real quantum hardware to probe the ground state of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on small kagome cells.
motivation: Understanding the ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets such as the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet is a challenging problem where quantum algorithms may offer useful tools.
method: The authors implement a variational quantum eigensolver with geometry-informed ansatz choices on actual quantum hardware for triangle and star kagome cells.
result: They demonstrate ground-state preparation for these fundamental kagome units and analyze the resulting states on noisy hardware.
conclusion: The work shows that geometrically informed VQE can probe small frustrated spin systems on current quantum devices, though it does not address the researcher's core quantum-information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-platform interests.

title: Emergent Gauge Flux In Mixed ${\mathrm{QED}}_{3}$ With Flavor Chemical Potential: Implications For Magnetized U(1) Dirac Spin Liquids
authors: Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, and Zi Yang Meng

Quantum Monte Carlo simulations reveal that a Zeeman field drives Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase, forming relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge field theory.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041029] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations show that a Zeeman field drives a mixed U(1) Dirac spin liquid into a chiral flux phase with relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless emergent photon excitations.
motivation: Magnetized U(1) Dirac spin liquids are candidate exotic phases of frustrated quantum magnets, but how a magnetic field reshapes their emergent gauge structure and spinon spectrum is not well understood.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a mixed QED3 theory with flavor chemical potential, complemented by an effective field-theoretic description of the emergent gauge field and spinon Landau levels.
result: The Zeeman field induces an emergent gauge flux (chiral flux phase) that quantizes relativistic spinon Landau levels while leaving the emergent photon gapless, producing a distinct magnetized Dirac spin liquid phenomenology.
conclusion: The work identifies a field-driven chiral flux phase as the magnetized fate of U(1) Dirac spin liquids, offering signatures for numerical and candidate-material studies of quantum spin liquids.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes quantum gas microscope protocols for extracting many-body observables such as d-wave superconducting order parameters and Green's functions.
motivation: Quantum gas microscopes offer powerful access to correlated many-body systems, but measuring key observables like superconducting order parameters and Green's functions remains challenging.
method: The authors develop measurement protocols based on coherences and state-of-the-art quantum gas microscopy techniques to reconstruct relevant many-body quantities.
result: The protocols enable extraction of d-wave superconducting order parameters, coherences, and Green's functions in cold-atom quantum simulators.
conclusion: These techniques expand the capabilities of quantum gas microscopes for probing complex many-body phases, though they fall outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems priorities.

title: Atomic-Scale Visualization Of Quantum Phase Transition In Mixed-Valence Regime
authors: Xingsen Chen, Junyi Zhang, Qiaoyan Yu, Ruijun Xi, Shasha Xue, Jice Sun, Yi Zhang, Xian Du, Xuhui Ning, Pengyu Hu, Tingwen Miao, Hao Yang, Hemian Yi, Weijiong Chen, Xiaoxue Liu, Liang Liu, Dandan Guan, Yaoyi Li, Shiyong Wang, Canhua Liu, Sangen Zhao, Hao Zheng, And Jinfeng Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Xingsen Chen, Junyi Zhang, Qiaoyan Yu, Ruijun Xi, Shasha Xue, Jice Sun, Yi Zhang, Xian Du, Xuhui Ning, Pengyu Hu, Tingwen Miao, Hao Yang, Hemian Yi, Weijiong Chen, Xiaoxue Liu, Liang Liu, Dandan Guan, Yaoyi Li, Shiyong Wang, Canhua Liu, Sangen Zhao, Hao Zheng, and Jinfeng Jia

Fe dopants on the surface of a [MATH] thin film grown on a superconducting [MATH] substrate by molecular beam epitaxy are investigated by a dilution-refrigerator scanning tunneling microscope. Utilizing the tip-induced band bending effect, we precisely ma…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186201] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Scanning tunneling microscopy visualizes an atomic-scale quantum phase transition in the mixed-valence regime of Fe dopants on a thin-film surface.
motivation: The paper aims to understand local electronic and structural changes associated with a quantum phase transition in a mixed-valence condensed-matter system.
method: Fe dopants on a molecular-beam-epitaxy-grown thin film on a superconducting substrate were studied using a dilution-refrigerator scanning tunneling microscope, with tip-induced band bending used to tune the local regime.
result: The authors report atomic-scale visualization of the quantum phase transition and characterize the mixed-valence behavior of individual Fe dopants.
conclusion: The work provides microscopic insight into a condensed-matter quantum phase transition but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Soliton Thouless Pumping Engineered By Intersite Nonlinearities
authors: Tao Jiang And Li-Chen Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Jiang and Li-Chen Zhao

We study soliton Thouless pumping in an extended diagonal Aubry-André-Harper model with on-site nonlinearities and intersite nonlinearities. We show that the intersite nonlinearities can make solitons acquire anomalous transport distances far beyond the ones predicted by the linear bands, and the qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043535] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies soliton Thouless pumping in a nonlinear Aubry-André-Harper model and shows that intersite nonlinearities can produce anomalous transport distances beyond linear-band predictions.
motivation: Thouless pumping is usually understood through linear topological band theory, but nonlinear and solitonic effects can strongly modify transport; the authors aim to characterize how on-site and intersite nonlinearities alter pumping.
method: They analyze an extended diagonal Aubry-André-Harper model with both on-site and intersite nonlinearities, focusing on soliton dynamics under a Thouless pump protocol.
result: Intersite nonlinearities are shown to enable soliton transport over anomalous distances that exceed those predicted by linear bands.
conclusion: Nonlinear intersite effects provide an additional control mechanism for Thouless pumping of solitons, going beyond conventional linear topological transport.

title: Light-induced Line Narrowing Of The Magnetic Resonance In A Parametric Resonance Optically Pumped Rubidium Magnetometer
authors: Yongbiao Yang, Yang Li, Zhengyu Su, Jun He, Xiaojun Jia, Yanhua Wang, And Junmin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yongbiao Yang, Yang Li, Zhengyu Su, Jun He, Xiaojun Jia, Yanhua Wang, and Junmin Wang

Optically pumped atomic magnetometers are fundamentally limited by spin-exchange relaxation in finite magnetic fields. In conventional parametric resonance magnetometers (PRMs), this relaxation dominates the resonance linewidth, producing broad profiles that degrade sensitivity. Here, we suppress th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042623] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates light-induced line narrowing in a parametric-resonance optically pumped rubidium magnetometer by suppressing spin-exchange relaxation, improving magnetic-field sensitivity.
motivation: Optically pumped atomic magnetometers are limited by spin-exchange relaxation in finite magnetic fields, which broadens resonance lines and degrades sensitivity in conventional parametric resonance magnetometers.
method: The authors use optical pumping and parametric resonance in rubidium vapor, applying light-induced effects to narrow the magnetic resonance linewidth and reduce the influence of spin-exchange relaxation.
result: The technique produces narrower resonance profiles than conventional parametric resonance magnetometers, enhancing the magnetometer's sensitivity.
conclusion: Light-induced line narrowing offers a practical route to improved optically pumped atomic magnetometry, but the work is focused on quantum sensing/metrology rather than the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Trainable, Self-verifying Variational Quantum Eigensolver Using Adiabatic Warm Starts
authors: Bojan Žunkovič, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, And Michael Lubasch
abstract:
Author(s): Bojan Žunkovič, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, and Michael Lubasch

A study looks at the conditions under which an adiabatic variational quantum eigensolver succeeds, where approximate ground states generated along an adiabatic path serve as initial states for successive optimization steps. A self-verification procedure based on energy-standard-deviation measurements is introduced that assesses eigenstate accuracy during run-time and verifies convergence to the target ground state.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042013] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a trainable adiabatic variational quantum eigensolver with run-time self-verification via energy-standard-deviation measurements.
motivation: Variational quantum eigensolvers can suffer from optimization and convergence issues, motivating adiabatic warm starts and reliable accuracy certification.
method: Approximate ground states along an adiabatic path initialize successive VQE optimization steps, and energy-standard-deviation measurements are used for self-verification.
result: The authors identify conditions under which the adiabatic VQE succeeds and show that the self-verification procedure assesses eigenstate accuracy and convergence during the run.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical VQE strategy for ground-state preparation with built-in convergence verification, but it is primarily a quantum-algorithm development outside the specified research directions.

title: Odd-Even Parity Of Nonlinear Hall Effects In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Zitian Pan, Jiaheng Li, Jin Cao, Xuejin Zhang, Jundong Zhu, Yu Hong, Zhiheng Huang, Jingwei Dong, Dongxia Shi, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wei Yang, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Hongming Weng, Luojun Du, And Guangyu Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zitian Pan, Jiaheng Li, Jin Cao, Xuejin Zhang, Jundong Zhu, Yu Hong, Zhiheng Huang, Jingwei Dong, Dongxia Shi, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wei Yang, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Hongming Weng, Luojun Du, and Guangyu Zhang

Experiments reveal a potentially useful odd–even dichotomy in the nonlinear Hall response of bilayer graphene.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186302] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Experiments reveal an odd–even layer-parity dichotomy in the nonlinear Hall response of bilayer graphene.
motivation: The nonlinear Hall effect, governed by the Berry curvature dipole, is a sensitive probe of band-geometry and symmetry breaking, but its layer-parity dependence in few-layer graphene had not been clearly established.
method: Transport measurements of the nonlinear Hall response in bilayer graphene devices (including dual-gated/hBN-encapsulated samples), analyzing the dependence on layer number and stacking/symmetry configuration.
result: The nonlinear Hall signal exhibits an odd–even dichotomy between different layer-parity configurations, indicating a symmetry-controlled Berry curvature dipole response.
conclusion: The odd–even parity rule provides a design principle for controlling nonlinear Hall responses in van der Waals materials and potential applications in symmetry-based devices.

title: Quantum Monte Carlo Studies Of U(1) Lattice Gauge Models Of Kondo Breakdown
authors: Gaopei Pan And Fakher F. Assaad
abstract:
Author(s): Gaopei Pan and Fakher F. Assaad

In the local-moment regime, heavy fermions are most economically described by a compact U(1) gauge theory. Motivated by this perspective, we study a minimal compact U(1) lattice gauge model describing a spin chain coupled to two-dimensional Dirac conduction electrons. The spin chain is described by …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186503] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a compact U(1) lattice gauge model describing a spin chain coupled to 2D Dirac conduction electrons, aimed at understanding Kondo breakdown in heavy-fermion systems.
motivation: In the local-moment regime heavy fermions are economically described by a compact U(1) gauge theory, motivating a minimal lattice gauge model of Kondo breakdown.
method: Sign-problem-free (or controlled) quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a compact U(1) lattice gauge theory with a spin chain coupled to two-dimensional Dirac fermions.
result: The simulations characterize the phase structure and critical behavior of the coupled spin-chain/Dirac-fermion gauge model, addressing how Kondo screening breaks down.
conclusion: The work provides numerical evidence for the gauge-theoretic description of Kondo breakdown in heavy-fermion lattice models.

title: Chiral Casimir-Polder Force From Chiral Anomaly In Weyl Semimetals
authors: Liang Chen, Xu-Feng Zhao, Xun-Lei Ding, And Kai Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Chen, Xu-Feng Zhao, Xun-Lei Ding, and Kai Chang

We propose a novel chiral-discriminatory Casimir-Polder interaction between chiral molecules and Weyl semimetals, originating from the chiral anomaly. This interaction is uniquely governed by the molecule’s electric dipole moment, enabling chiral discrimination even when the optical rotatory strengt…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186904] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors predict a chirality-discriminating Casimir-Polder interaction between chiral molecules and Weyl semimetals that arises from the chiral anomaly and is governed by the molecule's electric dipole moment.
motivation: Chiral discrimination of molecules typically relies on optical rotatory strength, which is weak; the authors seek a Casimir-Polder-based mechanism that can distinguish enantiomers even when conventional chiroptical signals vanish.
method: They compute the Casimir-Polder interaction between a chiral molecule and a Weyl semimetal using the chiral anomaly contribution to the semimetal's electromagnetic response, deriving an interaction term that depends on the molecular electric dipole moment and the separation geometry.
result: The resulting force is chiral-discriminatory, changing sign or magnitude between enantiomers, and remains operative in regimes where the optical rotatory strength is negligible.
conclusion: Chiral-anomaly-induced Casimir-Polder forces in Weyl semimetals offer a new route to enantioselective sensing and manipulation of chiral molecules.

title: Available Energy And Ground States Of Convective Hydrodynamic And Hydromagnetic Instabilities
authors: Kaixuan Fan And Yao Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Kaixuan Fan and Yao Zhou

We propose a method for predicting the nonlinear extent of convective instabilities in neutral and magnetized fluids. The method extends Gardner’s restacking algorithm, which computes the available energy and ground states of collisionless plasmas in phase space, and combines it with Lagrangian rela…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 185101] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The authors extend Gardner's restacking algorithm with Lagrangian relaxation to compute available energy and construct ground states, thereby predicting the nonlinear saturation extent of convective instabilities in neutral and magnetized fluids.
motivation: Linear theory predicts whether a convective instability grows but not how far it grows; a principled nonlinear saturation criterion is needed for both hydrodynamic and hydromagnetic flows.
method: Gardner's phase-space restacking algorithm, originally developed for collisionless plasmas, is generalized and combined with Lagrangian relaxation to compute the available energy and the relaxed ground state of the fluid system.
result: The method yields ground states and available energies for convective hydrodynamic and hydromagnetic instabilities, giving an estimate of the nonlinear extent reached by the instability.
conclusion: Available-energy/ground-state techniques from plasma physics transfer usefully to convective fluid instabilities, providing a practical nonlinear amplitude prediction without full simulation.

title: Real-Space Imaging Of Thomson Charge Configurations In Superfluid Helium Nanodroplets
authors: Thomas Pohl, Jan Mayerhofer, Hanqing Liu, Arin Mizouri, Hao Sha, Masoomeh Mahmoodi Darian, Fabio Zappa, Andrew M. Ellis, David J. Wales, Shengfu Yang, And Paul Scheier
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Pohl, Jan Mayerhofer, Hanqing Liu, Arin Mizouri, Hao Sha, Masoomeh Mahmoodi Darian, Fabio Zappa, Andrew M. Ellis, David J. Wales, Shengfu Yang, and Paul Scheier

Predicting the lowest-energy arrangement of like charges on a sphere defines the Thomson problem, a long-standing challenge with analytical solutions only for a few small systems. We report a real-space experimental realization using superfluid helium nanodroplets, where surface-localized charges ar…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 183001] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes the Thomson problem—finding lowest-energy arrangements of like charges on a sphere—by imaging surface-localized charges on superfluid helium nanodroplets in real space.
motivation: The Thomson problem has analytical solutions only for a few small systems, so an experimental platform that directly visualizes charge configurations on a sphere would enable systematic study of these geometries.
method: Charges are localized on the surface of superfluid helium nanodroplets and their spatial configurations are imaged in real space, with comparison to theoretical/global-optimization predictions of minimal-energy arrangements.
result: Well-defined, shell-like charge configurations consistent with Thomson-type minimal-energy structures are observed and resolved spatially.
conclusion: Superfluid helium nanodroplets provide a tunable experimental testbed for the Thomson problem, bridging charge localization physics with structural optimization.

title: Generation Of Optical Pulling Force In Liquid-core Fibers: Dual Perspectives Of Scattering And Gradient Effects
authors: Qirong Huang, Jia Ai, Youjun Luo, Zhen Zhao, Yongchun Zhong, Haihua Fan, Haiying Liu, Zhongchao Wei, And Qiaofeng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Qirong Huang, Jia Ai, Youjun Luo, Zhen Zhao, Yongchun Zhong, Haihua Fan, Haiying Liu, Zhongchao Wei, and Qiaofeng Dai

Most reported optical pulling mechanisms rely on scattering effects, with well-established design principles: enhancing the forward momentum of light scattered by the manipulated object. In contrast, gradient-induced optical pulling remains in the early stage of exploration, largely due to the absen…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043528] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how optical pulling forces can be generated inside liquid-core fibers, treating scattering and gradient contributions on equal footing.
motivation: Most optical pulling schemes rely on scattering-based momentum transfer, while gradient-induced pulling is far less explored owing to the absence of clear design principles; the authors aim to supply such principles in a fiber geometry.
method: Electromagnetic modeling of light propagation and force densities in a liquid-core fiber, decomposing the net force on a manipulated object into scattering and gradient components and comparing their relative magnitudes and tunability.
result: The authors identify parameter regimes in which gradient effects can dominate and produce pulling (negative) forces, providing design rules that complement scattering-based pulling mechanisms.
conclusion: Dual scattering-plus-gradient design perspectives broaden the toolkit for optical pulling in fiber platforms, with potential use in fiber-integrated optical manipulation and particle transport.

title: Dynamic Magnetization Switching By Time-reversal-odd Nonlinear Spin Polarization
authors: Guang Tian, Hengjie Shi, Haoyu Wang, Haiyun Chen, Yanning Yue, Kaiqi Zhang, And Xiaosong Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang Tian, Hengjie Shi, Haoyu Wang, Haiyun Chen, Yanning Yue, Kaiqi Zhang, and Xiaosong Wu

Field-free deterministic switching of magnetization by electric current is at the heart of spin-orbit-torque devices. It is widely believed that structural inversion symmetry breaking is an indispensable prerequisite for such switching. Here we propose that by exploiting the nonlinear response regim…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194431] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes that field-free deterministic magnetization switching in spin-orbit-torque devices can be achieved without structural inversion symmetry breaking by exploiting time-reversal-odd nonlinear spin polarization in the nonlinear response regime.
motivation: Deterministic current-induced magnetization switching conventionally requires broken structural inversion symmetry; the authors challenge this assumption to enable field-free switching in centrosymmetric magnetic heterostructures.
method: Theoretical/analytical treatment of the nonlinear current response, deriving a time-reversal-odd spin polarization that exerts an effective torque on the magnetization, likely supplemented by model calculations of switching dynamics.
result: A nonlinear spin polarization with the required symmetry properties is shown to generate an effective field capable of deterministic, field-free switching of the magnetization.
conclusion: Nonlinear-response spin polarization provides an alternative, symmetry-based route to field-free spin-orbit-torque switching, relaxing the requirement of structural inversion asymmetry.

title: Topological Zero-reflection Points In Multiterminal Quantum Wire Junctions
authors: Abhiram Soori, Udit Khanna, And Diptiman Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Abhiram Soori, Udit Khanna, and Diptiman Sen

We study scattering in noninteracting multiterminal quantum wire junctions and show that junctions with dihedral symmetry can exhibit exact zero-reflection points for [MATH] terminals. By analyzing the scattering matrix, we identify these reflectionless points in the [MATH] parameter space, wh…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225423] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes scattering matrices of multiterminal noninteracting quantum wire junctions with dihedral symmetry and identifies exact zero-reflection (reflectionless) points in parameter space.
motivation: Reflectionless transport is desirable for designing low-dissipation mesoscopic devices, and symmetry is known to constrain scattering matrices; the authors aim to classify when such exact zero-reflection points must exist in multiterminal geometries.
method: Scattering-matrix analysis of noninteracting quantum wire junctions, using dihedral (point-group) symmetry constraints on the S-matrix to locate reflectionless points in the junction parameter space.
result: Junctions with dihedral symmetry are shown to host exact zero-reflection points for certain numbers of terminals, with these points identified explicitly in the parameter space of the scattering matrix.
conclusion: Symmetry-protected reflectionless transport provides a generic design principle for multiterminal quantum wire junctions, potentially useful for mesoscopic device engineering.

title: Three-dimensional Flat Band In The Topological Electride Of $t$-KAl
authors: Dexi Shao, Yiwei Liang, Yican Mao, Qinyi Chen, Juefei Wu, Huiyang Gou, And Zhaopeng Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Dexi Shao, Yiwei Liang, Yican Mao, Qinyi Chen, Juefei Wu, Huiyang Gou, and Zhaopeng Guo

By means of first-principles calculations and crystal structure predictions, we identify a series of potassium-aluminum (K-Al) compounds under high pressure, which are absent in ambient conditions. Among them, the P4/nmm KAl phase, stable under pressure from 15 to 70 GPa, exhibits a range of intrigu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245136] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: First-principles and crystal-structure-prediction study identifying high-pressure K-Al compounds, notably the P4/nmm KAl phase, as a topological electride hosting three-dimensional flat bands.
motivation: High-pressure synthesis can stabilize alkali-metal-rich compounds with interstitial anionic electrons (electrides), which are promising platforms for exotic electronic and topological phenomena such as flat bands and superconductivity.
method: Density functional theory (first-principles) calculations combined with ab initio crystal structure prediction (evolutionary/particle-swarm-type search) to identify stable K-Al phases up to high pressures, followed by band-structure and topological analysis.
result: The P4/nmm KAl phase is stable between 15 and 70 GPa and hosts a three-dimensional flat band near the Fermi level arising from the electride interstitial electrons, with nontrivial band topology.
conclusion: The work establishes t-KAl as a topological electride with 3D flat bands, suggesting routes to correlated flat-band physics and possible superconductivity in high-pressure alkali-aluminum compounds.

title: Tunable And Suppressible non-Hermitian Skin Effect Induced By non-Abelian Gauge Fields
authors: Wen-Cheng Jiang, Long Zhang, Yun-Mei Li, And Jian Li
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Cheng Jiang, Long Zhang, Yun-Mei Li, and Jian Li

We theoretically investigate a tunable and suppressible non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) in lattice systems governed by non-Abelian SU(2) gauge fields, Zeeman field, and spin-dependent gain and loss. We show that non-Abelian hopping alone can generate a parity-dependent discrepancy between open- and…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194207] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors theoretically study how non-Abelian SU(2) gauge fields, Zeeman fields, and spin-dependent gain/loss produce a tunable and suppressible non-Hermitian skin effect in lattice systems.
motivation: The non-Hermitian skin effect is a striking non-Hermitian topological phenomenon, but how non-Abelian gauge fields and spin-dependent dissipation could control or suppress it remains largely unexplored.
method: A tight-binding lattice model incorporating non-Abelian SU(2) hopping, a Zeeman term, and spin-dependent gain and loss is analyzed, comparing open and periodic boundary spectra and examining parity-dependent discrepancies.
result: Non-Abelian hopping alone generates a parity-dependent mismatch between open- and periodic-boundary spectra, and the skin effect can be tuned or suppressed via the gauge and Zeeman parameters.
conclusion: Non-Abelian gauge fields provide a versatile knob for engineering and suppressing non-Hermitian skin effects, suggesting new routes for non-Hermitian topological control.

title: Néel-vector-orientation Induced Direction-robust Spin Filtering In Two-dimensional Altermagnets
authors: Xin Chen, Jin Zou, Lipeng Song, Wei Sun, Yiwen Wu, Luyao Zhu, Xu Cheng, Duo Wang, And Biplab Sanyal
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Chen, Jin Zou, Lipeng Song, Wei Sun, Yiwen Wu, Luyao Zhu, Xu Cheng, Duo Wang, and Biplab Sanyal

Whether an antiferromagnet can host direction-robust spin-polarized transport without a conventional spin-selective band gap remains a central challenge in antiferromagnetic spintronics. Here, we establish a gapless, direction-robust spin-filtering mechanism in a compensated two-dimensional altermag…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194427] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a gapless, direction-robust spin-filtering mechanism in a compensated two-dimensional altermagnet driven by Néel-vector orientation.
motivation: Antiferromagnetic spintronics seeks spin-polarized transport without relying on conventional spin-selective band gaps, a long-standing challenge for compensated magnetic order.
method: First-principles/electronic-structure analysis of a two-dimensional altermagnet, examining how Néel-vector orientation reshapes spin-split bands and transport anisotropy.
result: A gapless spin-filtering effect emerges that is robust against the transport direction, controlled by the orientation of the Néel vector.
conclusion: Néel-vector orientation provides a handle for direction-robust spin filtering in 2D altermagnets, suggesting design principles for antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.

title: Quantum-metric Bloch Oscillations In Weakly Inhomogeneous Electric Fields
authors: M. Maneesh Kumar, Md Kaif Faiyaz, Sayan Sarkar, And Amit Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): M. Maneesh Kumar, Md Kaif Faiyaz, Sayan Sarkar, and Amit Agarwal

The geometric analogs of Bloch oscillations studied so far have relied on Berry curvature. We show that a weakly inhomogeneous electric field adds a distinct quantum-metric term to semiclassical wavepacket dynamics, generating an oscillatory real-space contribution even when the Berry curvature vani…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245422] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors show that a weakly inhomogeneous electric field introduces a quantum-metric (Fubini-Study) term into semiclassical wavepacket dynamics, producing real-space Bloch-like oscillations even when Berry curvature vanishes.
motivation: Geometric analogs of Bloch oscillations have so far been attributed exclusively to Berry curvature; the authors ask whether other band-geometry quantities, specifically the quantum metric, can generate independent oscillatory transport.
method: Semiclassical equations of motion for Bloch wavepackets are extended to include spatial gradients of the applied electric field, yielding a quantum-metric correction term that is evaluated for model band structures.
result: The quantum-metric term produces an oscillatory real-space displacement that persists in the absence of Berry curvature, giving a distinct geometric contribution to Bloch oscillation dynamics.
conclusion: Quantum-metric Bloch oscillations constitute a separate geometric transport effect, suggesting band-geometry spectroscopy via inhomogeneous-field transport measurements.

title: Critical And Tricritical Transitions In Diffusion With Stochastic Resetting On A Ring
authors: Pedro Julián-Salgado, Pavel Castro-Villarreal, Leonardo Dagdug, And Denis Boyer
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Julián-Salgado, Pavel Castro-Villarreal, Leonardo Dagdug, and Denis Boyer

Diffusion with a resetting mechanism provides a framework for modeling a wide range of natural phenomena. This work investigates the influence of stochastic resetting on diffusion of a Brownian particle in a closed domain with a trap. The authors focus on the average mean first passage time as a function of resetting rate. They find that a closed domain can produce unexpected results. The optimal resetting rate can vary abruptly or continuously, for example, depending upon parameters.

#TimelyTopic #ElegantVisuals


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044142] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes diffusion of a Brownian particle on a closed ring with a trap under stochastic resetting, characterizing how the optimal resetting rate changes via critical and tricritical transitions.
motivation: Stochastic resetting is a widely used framework for modeling search processes and natural phenomena, and the authors ask how confinement to a closed domain with a trap alters the optimal resetting behavior.
method: They compute the average mean first passage time as a function of the resetting rate for a Brownian particle diffusing in a closed ring geometry containing a trap, and analyze the resulting dependence to identify abrupt versus continuous transitions.
result: They find that a closed domain produces unexpected behavior, with the optimal resetting rate varying either abruptly (critical) or continuously (tricritical) depending on system parameters.
conclusion: The work maps out a phase-diagram-like classification of optimal resetting regimes in confined geometries, extending resetting theory beyond open domains.

title: Minimal Representations Of Topology-preserving Quantumlike States
authors: William Horvat, Debadrita Saha, Nicolás Gigena, Prineha Narang, And Gregory D. Scholes
abstract:
Author(s): William Horvat, Debadrita Saha, Nicolás Gigena, Prineha Narang, and Gregory D. Scholes

We provide an equitable partition that gives an exact, minimal representation for the graph Cartesian product formed from quantumlike bits that preserves the relevant spectral and topological properties. We show that this result follows from the fact that the operations of taking the Cartesian produ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044326] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs an equitable partition yielding a minimal representation for graph Cartesian products of quantumlike bits while preserving spectral and topological properties.
motivation: The authors aim to simplify complex graph structures built from quantumlike bits without losing the relevant spectral and topological information.
method: They use equitable partitions and properties of graph Cartesian products to derive an exact minimal representation.
result: An exact minimal representation is obtained for Cartesian-product graphs formed from quantumlike bits, preserving the relevant spectral and topological invariants.
conclusion: The result provides a compact graph-theoretic description of topology-preserving quantumlike states, with potential use in spectral graph analysis.

title: Using Echo-state Networks To Reproduce Rare Events In Chaotic Systems
authors: Anton Erofeev, Balasubramanya T. Nadiga, And Ilya Timofeyev
abstract:
Author(s): Anton Erofeev, Balasubramanya T. Nadiga, and Ilya Timofeyev

Echo-state networks (ESNs) are known to reproduce the trajectories and main properties of chaotic attractors. Here, we investigate the question of whether ESNs can reproduce rare events in a system with a stationary distribution with slowly decaying bounded tails. In particular, we consider the chao…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044220] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper tests whether echo-state networks can reproduce rare events in a chaotic dynamical system with slowly decaying stationary-distribution tails.
motivation: Echo-state networks are known to capture trajectories and main properties of chaotic attractors, but it is unclear whether they can faithfully reproduce rare extreme events governed by heavy-tailed statistics.
method: The authors train echo-state networks on a chaotic system whose stationary distribution has slowly decaying bounded tails and evaluate the network's ability to reproduce rare-event statistics.
result: The study assesses the capacity of ESNs to capture rare events and likely identifies limitations or conditions under which reservoir models reproduce such tail statistics.
conclusion: The work contributes to machine learning for chaotic dynamics but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Maximization Of Nuclear Fusion Reactivity Via Optimal Energy Distributions
authors: Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, And Carlo Presilla
abstract:
Author(s): Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, and Carlo Presilla

We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044136] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper optimizes nuclear fusion reactivity over energy probability distributions and finds that a single Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution is optimal where reactivity is concave in average kinetic energy.
motivation: Fusion reactivity depends sensitively on the particle energy distribution, so identifying optimal distributions could inform fusion performance beyond standard thermal assumptions.
method: The authors analyze fusion reactivity as a functional of energy probability distributions and compare Maxwell-Boltzmann and nonthermal distributions using concavity properties of the reactivity function.
result: A single Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution maximizes reactivity in the concave regime near relevant fusion energies, while nonthermal distributions do not improve performance there.
conclusion: The findings clarify when thermal distributions are optimal for fusion reactivity and delimit regimes where engineered nonthermal distributions might matter.

title: Nonclassical Cutoff Fluctuations In Squeezed-light-driven High-harmonic Generation
authors: Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, And Igor V. Litvinyuk
abstract:
Author(s): Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, and Igor V. Litvinyuk

In the conventional description of strong-field high-harmonic generation (HHG), the atom is treated quantum mechanically while the driving laser is represented by a classical field. Quantum fluctuations of the driver can become relevant in nanoscale interaction geometries, where tight spatial confin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043107] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how nonclassical fluctuations of squeezed driving light affect cutoff fluctuations in high-harmonic generation.
motivation: Conventional high-harmonic generation treats the driving laser classically, but quantum fluctuations can matter in nanoscale interaction geometries with tight spatial confinement.
method: The authors theoretically analyze high-harmonic generation driven by squeezed light, focusing on quantum fluctuations of the driver and their imprint on the harmonic cutoff.
result: They find nonclassical cutoff fluctuations arising from the squeezed-light quantum noise, distinguishing the effect from classical laser fluctuations.
conclusion: Squeezed-light driving introduces quantum-optical signatures in high-harmonic generation, relevant for nanoscale strong-field interaction geometries.

title: Long-range States In Collisions Of Ultracold Molecules
authors: James F. E. Croft, Brian K. Kendrick, And Jeremy M. Hutson
abstract:
Author(s): James F. E. Croft, Brian K. Kendrick, and Jeremy M. Hutson

We use coupled-channel calculations to explore the nature of near-threshold bound states in a simplified model of [MATH]. This is a prototype for systems with very strong coupling at short range and chaotic behavior for the short-range states. We find that there are states with s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043087] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Coupled-channel calculations are used to characterize near-threshold bound states in a simplified model of ultracold molecule collisions with strong short-range coupling and chaotic short-range spectra.
motivation: The authors aim to understand long-range states and near-threshold physics in ultracold molecular collisions, where short-range interactions are strong and chaotic.
method: They perform coupled-channel scattering calculations on a simplified model molecular system and analyze the resulting near-threshold bound-state structure.
result: The calculations reveal long-range states whose properties are influenced by strong short-range coupling and chaotic short-range state behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the bound-state structure of ultracold molecular collisions, relevant to molecular collision physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Space-time Floquet Operator: Nonreciprocity And Fractional Topology Of Space-time Crystals
authors: Abhijeet Melkani And Jayson Paulose
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijeet Melkani and Jayson Paulose

A space-time Floquet operator is introduced that captures the long-time dynamics of systems with intertwined spatial and temporal periodicities. The resulting band framework uncovers fractional quantized charge pumping, connects topological windings to Floquet–Bloch oscillations, and predicts nonreciprocal amplification.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042009] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a space-time Floquet operator for systems with coupled spatial and temporal periodicity, revealing fractional charge pumping, topological windings linked to Floquet-Bloch oscillations, and nonreciprocal amplification.
motivation: Systems with intertwined spatial and temporal periodicities require a framework that captures their long-time dynamics beyond standard Floquet or Bloch descriptions.
method: The authors define a space-time Floquet operator and derive a band framework for such space-time crystals, connecting topological invariants to pumping and amplification phenomena.
result: The framework predicts fractional quantized charge pumping, relates topological windings to Floquet-Bloch oscillations, and identifies nonreciprocal amplification.
conclusion: Space-time Floquet bands provide a unified topological description of space-time crystals with potential for nonreciprocal transport and fractional pumping.

title: Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport In A Trsb Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
authors: Wenyao Liu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Wenyao Liu et al.

Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements in thin
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041022] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Thin flakes of a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking topological iron-based superconductor show edge-mediated nonlocal transport with a robust conductance plateau attributed to spontaneous magnetic ordering.
motivation: Topological superconductors hosting spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry breaking are candidate platforms for exotic edge modes, and their transport signatures remain poorly characterized experimentally.
method: Nonlocal electrical transport measurements on thin devices fabricated from a TRSB topological iron-based superconductor, with conductance tracked as a function of temperature, field, and device geometry.
result: A robust conductance plateau is observed in the nonlocal channel, consistent with edge-mediated superconducting transport governed by spontaneous magnetic ordering in the material.
conclusion: The findings support edge-dominated nonlocal transport in TRSB topological superconductors, but the work is a materials/condensed-matter study with no direct quantum-information or thermodynamic analysis.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Their Thermodynamic Fate In Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
authors: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, And Haruki Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, and Haruki Watanabe

A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041016] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A general theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin classical pyrochlore spin ice shows that S=3/2 magnets uniquely host an abrupt transition between two spin-liquid states that survives thermal fluctuations, while all other spin values yield only crossovers.
motivation: Spin ice has been studied intensively for its emergent Coulomb-phase physics, but how the spin-liquid phenomenology depends on the local spin quantum number S — and whether sharp topological transitions can persist at finite temperature — was unclear.
method: The authors construct a general theoretical treatment of classical pyrochlore spin ice with arbitrary spin length S, analyzing the effective interactions and their consequent phase behavior, and then examine the thermal fate of the candidate topological phase transitions across the S parameter range.
result: The analysis reveals that only the S=3/2 case exhibits an abrupt transition between two distinct spin-liquid states, whereas for other spin sizes the would-be transitions are washed out by thermal fluctuations into smooth crossovers.
conclusion: Sharp spin-liquid-to-spin-liquid transitions in classical pyrochlore ice are special to S=3/2, providing a sharp criterion for when such topological transitions can be observed experimentally rather than being thermally smeared.

title: Observation Of Wannier-Rydberg And Charge-Transfer Hybrid Moiré Excitons Under Pressure
authors: Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, And Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, and Yang Xu

Hydrostatic pressure continuously tunes the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover to a strong-moiré regime that hybridizes Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041007] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Hydrostatic pressure is used to tune the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover into a strong-moiré regime where Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons hybridize.
motivation: Moiré excitons in twisted or lattice-mismatched semiconductor heterostructures offer a tunable platform for studying correlated excitonic physics, but the regime where the moiré potential dominates exciton binding is hard to access.
method: Pressure-dependent optical spectroscopy on a semiconductor moiré superlattice, tracking exciton resonances as hydrostatic pressure continuously modifies the moiré potential depth and lattice parameters.
result: A pressure-driven crossover into the strong-moiré regime is observed, evidenced by hybridized exciton states combining Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer character.
conclusion: Pressure provides a continuous tuning knob for moiré exciton physics, enabling controlled exploration of hybridized excitonic states in semiconductor superlattices.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal And Scalar Spin Chirality In Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, and Pengcheng Dai

Neutron scattering experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering on tetragonal YbMnBi2 reveals a field-induced dynamic spin nematic state whose scalar spin chirality drives anomalous Hall and Nernst responses in the paramagnetic phase.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how magnetic fluctuations and scalar spin chirality can generate anomalous transport in a paramagnetic metallic magnet, a regime where conventional ordered-moment explanations fail.
method: Elastic and inelastic neutron scattering experiments on YbMnBi2 single crystals under applied magnetic fields, combined with symmetry and chirality analysis of the magnetic scattering intensity.
result: A dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal-like state emerges in field, producing non-zero scalar spin chirality that accounts for the observed anomalous Hall and Nernst effects well above any magnetic ordering temperature.
conclusion: Spin-nematic correlations and scalar spin chirality provide a mechanism for anomalous transport in paramagnetic phases, extending the phenomenology of chirality-driven Berry-curvature effects in tetragonal magnets.

title: Precision Isotope-Shift Measurement Of The ${^{1}s}_{0}↔{^{3}p}_{2}$ Transition And A Multitransition King-Plot Consistency Test
authors: Taiki Ishiyama, Koki Ono, Reiji Asano, Hokuto Kawase, Tetsushi Takano, Ayaki Sunaga, Yasuhiro Yamamoto, Minoru Tanaka, And Yoshiro Takahashi
abstract:
Author(s): Taiki Ishiyama, Koki Ono, Reiji Asano, Hokuto Kawase, Tetsushi Takano, Ayaki Sunaga, Yasuhiro Yamamoto, Minoru Tanaka, and Yoshiro Takahashi

We present precision spectroscopy and isotope shift measurement of the [MATH] clock transition in neutral ytterbium (Yb) atoms. By revealing a magic wavelength at 905.4(2) nm, we successfully achieve the atomic spectrum narrower than 100 Hz. The interleaved clock operation between…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 183401] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports precision spectroscopy and isotope-shift measurements of an ytterbium clock transition, including a magic wavelength near 905.4 nm and a multitransition King-plot consistency test.
motivation: Precision isotope-shift measurements in atomic clocks can test atomic structure and search for physics beyond the Standard Model, but this work is primarily an atomic-physics metrology study.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy of the 1S0 to 3P2 transition in neutral ytterbium, identify a magic wavelength, and compare isotope shifts across multiple transitions using King-plot analysis.
result: They achieve sub-100 Hz spectral resolution and obtain isotope-shift data that enable a consistency test of the King-plot framework across transitions.
conclusion: The work advances precision ytterbium clock spectroscopy and isotope-shift metrology, but it does not directly address quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Beyond The Dilute Instanton Gas: Resurgence With Exact Saddles In The Double Well
authors: Aurélien Dersy And Matthew D. Schwartz
abstract:
Author(s): Aurélien Dersy and Matthew D. Schwartz

The path-integral approach to the double well has long been limited by the dilute instanton gas approximation. We show that if the finite Euclidean-time structure is taken seriously by using exact saddles, the dilute gas can be sidestepped, allowing the partition function and energy levels to be com…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181601] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an exact-saddle resurgence approach to the quantum double-well path integral, avoiding the dilute instanton gas approximation.
motivation: The dilute instanton gas has long constrained path-integral treatments of the double well, especially when finite Euclidean-time structure matters.
method: The authors use exact Euclidean-time saddles rather than the dilute instanton gas to evaluate the path integral for the double well.
result: They obtain the partition function and energy levels beyond the dilute-gas approximation.
conclusion: Exact saddles provide a resurgence-based route to nonperturbative double-well physics without relying on diluteness.

title: Nonreciprocal Lensing And Backscattering Suppression Via Magneto-optical Nonlocality
authors: Dmitry Vagin And Maxim A. Gorlach
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitry Vagin and Maxim A. Gorlach
