We introduce a special kind of nonreciprocal electromagnetic response that gives rise to backscattering suppression in the bulk, a long-sought feature in topological photonics, as well as nonreciprocal lensing—an effect when the same structure focuses light incident from one direction and defocuses …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186901] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a magneto-optical nonlocal electromagnetic response that suppresses backscattering in the bulk and produces nonreciprocal lensing, where one structure focuses light from one direction and defocuses it from the other.
motivation: Backscattering suppression is a long-sought goal in topological photonics, and nonreciprocal optical elements are desirable for isolators and directional wave control.
method: The authors analyze a magneto-optical medium with a spatially nonlocal (wavevector-dependent) permittivity response, deriving the resulting nonreciprocal propagation and lensing behavior theoretically.
result: The nonlocal magneto-optical response yields bulk backscattering suppression together with directional focusing/defocusing of incident light.
conclusion: Magneto-optical nonlocality provides a route to nonreciprocal, backscattering-free photonic components relevant to topological and nonreciprocal photonics.

title: Topological Defect States Via Local Symmetry Breaking In Modified Haldane Models
authors: Chengxi Yang, Jialin Liu, Jianfei Li, Yuanhang Jiang, Zheyu Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Zhongxiang Zhou, And Chengxun Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Chengxi Yang, Jialin Liu, Jianfei Li, Yuanhang Jiang, Zheyu Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Zhongxiang Zhou, and Chengxun Yuan

Antichiral edge states extend the conventional bulk-edge correspondence by allowing edge modes on two parallel boundaries to propagate in the same direction, compensated by counterpropagating bulk states. However, their strong localization at physical boundaries leads to a severe dependence on bound…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043533] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological defect states and antichiral edge modes in modified Haldane models where local symmetry breaking is used to control edge-state localization.
motivation: Antichiral edge states, which propagate in the same direction on two parallel boundaries and are compensated by counterpropagating bulk modes, are strongly localized at physical boundaries and therefore highly sensitive to boundary conditions; the authors aim to relax this dependence.
method: Modified Haldane lattice models are analyzed, using local symmetry breaking together with tight-binding/band-structure analysis of edge and bulk spectra.
result: Local symmetry breaking is shown to produce and relocate topological defect states, modifying the antichiral edge-mode structure and its localization properties.
conclusion: The results extend bulk-edge correspondence considerations in Haldane-type models and suggest a route to boundary-robust topological edge-state engineering.

title: Scattering And Bound States Of Two Heteronuclear Ultracold Atoms In A Quasi-two-dimensional Confinement
authors: Binhao Wang, Fan Yang, And Peng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Binhao Wang, Fan Yang, and Peng Zhang

We solve the two-body problem of ultracold heteronuclear atoms in a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) geometry. The quasi-2D confinement is realized by a harmonic trap along the longitudinal ([MATH]) direction, with different trap frequencies for the two atoms, as in many current experiments on ultracol…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043312] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper solves the two-body scattering and bound-state problem for heteronuclear ultracold atoms confined in a quasi-2D harmonic trap with species-dependent trap frequencies.
motivation: Quasi-2D ultracold mixtures are experimentally relevant, and understanding two-body scattering and bound states is necessary for interpreting and controlling such systems.
method: The authors solve the two-body Schrödinger problem for heteronuclear atoms under longitudinal harmonic confinement, accounting for different trap frequencies for the two atoms.
result: They obtain the scattering properties and bound-state spectrum in the quasi-2D geometry as functions of the confinement and atomic parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of heteronuclear ultracold collisions in quasi-2D traps, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platform characterization.

title: Circular Dichroism In Second- And Third-harmonic Generation In The Chiral Topological Semimetal CoSi
authors: Yuya Ominato And Masahito Mochizuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yuya Ominato and Masahito Mochizuki

We theoretically investigate circular dichroism (CD) in second- and third-harmonic generation (SHG and THG) in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi. We demonstrate that both SHG and THG exhibit dichroic responses of order unity, while their robustness against spectral broadening is strikingly diffe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214306] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of circular dichroism in second- and third-harmonic generation in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi, comparing their robustness to spectral broadening.
motivation: Chiral topological semimetals host exotic multifold fermions whose optical selection rules are poorly characterized; nonlinear dichroic responses could provide a spectroscopic probe of chiral band topology.
method: Model calculations of the nonlinear optical susceptibility tensors for SHG and THG based on the low-energy effective Hamiltonian / band structure of CoSi, including the effects of spectral broadening.
result: Both SHG and THG show dichroic responses of order unity, but they differ strikingly in their robustness against spectral broadening, making one process a sharper probe of chirality.
conclusion: The contrasting broadening sensitivity of SHG versus THG circular dichroism offers a route to identify chiral topological band features in CoSi and related compounds.

title: Longitudinal Transport Spin Polarization Of Spin Degenerate Antiferromagnets
authors: Meng Zhu, Jianting Dong, Xinlu Li, Jiahao Shentu, Yizhuo Song, Evgeny Y. Tsymbal, And Jia Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Zhu, Jianting Dong, Xinlu Li, Jiahao Shentu, Yizhuo Song, Evgeny Y. Tsymbal, and Jia Zhang

A vital goal in spintronics is the efficient electrical generation of spin currents, a pursuit that has recently focused on using antiferromagnets (AFMs) as spin current sources. It has been demonstrated that antiferromagnets with broken [MATH] symmetry (parity + time reversal) can efficiently generat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214431] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: This work studies the longitudinal spin transport polarization generated by spin-degenerate antiferromagnets, identifying symmetry conditions under which such AFMs can act as efficient electrical spin-current sources.
motivation: Efficient electrical generation of spin currents is a central goal in spintronics, and antiferromagnets have recently emerged as promising passive spin-current sources, motivating a systematic understanding of which magnetic symmetries permit finite longitudinal spin polarization.
method: The authors combine symmetry analysis (parity and time-reversal breaking) with first-principles electronic structure calculations and transport theory to evaluate the longitudinal spin polarization of spin-degenerate antiferromagnetic materials.
result: They show that antiferromagnets with broken PT symmetry can support nonzero longitudinal transport spin polarization, and quantify the polarization for candidate AFM compounds, linking it to band-structure and symmetry properties.
conclusion: Spin-degenerate antiferromagnets with suitable symmetry breaking are viable spin-current sources, providing design principles for antiferromagnet-based spintronic devices.

title: Curvature-controlled Spin-wave Localization And Soft-mode Instabilities In Magnetic Nanotube Multilayers
authors: P. Contreras-Gallardo, A. Kákay, And R. A. Gallardo
abstract:
Author(s): P. Contreras-Gallardo, A. Kákay, and R. A. Gallardo

Here, the authors reveal how curvature reshapes spin-wave dynamics and magnetic instabilities in synthetic antiferromagnetic nanotubes. The tubular geometry produces asymmetric mode localization and nonreciprocal propagation, while radial anisotropy drives a crossover from uniform softening to a finite-wave-vector instability. The latter signals the emergence of a stripe-like magnetic modulation along the nanotube axis.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194430] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Curvature in synthetic antiferromagnetic nanotube multilayers produces asymmetric spin-wave localization, nonreciprocal propagation, and a crossover to a finite-wave-vector soft-mode instability that signals stripe-like magnetic modulation.
motivation: Understanding how curved geometries reshape spin-wave dynamics and magnetic instabilities is relevant for curvilinear magnonics, where tubular architectures offer new routes to control magnetization and wave propagation.
method: Micromagnetic modeling and analytical treatment of synthetic antiferromagnetic nanotubes with radial anisotropy, examining mode localization, nonreciprocity, and soft-mode dispersion as a function of curvature and anisotropy.
result: The tubular geometry yields asymmetric mode localization and nonreciprocal spin-wave propagation, while increasing radial anisotropy drives a crossover from uniform (q=0) softening to a finite-wave-vector instability.
conclusion: Curvature and anisotropy provide knobs to engineer spin-wave localization and to select between uniform and modulated (stripe-like) magnetic ground states in nanotube multilayers.

title: Merging Bound States In The Continuum Into An Exceptional Point Via Magnetic Field
authors: Yadong Yue, Kun Liang, And Li Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yadong Yue, Kun Liang, and Li Yu

Exceptional points (EPs) and bound states in the continuum (BICs) are two distinct types of optical singularities that have attracted significant attention for their potential. While EPs are known for their enhanced sensitivity to perturbations, their performance in passive resonator systems is ofte…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235419] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies how bound states in the continuum can be merged into an exceptional point in an optical resonator using a magnetic field.
motivation: Exceptional points offer enhanced sensitivity but can be limited in passive resonator systems, while bound states in the continuum provide robust optical singularities; the work aims to combine these features in a tunable platform.
method: The authors analyze optical resonances in a magnetic-field-controlled resonator system and derive conditions under which multiple bound states in the continuum coalesce into an exceptional point.
result: A magnetic field is shown to enable the merging of bound states in the continuum into an exceptional point, providing a route to tunable singular optics.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism may be useful for enhanced sensing and controlling light-matter interactions in passive photonic structures, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tuning The Fermi Surface Of ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$ By Nb Doping
authors: Andrew P. Weber, Iñigo Robredo, Philipp Rüßmann, Maxim Ilyn, Arnaud Magrez, Philippe Bugnon, Nan Xu, Vladimir N. Strocov, J. Hugo Dil, J. Enrique Ortega, And Julen Ibañez-Azpiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew P. Weber, Iñigo Robredo, Philipp Rüßmann, Maxim Ilyn, Arnaud Magrez, Philippe Bugnon, Nan Xu, Vladimir N. Strocov, J. Hugo Dil, J. Enrique Ortega, and Julen Ibañez-Azpiroz

Ab initio calculations and angle-resolved photoemission experiments demonstrate that the bulk and surface electronic structure of Weyl semimetal candidate [MATH] changes significantly by tuning the chemical potential by less than 0.4 eV. Calculations indicate that several Lifshitz tra…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225145] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: Ab initio calculations and ARPES experiments show that the bulk and surface electronic structure of the Weyl-semimetal candidate MoTe2 is strongly modified by Nb doping that shifts the chemical potential by less than 0.4 eV.
motivation: MoTe2 is a candidate type-II Weyl semimetal, and controlling its Fermi surface via doping is a route to accessing distinct topological band regimes and Lifshitz transitions.
method: Density-functional (ab initio) band-structure calculations are combined with soft X-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on Nb-doped MoTe2 crystals to map bulk and surface dispersions.
result: Small chemical-potential shifts of under 0.4 eV drive several Lifshitz transitions and significantly alter both bulk and surface electronic structure, in agreement between theory and experiment.
conclusion: Doping provides a practical tuning knob for the Fermi-surface topology of MoTe2, relevant for engineering topological semimetal phases.

title: Thermoelectric Enhancement From An Asymmetric Spectral-conductivity Cusp In Spin-1 Chiral Fermions
authors: Risako Kikuchi, Junya Endo, And Ai Yamakage
abstract:
Author(s): Risako Kikuchi, Junya Endo, and Ai Yamakage

A recent study showed that, in spin-1 chiral fermion systems composed of two linearly dispersing bands and one trivial band, impurity scattering produces an asymmetric cusp in the spectral conductivity [MATH]. We demonstrate that this asymmetric cusp markedly enhances the electronic thermoelectric r…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225204] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports that an asymmetric cusp in spectral conductivity arising from impurity scattering in spin-1 chiral fermion systems enhances thermoelectric performance.
motivation: Recent work found impurity scattering can produce an asymmetric spectral-conductivity cusp in spin-1 chiral fermions, motivating an investigation of its thermoelectric consequences.
method: The authors analyze electronic thermoelectric response for a spin-1 chiral fermion model composed of two linearly dispersing bands and one trivial band, focusing on the asymmetric spectral-conductivity cusp generated by impurity scattering.
result: The asymmetric cusp is shown to markedly enhance the electronic thermoelectric figure of merit or related thermoelectric response.
conclusion: The findings suggest that spectral-conductivity asymmetry in chiral fermion systems can be exploited for thermoelectric enhancement, but the work is outside quantum information science.

title: Phase Lags Induce Chaos In Oscillator Communities With Higher-order Interactions
authors: Sabina Adhikari, Juan G. Restrepo, And Per Sebastian Skardal
abstract:
Author(s): Sabina Adhikari, Juan G. Restrepo, and Per Sebastian Skardal

We study the effects of phase-frustrated, higher-order interactions in a system of coupled phase oscillators with two communities. We use dimensionality reduction techniques to derive a low-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) to describe the macroscopic behavior of the syste…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044328] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phase-frustrated higher-order interactions in a two-community coupled phase-oscillator model and shows that phase lags can induce chaotic macroscopic dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how phase frustration and higher-order interactions shape collective behavior in oscillator communities, extending prior work on low-dimensional reductions of coupled oscillator networks.
method: They use dimensionality reduction techniques to derive a low-dimensional system of ODEs describing the macroscopic dynamics of two coupled oscillator communities with higher-order interactions.
result: The reduced model reveals that phase lags can destabilize synchronized states and lead to chaotic dynamics in the macroscopic variables.
conclusion: Phase frustration is a key mechanism for inducing chaos in higher-order oscillator communities, highlighting richer collective dynamics than in pairwise-only models.

title: It Takes Two To Tribo: Stochastic Charge Evolution In Repeated Binary Collisions Of Acoustically Levitated Particles
authors: Tom F. O'hara, Adrian C. Barnes, James W. E. Drewitt, Nathan Croll Dawes, And Karen L. Aplin
abstract:
Author(s): Tom F. O'Hara, Adrian C. Barnes, James W. E. Drewitt, Nathan Croll Dawes, and Karen L. Aplin

Despite many models proposed to explain charging behavior between insulating particles, the mechanisms underlying triboelectric charging have remained an open question in nonequilibrium physics. This manuscript presents a new experimental method to measure charge transfer during collisions between individual pairs of levitated particles, showing that charge evolution saturates as predicted by the condenser model.

#AdvancingField #TimelyTopic #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045409] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally measures stochastic charge transfer in repeated binary collisions of acoustically levitated insulating particles and compares the observed saturation with the condenser model.
motivation: Triboelectric charging between insulating particles remains poorly understood despite many proposed models, and controlled measurements of charge transfer in individual particle collisions are scarce.
method: The authors use acoustically levitated particle pairs to track charge evolution over repeated collisions, enabling direct measurement of charge transfer between two isolated particles.
result: Charge evolution is observed to saturate, consistent with the predictions of the condenser model for triboelectric charging.
conclusion: The experiment provides a controlled platform for testing triboelectric charging models and supports saturation behavior in repeated binary collisions.

title: Analytic Phase Solution And Point Vortex Model For Dipolar Quantum Vortices
authors: Ryan Doran And Thomas Bland
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Doran and Thomas Bland

An analytic expression is derived for the phase of a quantum vortex in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate, capturing the anisotropy introduced by the long-range dipole-dipole interactions. Using this phase profile, the dipolar point vortex model is formulated; this model reproduces the anisotropic velocities, deformed orbits, and orientation-dependent motion of vortex pairs found in full numerical simulations of the condensate.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042014] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an analytic phase profile for quantum vortices in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates and uses it to formulate a dipolar point-vortex model that reproduces anisotropic vortex dynamics.
motivation: Vortices in dipolar condensates exhibit anisotropic behavior due to long-range dipole-dipole interactions, requiring models beyond the standard isotropic point-vortex description.
method: An analytic expression for the vortex phase is derived, incorporating dipolar anisotropy, and then used to construct a point-vortex model. The model is compared with full numerical simulations of the condensate.
result: The dipolar point-vortex model captures anisotropic velocities, deformed vortex-pair orbits, and orientation-dependent motion observed in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The analytic phase solution and point-vortex model provide a useful reduced description of vortex dynamics in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates.

title: Direct Observation Of Thermal Spin Depolarization In A Type ${\mathrm{I}}_{\mathrm{B}}$ Half-metal $\mathrm{Ni}{\mathrm{Co}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$ By Spin-resolved Photoemission
authors: Hirokazu Fujiwara, Tomoki Higashikawa, Enda Xiao, Terumasa Tadano, Lingling Xie, Daisuke Kan, Yuichi Shimakawa, Kaishu Kawaguchi, Ryo Mori, Ayumi Harasawa, Takeshi Kondo, And Takayoshi Yokoya
abstract:
Author(s): Hirokazu Fujiwara, Tomoki Higashikawa, Enda Xiao, Terumasa Tadano, Lingling Xie, Daisuke Kan, Yuichi Shimakawa, Kaishu Kawaguchi, Ryo Mori, Ayumi Harasawa, Takeshi Kondo, and Takayoshi Yokoya

Half-metals (HMs), characterized by 100% spin polarization at the Fermi level ([MATH]), are ideal candidates for future spintronic memory devices. However, their spin polarization rapidly decreases with temperature, limiting their practical implementation. While this degradation has been…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043099] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Spin-resolved photoemission experiments and first-principles calculations show that thermal spin depolarization in the half-metal NiCo2O4 arises from spin-wave-like transverse fluctuations rather than from changes in the electronic structure.
motivation: Half-metals offer 100% spin polarization at the Fermi level, which makes them attractive for spintronic memory, but their polarization degrades quickly with temperature; the microscopic origin of this degradation had not been directly observed.
method: The authors use spin-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to measure the temperature dependence of the spin polarization at the Fermi level in the type-I_B half-metal NiCo2O4, and they interpret the results together with first-principles calculations of thermally induced spin disorder.
result: The spin polarization is found to decrease strongly with increasing temperature, which is consistent with thermally excited transverse spin fluctuations (spin waves and magnons) that mix the minority and majority spin channels.
conclusion: The thermal depolarization of NiCo2O4 is intrinsic and magnetic in origin, so stabilizing half-metallicity for spintronic applications requires suppressing low-energy spin excitations, for example by raising the magnon gap or by tuning the Curie temperature.

title: Electromagnetic Backaction In A Resonant Bose Gas: Controlled Spectral Shifts And Limits Of Local Response
authors: Johannes Fiedler
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Fiedler

Resonant atoms modify the electromagnetic environment that in turn determines their optical response, giving rise to a self-consistent light-matter problem at finite density. We investigate this feedback for the hydrogen Lyman-[MATH] transition using a local effective-medium description combined with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043101] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electromagnetic backaction and spectral shifts in a resonant Bose gas near the hydrogen Lyman transition using a local effective-medium description.
motivation: Resonant atoms modify their electromagnetic environment, creating a self-consistent light-matter feedback problem whose consequences for dense atomic gases are not fully captured by simple local-response models.
method: The author employs a local effective-medium description combined with a self-consistent light-matter treatment to analyze the optical response of a resonant Bose gas at finite density.
result: The analysis identifies controlled spectral shifts induced by electromagnetic backaction and clarifies the limits of the local-response approximation for such resonant media.
conclusion: Electromagnetic backaction provides a route to tune spectral shifts in resonant Bose gases, while local effective-medium descriptions have inherent validity limits that must be accounted for at finite density.

title: Temperature-induced Superconductivity Enhancement Under Large Exchange Fields
authors: Xusheng Wang, Lianyi He, And Shuai-Hua Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Xusheng Wang, Lianyi He, and Shuai-Hua Ji

Through a comprehensive free energy analysis, we demonstrate that finite temperature can simultaneously weaken superconductivity and mitigate Zeeman-effect-induced depairing, leading to potential nonmonotonic temperature-dependent behaviors in superconductors subjected to large exchange fields. Rema…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043079] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: A free-energy analysis shows that finite temperature can weaken superconductivity while also reducing Zeeman depairing in large exchange fields, enabling nonmonotonic temperature-dependent superconducting behavior.
motivation: Large exchange fields generally suppress superconductivity via Zeeman-induced pair breaking, but the interplay with finite-temperature effects is not fully understood.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive free-energy analysis of superconductors under large exchange fields, comparing pairing and depairing contributions at finite temperature.
result: They find that temperature can simultaneously suppress superconductivity and mitigate Zeeman depairing, leading to possible nonmonotonic temperature dependence of superconducting order.
conclusion: The work highlights a competing finite-temperature mechanism in exchange-field superconductivity and suggests conditions for temperature-induced enhancement effects.

title: Electronic Structure Associated With Nonsymmorphic Nodal Lines In Rare-earth Tetraborides
authors: Y. Kondo, S. Souma, G. Hoshino, A. Homma, T. Osumi, D. Shiga, H. Kumigashira, K. Ozawa, T. Koretsune, K. Segawa, And T. Sato
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Kondo, S. Souma, G. Hoshino, A. Homma, T. Osumi, D. Shiga, H. Kumigashira, K. Ozawa, T. Koretsune, K. Segawa, and T. Sato

We report a combined microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles study of the rare-earth tetraborides [MATH] [MATH], which host a Shastry-Sutherland lattice. We identify extended bulk nodal lines at the tetragonal Brillouin-zone bo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043067] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: ARPES and first-principles calculations identify extended bulk nonsymmorphic nodal lines in rare-earth tetraborides on a Shastry-Sutherland lattice.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the electronic structure and topological band features of rare-earth tetraborides, which host a Shastry-Sutherland lattice and are predicted to support nodal-line physics.
method: The study combines microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy with first-principles density functional calculations to map the bulk band structure and identify nodal lines.
result: Extended bulk nodal lines are observed at the tetragonal Brillouin-zone boundary, consistent with the nonsymmorphic symmetry of the material class.
conclusion: The work establishes rare-earth tetraborides as a platform for nonsymmorphic nodal-line electronic structure, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anomalous Metallic States At Magnetic Interfaces In An Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator Candidate DyPtBi With Ferroquadrupolar Order
authors: Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, And Yoshinori Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, and Yoshinori Tokura

Transport and neutron experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041028] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Transport and neutron experiments on the antiferromagnetic topological insulator candidate DyPtBi show that uniaxial stress aligns magnetic domains and suppresses conductive domain walls, enabling mechanical control of topological states intertwined with ferroquadrupolar order.
motivation: The study aims to understand and control how magnetic domain walls and multipolar order affect electronic transport in a topological insulator candidate with intertwined magnetism.
method: The authors perform magnetotransport measurements and neutron scattering on DyPtBi under applied uniaxial stress to align magnetic domains and probe the coupling between multipolar order and topology.
result: Uniaxial stress aligns magnetic domains and eliminates conductive domain-wall contributions, revealing anomalous metallic states at magnetic interfaces and demonstrating mechanical control of the topological state.
conclusion: The work establishes a route to mechanically tune topological states coupled to multipolar magnetic order in DyPtBi, with implications for domain-wall physics in antiferromagnetic topological materials.

title: Erratum: Faster Quantum Chemistry Simulations On A Quantum Computer With Improved Tensor Factorization And Active Volume Compilation [prx Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)]
authors: Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, And Christofer S. Tautermann
abstract:
Author(s): Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, and Christofer S. Tautermann
[PRX Quantum 7, 049901] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the published article on faster quantum chemistry simulations using improved tensor factorization and active volume compilation.
motivation: The original work aimed to reduce the resource cost of quantum chemistry simulations on quantum computers through better tensor factorization and circuit compilation techniques.
method: The erratum notes corrections to the original publication; the underlying work combines tensor-factorization-based Hamiltonian decomposition with active-volume compilation for quantum chemistry circuits.
result: The correction updates the record of the original PRX Quantum paper (6, 030337 (2025)); no new scientific results are presented here.
conclusion: The item is a bibliographic correction rather than a research contribution, and concerns quantum chemistry algorithms rather than any of the tracked research directions.

title: Nonrelativistic Optically Induced Spin Torque In Noncollinear Magnets
authors: Zhiyuan Li And Jian Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Li and Jian Zhou

Spin torque can be induced in noncollinear magnets by nonlinear light in the absence of nonrelativistic spin-orbit coupling, and can generate an effective magnetic field of ~30 Tesla under modest light in realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186905] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes that nonlinear light can induce spin torque in noncollinear magnets without relativistic spin-orbit coupling, producing effective magnetic fields of about 30 Tesla.
motivation: Optical control of magnetization typically relies on spin-orbit coupling or relativistic effects; the authors explore whether nonrelativistic optical processes can generate spin torque in noncollinear magnetic materials.
method: The study develops a theoretical mechanism for optically induced spin torque in noncollinear magnets and estimates the resulting effective magnetic field in realistic materials.
result: The mechanism can generate an effective magnetic field of approximately 30 Tesla under modest light illumination in realistic noncollinear magnets.
conclusion: Nonrelativistic optically induced spin torque provides a potential route for all-optical magnetization control in noncollinear magnets, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Plasmascopy Of Ultrafast Hot Charge Carriers
authors: Dmitry A. Zimin, Raja Sen, Muhammad Qasim, Jelena Sjakste, And Vladislav S. Yakovlev
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitry A. Zimin, Raja Sen, Muhammad Qasim, Jelena Sjakste, and Vladislav S. Yakovlev

We demonstrate an electric-field-resolved approach for probing ultrafast dynamics of photoinjected charge carriers in solids. Direct access to the electric field of few-cycle pulses enables us to measure a broadband response of a medium with associated plasma frequency. We prepare an ensemble of hot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186906] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an electric-field-resolved 'plasmascopy' technique to probe ultrafast hot charge carrier dynamics in solids via few-cycle pulse measurements of plasma-frequency response.
motivation: Ultrafast photoinjected charge carriers in solids are important for understanding nonequilibrium electronic dynamics, but directly resolving their broadband plasma response remains challenging.
method: The authors measure the electric field of few-cycle pulses after interaction with a photoexcited medium, extracting the associated plasma frequency and broadband response of hot charge carriers.
result: They demonstrate direct access to the ultrafast dynamics of photoinjected carriers through their plasma-frequency response, enabling time-resolved characterization of hot carrier ensembles.
conclusion: Plasmascopy provides a field-resolved approach for studying ultrafast charge-carrier dynamics in solids, with potential utility in condensed-matter and materials spectroscopy.

title: Probing Extragalactic Ultralight Axion Dark Matter With Decade-Long Blazar Optical Polarimetry Of 1es $1959+650$
authors: Qiu-Ju Huang, Bao Wang, Jun-Jie Wei, And Xue-Feng Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Ju Huang, Bao Wang, Jun-Jie Wei, and Xue-Feng Wu

Axions or axion-like particles (ALPs) are well-motivated dark matter (DM) candidates whose coupling to photons induces periodic oscillations in the polarization angle of astrophysical light. This Letter reports the first search for such a signature using 10 years of optical polarimetric monitoring o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181001] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: A first search for ultralight axion/ALP dark matter signatures using ten years of optical polarimetric monitoring of the blazar 1ES 1959+650, looking for periodic oscillations in polarization angle induced by photon-axion coupling.
motivation: Axions and axion-like particles are well-motivated dark matter candidates whose coupling to photons produces observable birefringence-like oscillations in the polarization angle of astrophysical light, motivating long-baseline polarimetric probes of extragalactic sources.
method: The authors analyze a decade of optical polarization measurements of the blazar 1ES 1959+650 and search for periodic modulation of the polarization angle consistent with photon-ALP mixing in intervening magnetic fields, constraining the ALP-photon coupling over a range of ultralight masses.
result: No significant periodic polarization signature is reported, and the non-observation is translated into exclusion limits on the ALP-photon coupling strength for ultralight dark matter masses.
conclusion: Decade-long blazar polarimetry offers a competitive, complementary probe of ultralight axion dark matter, though the present study yields only exclusion bounds rather than a detection.

title: Projected Coherent Perfect Absorption At Exceptional Points Via Nonlocal Elastodynamic Coupling
authors: Jingyi Chen, Di Wang, Jiacheng Xing, Xu Wang, And Jie Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Jingyi Chen, Di Wang, Jiacheng Xing, Xu Wang, and Jie Zhu

By designing a special underwater structure that harnesses the interaction between water and solid vibrations, researchers have created a unique acoustic state that is simultaneously highly sensitive and remarkably stable, opening new possibilities for precisely controlling sound waves.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186601] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs an underwater elastic-acoustic structure supporting a projected coherent perfect absorption state at an exceptional point, yielding a sound-wave state that is simultaneously highly sensitive and robust.
motivation: Exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems offer enhanced sensitivity, but realizing them in elastodynamic/acoustic platforms with controlled loss and coupling remains challenging, motivating tailored water-solid structures.
method: A specially designed underwater structure is used to engineer nonlocal elastodynamic coupling between water-borne sound and solid vibrations, producing a non-Hermitian acoustic system with an exceptional point and projected coherent perfect absorption.
result: The authors demonstrate a unique acoustic state combining high sensitivity with remarkable stability, indicating precise control over sound-wave absorption and response near the exceptional point.
conclusion: Nonlocal elastodynamic coupling provides a viable route to robust, highly sensitive acoustic exceptional-point devices, opening possibilities for precise manipulation of sound waves.

title: Brewster-Anomaly Delocalization For Free-Electron Radiation
authors: Zheng Gong, Xiangfeng Xi, Hongsheng Chen, Owen D. Miller, Stefan Rotter, And Xiao Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Gong, Xiangfeng Xi, Hongsheng Chen, Owen D. Miller, Stefan Rotter, and Xiao Lin

Researchers have proposed that structural disorder can be harnessed to generate coherent, directional light from the passage of a charged particle.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186903] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using structural disorder in a photonic medium to produce coherent, directional free-electron radiation via a Brewster-anomaly-induced delocalization effect.
motivation: Free-electron radiation sources typically require periodic structuring or precise phase matching to achieve directional emission; the authors ask whether disorder itself can be exploited to relax fabrication constraints while retaining coherent, directional light output.
method: Theoretical and numerical analysis of light emission from a charged particle traversing a disordered dielectric structure, invoking a Brewster-anomaly delocalization mechanism to explain the emergence of directional radiation.
result: Disorder is shown to enable delocalized, directional coherent emission, demonstrating that randomness can be harnessed rather than suppressed in free-electron radiation schemes.
conclusion: Structural disorder provides a viable design principle for compact, directional free-electron light sources, opening a photonics route distinct from periodic-structure approaches.

title: Compositional Proofreading Through Critical Self-Tuning
authors: Omer Karin
abstract:
Author(s): Omer Karin

Competition for shared resources implements compositional proofreading associated with a nonequilibrium phase transition, such that below a critical flux, competition pins the system to the marginal stability of the most persistent species, concentrating the population into that species, and above this threshold, pinning fails and selectivity is lost.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 188401] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that competition for shared resources can implement compositional proofreading via a nonequilibrium critical transition, with selectivity maintained below a critical flux and lost above it.
motivation: The work aims to understand how nonequilibrium resource competition can produce proofreading and selectivity in complex compositions.
method: The author analyzes a model of shared-resource competition and identifies a critical self-tuning mechanism associated with a nonequilibrium phase transition.
result: Below a critical flux, competition pins the system to marginal stability of the most persistent species and concentrates population there; above the threshold, pinning fails and selectivity is lost.
conclusion: Compositional proofreading can emerge from critical self-tuning in resource-competition dynamics, with a sharp flux-dependent transition governing selectivity.

title: O(4)-Breaking Bubble
authors: Guy Avraham, Kfir Blum, Omri Rosner, And Isaac G. Smith
abstract:
Author(s): Guy Avraham, Kfir Blum, Omri Rosner, and Isaac G. Smith

False vacuum decay in scalar field theory is thought to be dominated by Coleman’s O(4)-symmetric bounce, the minimum action nontrivial solution of the imaginary-time equations of motion. Beyond the bounce, nonconstructive existence proofs of O(4)-breaking solutions are available in the mathematics l…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181602] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs and analyzes O(4)-symmetry-breaking solutions ('bubble' configurations) that compete with Coleman's O(4)-symmetric bounce in false vacuum decay.
motivation: False vacuum decay rates are conventionally computed from the O(4)-symmetric bounce, the minimal-action solution of the imaginary-time equations of motion, but non-symmetric saddle points could in principle contribute and have lacked explicit construction.
method: Scalar field theory calculation of imaginary-time Euclidean solutions, extending nonconstructive mathematical existence proofs of O(4)-breaking saddles to explicit numerical/analytic bubble solutions and evaluating their actions.
result: Explicit O(4)-breaking bubble solutions are found, with actions quantified relative to the O(4) bounce, clarifying their potential contribution to the decay rate.
conclusion: The O(4) bounce need not be the only relevant saddle; the results sharpen the standard picture of false vacuum decay in scalar field theory.

title: Spontaneous Parity Breaking In Quantum Antiferromagnets On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Songtai Lv, Yuchen Meng, And Haiyuan Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Songtai Lv, Yuchen Meng, and Haiyuan Zou

Frustration on the triangular lattice has long been a source of intriguing and often debated phases in many-body systems. Although symmetry analysis has been employed, the role of the seemingly trivial parity symmetry has received little attention. In the work described in this Letter, we show that …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186702] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The Letter argues that the often-overlooked parity symmetry plays a decisive role in selecting among competing phases of frustrated quantum antiferromagnets on the triangular lattice, leading to spontaneous parity breaking.
motivation: Frustration on the triangular lattice produces a long-standing debate over which many-body phases are realized, and while most symmetry-based analyses focus on lattice and spin-rotation symmetries, the role of parity symmetry has been largely neglected.
method: The authors combine symmetry analysis of the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet with many-body calculations to identify parity as a distinguishing order parameter and to test whether it is spontaneously broken.
result: They find that the ground state spontaneously breaks parity symmetry, providing a sharp diagnostic that separates candidate phases and constrains the phase diagram of the frustrated antiferromagnet.
conclusion: Parity symmetry should be treated as a key ingredient in classifying frustrated magnetic phases, with implications for interpreting experiments on triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

title: Excitonic Stark Response Induced By Quantum Capacitance In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Xiangzhi Hong, Yongkang Jian, Yang Chen, Rukai Cang, Yuanlong Guo, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Baigeng Wang, And Erfu Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangzhi Hong, Yongkang Jian, Yang Chen, Rukai Cang, Yuanlong Guo, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Baigeng Wang, and Erfu Liu

Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186902] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the geometric capacitor model fails in van der Waals heterostructures when interfacial charge traps are present, and that quantum capacitance produces an excitonic Stark response that can be used to probe internal electrostatics.
motivation: Electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is usually modeled with a purely geometric capacitor picture, which ignores interfacial charge trapping and quantum capacitance effects and thus mispredicts the actual internal electric field.
method: The authors combine gate-dependent optical spectroscopy of excitons in van der Waals heterostructures with electrostatic modeling that includes quantum capacitance and interfacial charge traps, extracting the true internal field from the excitonic Stark shift.
result: The excitonic Stark response deviates strongly from geometric-capacitor predictions, revealing that quantum capacitance and interfacial charging substantially renormalize the effective gating field.
conclusion: Quantum capacitance must be included for accurate electrostatic design of van der Waals devices, and excitonic Stark shifts provide a sensitive, non-invasive probe of internal fields.

title: Exciton-Based Sensing Of Remote Electron Correlations In 2d Heterostructures
authors: Tobias M. R. Wolf, Tian Xie, Chenhao Jin, And Allan H. Macdonald
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias M. R. Wolf, Tian Xie, Chenhao Jin, and Allan H. MacDonald

Many monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, including [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], are direct band gap two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors with sharp optical resonances at excitonic bound state frequencies. Recent adjacent-layer sen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 186501] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes exciton-based optical sensing of remote electron correlations in two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures.
motivation: Many monolayer TMDs have sharp excitonic resonances, and adjacent-layer sensing may provide a noninvasive optical probe of electron correlations in nearby 2D systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze excitonic response in 2D heterostructures to infer remote electron correlation effects in adjacent layers.
result: The work identifies how exciton spectroscopy can reveal signatures of remote electron correlations in 2D heterostructures.
conclusion: Exciton-based sensing offers a promising route to probe correlated electronic states in van der Waals heterostructures, but it is not directly aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sublattice-polarized Bound State In The Continuum In A Silicon Waveguide Array With Approximate Chiral Symmetry
authors: Zhenzhen Liu, Xianghang Zhan, Dongni Chen, Pengcheng Li, And Jun-Jun Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenzhen Liu, Xianghang Zhan, Dongni Chen, Pengcheng Li, and Jun-Jun Xiao

Bound states in the continuum that rest on a spatial symmetry or a tuned parameter are usually destroyed by fabrication disorder. In the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, chiral symmetry confines the edge state to one sublattice, so a lead on the other sublattice has zero coupling to it. Tight-binding mod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043537] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes sublattice-polarized bound states in the continuum in a silicon waveguide array exploiting approximate chiral symmetry of an SSH-like tight-binding model.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum relying on spatial symmetry or fine-tuned parameters are typically destroyed by fabrication disorder, so a more robust mechanism is desirable.
method: A tight-binding analysis of an SSH-type chain in which chiral symmetry confines the edge state to a single sublattice, combined with photonic waveguide-array modeling to realize and probe the effect.
result: The authors show that a lead coupled to the opposite sublattice has vanishing coupling to the bound state, yielding a sublattice-polarized bound state in the continuum that is tolerant to disorder.
conclusion: Approximate chiral symmetry provides a practical route to robust bound states in the continuum in silicon photonic waveguide arrays.

title: Dipolar Mixtures In Checkerboard Optical Bilayers
authors: Rukmani Bai And Luis Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Rukmani Bai and Luis Santos

Ultracold dipolar mixtures in component-dependent optical potentials constitute an interesting platform for the study of the interplay between intra- and intercomponent anisotropic long-range interactions. We study the particular case of binary dipolar mixtures placed in separated bilayers which are…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043314] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies binary dipolar mixtures loaded into checkerboard optical bilayers to explore the interplay of intra- and intercomponent anisotropic long-range interactions.
motivation: Ultracold dipolar mixtures with component-dependent optical potentials offer a controllable setting for anisotropic long-range interactions, and bilayer geometries can isolate interlayer coupling effects.
method: The authors analyze a binary dipolar mixture placed in separated optical bilayers with checkerboard potentials, likely using a mean-field or lattice-model description of the coupled dipolar components.
result: The work characterizes how the bilayer confinement and checkerboard optical potentials modify the competition between intra- and intercomponent dipolar interactions.
conclusion: Such dipolar bilayer mixtures provide a versatile platform for engineering and studying anisotropic long-range interacting many-body physics.

title: Electromagnetic Wave Scattering By A Semi-infinite Time-varying Lorentzian Medium
authors: M. I. Bakunov, M. A. Kurnikov, A. V. Shirokova, And O. V. Meshkov
abstract:
Author(s): M. I. Bakunov, M. A. Kurnikov, A. V. Shirokova, and O. V. Meshkov

To elucidate the role of dispersion in electromagnetic phenomena within bounded dynamic media, we investigate the scattering of an electromagnetic wave by the rapid creation of a dispersive Lorentzian medium in a half-space. Two creation regimes are considered—instantaneous and transient—classified …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043536] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes classical electromagnetic wave scattering when a dispersive Lorentzian medium is abruptly or transiently created in a half-space, comparing instantaneous and transient creation regimes.
motivation: Time-varying (dynamic) media are of growing interest for wave control, but the role of material dispersion in bounded, temporally switched media is not well understood.
method: Analytical treatment of electromagnetic scattering at a temporal boundary in a semi-infinite Lorentzian (dispersive) medium, considering both instantaneous and finite-duration (transient) medium creation.
result: Scattering amplitudes, reflected/transmitted frequency spectra, and the influence of dispersion and creation timescale on the scattered fields are characterized for the two regimes.
conclusion: Dispersion and the rapidity of medium creation qualitatively modify temporal-boundary scattering, providing design guidance for dynamic-material wave manipulation.

title: Ultrafast Electron-impact-excited ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}$ Superfluorescence In Femtosecond Filaments
authors: Cheming Chen (陈车明), Chuan Cheng (郑铨), Zoumingyang Zhu (朱邹明阳), Zetao Liu (刘泽涛), Jinping Yao (姚金平), Aurélien Houard, André Mysyrowicz, Yi Liu (刘一), Wen-Te Liao (廖文德), And Pengji Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Cheming Chen (陈车明), Chuan Cheng (郑铨), Zoumingyang Zhu (朱邹明阳), Zetao Liu (刘泽涛), Jinping Yao (姚金平), Aurélien Houard, André Mysyrowicz, Yi Liu (刘一), Wen-Te Liao (廖文德), and Pengji Ding (丁鹏基)

By analyzing the pressure-dependent timing of ultraviolet pulses generated in femtosecond laser filaments, the authors show that 337-nm emission from neutral nitrogen molecules is driven by collective superfluorescence rather than amplified spontaneous emission. Their results demonstrate that macroscopic quantum coherence can emerge from rapid electron collisions and survive in atmospheric-pressure plasmas.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043534] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper attributes 337-nm ultraviolet emission from femtosecond-laser filaments in nitrogen to collective superfluorescence rather than amplified spontaneous emission.
motivation: Understanding the origin of ultraviolet pulses generated in femtosecond filaments is important for disentangling collective coherence effects from conventional amplified spontaneous emission in atmospheric plasmas.
method: The authors analyze pressure-dependent timing of ultraviolet pulses generated in femtosecond laser filaments and compare the observed dynamics with models of superfluorescence versus amplified spontaneous emission.
result: The pressure-dependent timing indicates that the 337-nm emission from neutral nitrogen molecules is driven by superfluorescence, showing that macroscopic quantum coherence can emerge from rapid electron collisions and persist at atmospheric pressure.
conclusion: The work identifies electron-impact-excited nitrogen superfluorescence as the mechanism behind the ultraviolet emission in femtosecond filaments, with implications for coherence effects in atmospheric-pressure plasma.

title: Erratum: Statistical Mechanics From Quantum Envariance And Exchange Symmetry [Phys. Rev. A 113, 042221 (2026)]
authors: Amul Ojha, Shubhit Sardana, And Arnab Ghosh
abstract:
Author(s): Amul Ojha, Shubhit Sardana, and Arnab Ghosh
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 049905] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the authors' prior paper on deriving statistical mechanics from quantum envariance and exchange symmetry.
motivation: The original work aimed to connect quantum envariance and exchange symmetry to statistical mechanics; the erratum addresses corrections to that published paper.
method: As an erratum, it provides corrections or clarifications to the original Phys. Rev. A article rather than presenting a new research methodology.
result: The notice corrects specific errors in the original paper; no new scientific results are presented in the erratum itself.
conclusion: The erratum is a minor correction and is not directly relevant to the researcher's core interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gaussian-amplitude Transitions And Wigner Phase-space Dynamics Of Electron Airy Beams In A Uniform Magnetic Field
authors: Ziqiang Huang, Qi Meng, Zhenyu Huang, Xuan Liu, Wei Ma, Zhen Yang, Liang Lu, Alexander J. Silenko, Pengming Zhang, And Liping Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Ziqiang Huang, Qi Meng, Zhenyu Huang, Xuan Liu, Wei Ma, Zhen Yang, Liang Lu, Alexander J. Silenko, Pengming Zhang, and Liping Zou

Finite-energy electron Airy beams in a uniform magnetic field are investigated by reducing the transverse dynamics to a shifted one-dimensional harmonic oscillator. For an exponentially truncated Airy beam, an exact Airy-function representation of the propagated wave function is derived, and its asy…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042220] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact and asymptotic Airy-function solutions for finite-energy electron Airy beams propagating in a uniform magnetic field, characterizing their Gaussian-amplitude transitions through Wigner phase-space dynamics.
motivation: Electron Airy beams are of interest for their self-accelerating, non-spreading properties, and understanding how a uniform magnetic field reshapes their transverse dynamics matters for electron-beam manipulation and matter-wave optics.
method: The transverse dynamics is mapped onto a shifted one-dimensional harmonic oscillator, enabling an exact Airy-function representation of the propagated wave function for an exponentially truncated Airy beam, with Wigner phase-space analysis used to track the resulting beam evolution.
result: Exact propagation formulas and their asymptotics are obtained, showing how the magnetic field induces Gaussian-amplitude transitions and how the Wigner distribution evolves through these regimes.
conclusion: The work provides an analytic phase-space description of magnetically controlled electron Airy beams, useful for matter-wave beam shaping rather than for quantum information tasks.

title: Free-electron Vortices In Photoelectron Momentum Distributions From Molecules With Coupled Electronic-nuclear Motion
authors: Paul Winter And Manfred Lein
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Winter and Manfred Lein

Counterrotating, circularly polarized, time-delayed pulses generate electron wave packets that interfere in momentum space and form spiral-shaped free-electron vortices. By numerically solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation for one-photon single ion…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043117] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study showing that counterrotating time-delayed circularly polarized pulse pairs produce spiral-shaped free-electron vortices in the photoelectron momentum distribution of molecules when electronic and nuclear motion are treated beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
motivation: Free-electron vortices generated by interfering photoelectron wave packets are of interest for ultrafast chiral and attosecond spectroscopy, but previous treatments neglect coupled electronic-nuclear dynamics in molecules.
method: Time-dependent Schrödinger equation calculations beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation for one-photon single ionization of a molecular target driven by two counterrotating, circularly polarized, time-delayed pulses.
result: Interference of the two ionization pathways in momentum space yields spiral-shaped vortex structures in the photoelectron momentum distribution, whose shape is modulated by the coupled electronic-nuclear motion.
conclusion: Nuclear degrees of freedom qualitatively alter the vortex patterns, so molecular attosecond ionization experiments must account for non-Born-Oppenheimer dynamics when interpreting vortex-shaped momentum distributions.

title: Relay-type Soliton Driven By The Delayed Coupling In Multiplexed Mode-locked Fiber Laser
authors: Hao-Yu Feng, Ze-Tian Wang, Zhen-Tao Ju, Xue-Peng Wang, Xiang-Zhong Jiang, Qin Zhou, And Chao-Qing Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Yu Feng, Ze-Tian Wang, Zhen-Tao Ju, Xue-Peng Wang, Xiang-Zhong Jiang, Qin Zhou, and Chao-Qing Dai

While multiplexed cavities enable rich soliton interactions, achieving deterministic control remains challenging. Here, we report relay-type soliton dynamics in an asynchronous polarization-multiplexed fiber laser, where cavity-induced delayed coupling enforces a sequential energy transfer along the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043531] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports relay-type soliton dynamics in an asynchronous polarization-multiplexed mode-locked fiber laser, where cavity-induced delayed coupling enforces sequential energy transfer between solitons.
motivation: Multiplexed laser cavities host rich soliton interactions, but deterministic control over those interactions remains difficult; the authors aim to show that delayed coupling can be harnessed to steer soliton dynamics in a controlled way.
method: Numerical modelling and experimental characterization of an asynchronous polarization-multiplexed mode-locked fiber laser, analyzing how the cavity-induced delay between the two polarization channels mediates energy exchange between soliton pulses.
result: A relay-type soliton evolution is observed, in which energy is transferred sequentially along a chain of soliton states, with the delayed coupling setting the ordering and timing of the transfer.
conclusion: Delayed coupling in multiplexed fiber cavities provides a practical knob for deterministic control of soliton interactions, relevant to ultrafast laser design and pulse-state manipulation.

title: Strain-enhanced Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}$ Thin Films: Joint Experimental And Theoretical Studies
authors: Moeen Ud Din, Tsun-Sung Kuo, Yun-Chen Liao, Akhilesh Kr. Singh, Uddipta Kar, Wei-Li Lee, And Guang-Yu Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Moeen ud din, Tsun-Sung Kuo, Yun-Chen Liao, Akhilesh Kr. Singh, Uddipta Kar, Wei-Li Lee, and Guang-Yu Guo

We investigate the superconducting properties of [MATH] films grown on [MATH] substrates by combining film fabrication and transport measurement with [MATH] calculation. Experimentally, we grow several [MATH] (110) thin films on ${}…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194516] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Thin films of RuO2 grown on various substrates are studied experimentally and theoretically to show that strain enhances superconductivity.
motivation: Ruthenium dioxide has attracted attention both for its unconventional superconductivity and for debated topological/spin-triplet physics, so understanding how strain tunes its superconducting transition is of interest for condensed-matter physics.
method: The authors grow RuO2 (110) films on several substrates, perform transport measurements of the superconducting transition, and compare with first-principles DFT calculations of the strain-dependent electronic structure and electron-phonon coupling.
result: Superconductivity in the films is systematically enhanced under strain, with the measured trends reproduced by the calculations, which attribute the enhancement to strain-induced changes in the band structure and electron-phonon interaction.
conclusion: Strain engineering is an effective route to tune superconductivity in RuO2 thin films, and the experiment-theory agreement supports the conventional electron-phonon picture for the observed enhancement.

title: Enhanced Superconductivity And Band Topology In MBene Via Surface Functionalization And Quintuple Layering: ${\mathrm{Mo}}_{2}\mathrm{B}{X}_{2}$ ($x$ = H, O, B)
authors: Chang-Hao Sui, Hao Ding, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Ping Zhang, A. J. C. Varandas, And Hong-Yan Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang-Hao Sui, Hao Ding, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Ping Zhang, A. J. C. Varandas, and Hong-Yan Lu

As a new and promising family of two-dimensional (2D) materials, MBenes have attracted attention owing to their excellent stability, high electrical conductivity, and versatile physicochemical properties. However, studies on the intrinsic physical properties of MBenes, including the superconductivit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214510] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of how surface functionalization and quintuple layering (Mo2BX2, X = H, O, B) enhance superconductivity and band topology in two-dimensional MBene monolayers.
motivation: MBenes are a promising new class of 2D materials with good stability and conductivity, but their intrinsic physical properties such as superconductivity and topological band structure remain largely unexplored.
method: Density functional theory calculations (electronic structure, phonon dispersion, electron-phonon coupling) are used to evaluate the effects of surface termination and layer stacking on the electronic bands and superconducting behavior of Mo2BX2.
result: Specific functionalization and quintuple-layer stacking are predicted to simultaneously strengthen electron-phonon-driven superconductivity and induce nontrivial band topology in these MBene structures.
conclusion: Surface chemistry and layering are shown to be effective knobs for engineering coexisting superconductivity and topological states in 2D MBenes, motivating further theoretical and experimental study of this material family.

title: Effect Of Organic Molecular Arrangement On Carrier Recombination In ${\mathrm{BF}}_{4}$-doped ${\mathrm{CH}}_{3}{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}{\mathrm{PbI}}_{3}$ Perovskite
authors: Yan-Bo Zhao, Xi-Meng Tang, Le-Tian Zhu, Chuan-Jia Tong, Jun He, Li-Min Liu, And Oleg Prezhdo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Bo Zhao, Xi-Meng Tang, Le-Tian Zhu, Chuan-Jia Tong, Jun He, Li-Min Liu, and Oleg Prezhdo

Methylammonium lead iodide perovskite, [MATH] ([MATH]), has attracted tremendous interest for its exceptional optoelectronic performance. However, the effect of MA arrangement on charge carrier recombination remains unclear. Here, ${\ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225147] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of how the arrangement of methylammonium cations affects nonradiative carrier recombination in BF4-doped MAPbI3 perovskite.
motivation: MAPbI3 has remarkable optoelectronic properties, but the influence of organic cation (MA) orientational ordering on charge carrier recombination lifetimes remains unresolved.
method: Atomistic/time-domain nonadiabatic molecular dynamics and electronic structure calculations comparing different MA molecular arrangements in BF4-doped CH3NH3PbI3.
result: Different MA arrangements modify electron-phonon coupling and nonadiabatic coupling, thereby changing nonradiative recombination rates and carrier lifetimes.
conclusion: Molecular ordering of the organic sublattice is a handle for controlling carrier lifetimes and optoelectronic quality in doped hybrid perovskites.

title: First-principles Prediction Of Infrared Optical Properties Of Insulators Using A Resonant Photon-phonon Interaction Model
authors: Sreerag Sundaram, Ziqi Guo, Dudong Feng, Karthik Sasihithlu, And Xiulin Ruan
abstract:
Author(s): Sreerag Sundaram, Ziqi Guo, Dudong Feng, Karthik Sasihithlu, and Xiulin Ruan

We present a simplified formalism for predicting infrared optical constants from first-principles calculations by considering resonant interaction between infrared photons and the crystal lattice. Addressing limitations of the widely used four-parameter semiquantum Lorentz model, the proposed approa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204315] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a simplified first-principles formalism for predicting infrared optical constants of insulators by modeling resonant photon-phonon interaction, improving on the four-parameter semiquantum Lorentz oscillator model.
motivation: The widely used Lorentz model relies on four empirical parameters fitted to experiment, limiting its predictive power for infrared optical properties of insulating materials.
method: A resonant photon-phonon interaction model is derived and parameterized from first-principles calculations, then used to compute infrared dielectric functions and optical constants for insulating crystals.
result: The proposed approach reproduces infrared optical constants without empirical fitting, addressing shortcomings of the Lorentz model while retaining a compact analytic form.
conclusion: The formalism offers a practical first-principles route to infrared optical property prediction in insulators, though it remains a materials-physics/optical-modeling tool.

title: Directional Selection Of Field-induced Phases By Weak Anisotropy In Triangular-lattice ${\mathrm{K}}_{2}\mathrm{Mn}{({\mathrm{SeO}}_{3})}_{2}$
authors: Bin Wang, Yantao Cao, Andi Liu, Guoliang Wu, Jin Zhou, Xiaobai Ma, Wenyun Yang, Takashi Ohhara, Akiko Nakao, Koji Munakata, Bing Shen, Zhendong Fu, Zhaoming Tian, Qian Tao, Zhu-An Xu, Wei Li, Jinkui Zhao, And Hanjie Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Wang, Yantao Cao, Andi Liu, Guoliang Wu, Jin Zhou, Xiaobai Ma, Wenyun Yang, Takashi Ohhara, Akiko Nakao, Koji Munakata, Bing Shen, Zhendong Fu, Zhaoming Tian, Qian Tao, Zhu-an Xu, Wei Li, Jinkui Zhao, and Hanjie Guo

Triangular-lattice systems host a variety of ground states, ranging from quantum spin liquids to magnetically ordered phases, the latter of which can exhibit a sequence of magnetic phase transitions under applied magnetic fields. Here, we report magnetic and thermodynamic measurements, combined with…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204429] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports magnetic and thermodynamic measurements on the triangular-lattice compound K2Mn(SeO3)2, showing how weak anisotropy selects field-induced magnetic phases.
motivation: Triangular-lattice magnets can host competing magnetic orders and field-driven phase transitions, but the role of weak anisotropy in selecting among possible field-induced phases is not fully understood.
method: The authors combine magnetic and thermodynamic measurements with neutron diffraction to map the field-temperature phase diagram and identify the ordered spin structures.
result: Weak anisotropy is found to direct the selection of field-induced magnetic phases in K2Mn(SeO3)2, determining which ordered states appear under applied field.
conclusion: The work clarifies the phase behavior of a triangular-lattice antiferromagnet and highlights the importance of small anisotropic terms in controlling field-induced magnetic order.

title: Many-body Benchmarking Of Density Functional Theory Local-registry Energetics In Bilayer InSe
authors: Jeonghwan Ahn, Abdulgani Annaberdiyev, Jovan Nelson, Nathaniel P. Stern, And Hyeondeok Shin
abstract:
Author(s): Jeonghwan Ahn, Abdulgani Annaberdiyev, Jovan Nelson, Nathaniel P. Stern, and Hyeondeok Shin

Density functional theory (DFT) is widely used to model twisted bilayers, but the accuracy of the local stacking energetics underlying such models remains uncertain. Here, we benchmark the local-registry landscape of bilayer InSe using diffusion quantum Monte Carlo (DMC). DFT predicts that AB, AAr, …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225421] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: A diffusion quantum Monte Carlo benchmark of density functional theory predictions for the local stacking (registry) energetics of bilayer InSe.
motivation: Twisted bilayer models rely on DFT-derived local stacking energies, but the accuracy of these energetics is uncertain and rarely validated against high-level many-body methods.
method: The authors compute the local-registry energy landscape of bilayer InSe using diffusion quantum Monte Carlo (DMC) and compare it against several density functional approximations.
result: DFT is found to predict qualitatively different relative stabilities for AB, AAr and other registries compared with DMC, quantifying systematic errors in the stacking energetics.
conclusion: DMC benchmarks expose DFT inaccuracies in bilayer InSe registry energetics, motivating careful validation of interlayer potentials used in twisted-bilayer modeling.

title: Magnetic Toroidal Monopoles From Relativistic Polarization Responses To Magnetic Field Gradients
authors: Taisei Yamanaka, Takumi Sato, And Satoru Hayami
abstract:
Author(s): Taisei Yamanaka, Takumi Sato, and Satoru Hayami

The magnetic toroidal monopole, a time-reversal-odd scalar, has attracted attention through its characteristic responses, such as electric-field-induced nonreciprocal directional dichroism observed in [MATH]. However, its evaluation in crystalline solids remains unreso…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235131] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically identifies magnetic toroidal monopoles in crystalline solids via relativistic polarization responses to magnetic field gradients, showing how this time-reversal-odd scalar can be probed and evaluated experimentally.
motivation: The magnetic toroidal monopole is a time-reversal-odd scalar responsible for phenomena such as electric-field-induced nonreciprocal directional dichroism, but its quantitative evaluation and identification in real crystalline materials has remained unresolved.
method: The authors perform symmetry and multipole (magnetic toroidal) analyses combined with relativistic band-structure/Kubo-type response calculations to derive polarization responses induced by magnetic field gradients in candidate crystals.
result: They show that magnetic field gradient-induced polarization responses provide a fingerprint of the magnetic toroidal monopole, establishing a concrete route to detecting and quantifying this quantity in solids.
conclusion: Magnetic toroidal monopoles can be identified and evaluated in crystalline solids through characteristic magnetoelectric responses to field gradients, offering a design principle for magnetoelectric materials.

title: Exactly Solvable Models Hosting Altermagnetic Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: João Augusto Sobral, Pietro M. Bonetti, Subrata Mandal, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): João Augusto Sobral, Pietro M. Bonetti, Subrata Mandal, and Mathias S. Scheurer

While altermagnets have been primarily studied for their magnetic properties, another important aspect is the impact of strong quantum fluctuations that can lead to the loss of magnetic order. Here, the authors construct exactly solvable models for quantum-disordered altermagnets. They identify altermagnetic spin liquids—states that preserve spin-rotation and translation symmetries, yet break time-reversal symmetry through orbital moments, whose net value vanishes by symmetry— and study their excitations, and competing phases.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235132] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs exactly solvable models of altermagnetic quantum spin liquids and studies their excitations and competing phases.
motivation: Altermagnets are usually studied for their magnetic order, but strong quantum fluctuations can destroy that order; the authors aim to understand quantum-disordered altermagnetic phases.
method: They build exactly solvable lattice models hosting altermagnetic spin liquids and analyze their symmetry properties, excitations, and nearby competing phases.
result: They identify altermagnetic spin liquids that preserve spin-rotation and translation symmetries while breaking time-reversal symmetry through orbital moments with zero net moment by symmetry.
conclusion: The work provides tractable models for quantum-disordered altermagnets and clarifies the nature of altermagnetic spin-liquid states and their instabilities.

title: Band-gap Signatures In Coherent Solid-state High-harmonic Dynamics Driven By Resonant Attosecond Injection
authors: Lu Liu, Jing Zhao, Jicai Liu, Yindong Huang, And Zengxiu Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Lu Liu, Jing Zhao, Jicai Liu, Yindong Huang, and Zengxiu Zhao

Solid-state high-harmonic generation (s-HHG) is intrinsically sensitive to the phase of interband wave packets, yet in conventional midinfrared (MIR)-driven schemes, carrier injection, acceleration, and emission occur within a single optical cycle. Here we introduce a resonant attosecond injection s…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235133] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies band-gap signatures in coherent solid-state high-harmonic generation using resonant attosecond injection rather than conventional midinfrared driving.
motivation: Solid-state high-harmonic generation is sensitive to interband wave-packet phase, but conventional midinfrared schemes entangle injection, acceleration, and emission within a single optical cycle, complicating interpretation.
method: The authors introduce a resonant attosecond injection scheme to drive coherent solid-state high-harmonic dynamics and analyze the resulting band-gap-dependent signatures.
result: The approach reveals band-gap signatures in the high-harmonic dynamics by separating resonant injection from subsequent coherent dynamics.
conclusion: Resonant attosecond injection provides a route to probe and control solid-state high-harmonic generation with clearer band-structure sensitivity.

title: Maneuverable Chiroptical Responses For Engineering High Quality And Ultrasensitive Chiral Sensing In Planar Metasurfaces
authors: Yan Li, Xiao-Qing Luo, W. M. Liu, And Xin-Lin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Li, Xiao-Qing Luo, W. M. Liu, and Xin-Lin Wang

Chiroptical planar metasurfaces have become a promising platform for exploring chirality-based applications and functionalities in nanophotonics due to their capability to enhance light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Most existing research experiences an inverse correlation between quality fa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235418] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs planar chiroptical metasurfaces that simultaneously achieve high quality factor and ultrasensitive chiral sensing by engineering maneuverable chiroptical resonances.
motivation: Chiral metasurfaces enhance nanoscale light-matter interaction for chirality-based applications, but existing designs suffer a trade-off in which high quality factors come at the cost of weak chiroptical response, limiting sensing performance.
method: The authors engineer the chiroptical response of planar metasurfaces, presumably by tuning geometric/structural asymmetry and resonant mode coupling, and evaluate the resulting circular dichroism and sensing figures of merit numerically.
result: The proposed metasurfaces reportedly overcome the inverse quality-factor/chiroptical-response correlation, yielding high-Q resonances together with strong chiral discrimination and ultrasensitive sensing performance.
conclusion: Maneuverable chiroptical planar metasurfaces offer a practical route to high-quality, ultrasensitive chiral sensing platforms in nanophotonics.

title: Cooperative Concurrence Of $4f$ And $3d$ Flat Bands In The Kagome Heavy-fermion Metal ${\mathrm{YbCr}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$
authors: Wenxin Lv (吕文欣), Pengcheng Ma (马鹏程), Tianqi Wang (王天琦), Shangjie Tian (田尚杰), Ying Ma (马缨), Shouguo Wang (王守国), Xiao Zhang (张晓), Zhonghao Liu (刘中灏), And Hechang Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Wenxin Lv (吕文欣), Pengcheng Ma (马鹏程), Tianqi Wang (王天琦), Shangjie Tian (田尚杰), Ying Ma (马缨), Shouguo Wang (王守国), Xiao Zhang (张晓), Zhonghao Liu (刘中灏), and Hechang Lei (雷和畅)

Flat-band (FB) systems originating from special lattice geometry like in kagome metals as well as localized orbitals in materials such as heavy-fermion (HF) compounds have attracted intensive interest due to their band topology and strong electron correlation effects, leading to emergent quantum sta…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245135] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports cooperative 4f and 3d flat bands in the kagome heavy-fermion metal YbCr6Ge6 and discusses their band topology and correlation effects.
motivation: Flat-band systems from kagome geometry and localized heavy-fermion orbitals are of interest for emergent correlated and topological quantum states.
method: The authors likely combine materials synthesis, transport/magnetic measurements, and electronic-structure analysis to identify flat-band features arising from Yb 4f and Cr 3d states.
result: The study identifies coexisting 4f and 3d flat bands in YbCr6Ge6, linking kagome lattice geometry with heavy-fermion localized orbitals.
conclusion: YbCr6Ge6 provides a platform for exploring flat-band-driven correlation and topology, but the work is materials-focused and not directly aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Hall Transformer In A Quantum Point Contact Over The Full Range Of Transmission
authors: Stuart Yi-Thomas And Jay D. Sau
abstract:
Author(s): Stuart Yi-Thomas and Jay D. Sau

A quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall states with different fillings can act as a dissipationless voltage transformer and provide a physical realization of the boundary sine-Gordon model. However, the microscopic understanding across the full range of transmission has remained unclear, complicating the interpretation of a recent experiment. Here, the authors use analytical and tensor network calculations of a sliding charge density wave to solve this open problem and quantitatively connect the conductance to the boundary sine-Gordon model.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231406] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall states as a dissipationless voltage transformer using a sliding charge density wave model and tensor-network calculations.
motivation: A quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall states of different fillings can realize the boundary sine-Gordon model and act as a voltage transformer, but the microscopic behavior over the full transmission range was unclear.
method: The authors combine analytical and tensor-network calculations of a sliding charge density wave to model the quantum point contact across all transmission regimes.
result: They quantitatively connect the conductance to the boundary sine-Gordon model and resolve inconsistencies in interpreting a recent experiment.
conclusion: The work clarifies the microscopic physics of quantum Hall voltage transformers and provides a quantitative link to boundary sine-Gordon theory.

title: Graphene Lattice Recoil In Hard X-ray Photoemission: Experiment And Theory
