authors: Simone Ritarossi, Alice Apponi, Orlando Castellano, José Lorenzana, Domenica Convertino, Camilla Coletti, Tien-Lin Lee, Francesco Offi, And Alessandro Ruocco
abstract:
Author(s): Simone Ritarossi, Alice Apponi, Orlando Castellano, José Lorenzana, Domenica Convertino, Camilla Coletti, Tien-Lin Lee, Francesco Offi, and Alessandro Ruocco

Hard-x-ray C [MATH] photoemission from monolayer graphene probes a regime in which nuclear recoil and intrinsic electronic asymmetry contribute on comparable energy scales to the observed spectral line shape. Here we combine experiment and modeling over the photon-energy range $0.8–8\phantom{\rule{0.2…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194307] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Hard X-ray C 1s photoemission from monolayer graphene is studied experimentally and theoretically to disentangle nuclear recoil effects from intrinsic electronic asymmetry in the spectral line shape.
motivation: In hard X-ray photoemission, nuclear recoil and intrinsic electronic asymmetry contribute on comparable energy scales, making line-shape interpretation ambiguous for light elements in graphene.
method: Angle-resolved hard X-ray photoemission measurements on monolayer graphene over photon energies of 0.8–8 keV are combined with modeling of recoil and electronic asymmetry contributions to the C 1s line shape.
result: The recoil-induced and electronic-asymmetry contributions are quantified and shown to be separable across the photon-energy range, reproducing the observed spectral line shapes.
conclusion: Nuclear recoil must be accounted for in hard X-ray photoemission of graphene, and the combined experiment-theory framework provides a basis for interpreting core-level spectra of 2D materials.

title: Superconductivity In Pressure-stabilized Hexagonal ${\mathrm{Na}}_{2}{\mathrm{HeB}}_{2}$ With Na-He Co-intercalation And A Honeycomb Boron Network
authors: Hang Xie, Yingnan Liu, Jianjun Zhang, Xin Zhong, Hanyu Liu, And Shoutao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xie, Yingnan Liu, Jianjun Zhang, Xin Zhong, Hanyu Liu, and Shoutao Zhang

Materials containing unreactive elements are attracting increasing attention for their unexpected characteristics such as pressure-driven superconductivity. However, the known helium-incorporating superconductors (HISCs) are constrained by extreme compression, and thus achieving high-temperature sup…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194515] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: First-principles prediction of a pressure-stabilized hexagonal Na2HeB2 compound with Na–He co-intercalation and a honeycomb boron network that becomes a high-temperature superconductor.
motivation: Known helium-incorporating superconductors require extreme compression; the authors seek a helium-based superconductor that can reach high critical temperatures under more accessible or differently stabilized conditions.
method: Structure prediction and density functional theory calculations (enthalpy convex hull, phonon dispersion, electron-phonon coupling, Eliashberg theory) are used to identify and characterize the Na2HeB2 phase.
result: A stable hexagonal Na2HeB2 structure with a honeycomb boron sublattice is predicted to be dynamically stable and superconducting, with an estimated Tc driven by boron-derived electronic states and strong electron-phonon coupling.
conclusion: Na–He co-intercalation offers a route to designing helium-containing high-temperature superconductors, extending the family of pressure-stabilized superconducting materials.

title: Unconventional Magnetism In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{Ca}}_{3}{\mathrm{CoSb}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{9}$
authors: Sanjay Kumar, Rashi Nathawat, Arvind Kumar Yogi, And Satyapal S. Rathore
abstract:
Author(s): Sanjay Kumar, Rashi Nathawat, Arvind Kumar Yogi, and Satyapal S. Rathore

Motivated by intriguing properties of geometrically frustrated systems, in the present work, another member of the triple perovskite family, [MATH], with a [MATH] triangular motif, has been synthesized, and its structural, magnetic, and the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204428] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Synthesis and structural/magnetic characterization of the triple perovskite Ca3CoSb2O9, a triangular-lattice antiferromagnet exhibiting unconventional magnetism driven by geometric frustration.
motivation: Geometrically frustrated magnets are of interest because they can host exotic magnetic ground states and unusual spin dynamics that evade conventional ordering.
method: The compound was synthesized and its crystal structure, magnetic susceptibility, and related properties were measured experimentally, with the triangular Co2+ motif analyzed in the context of frustration.
result: The measurements reveal unconventional magnetic behavior attributed to the frustrated triangular lattice of the CoSb2O9 layers, deviating from simple Néel-type ordering.
conclusion: Ca3CoSb2O9 expands the family of frustrated triple perovskites and provides a new platform for studying frustration-induced magnetism in two-dimensional triangular lattices.

title: High Resolution Study Of The Two-dimensional Axial Next-nearest-neighbor Ising Model Using A Two-replica Cluster Algorithm And Population Annealing
authors: Shane Keiser And Jonathan Machta
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Keiser and Jonathan Machta

The axial next-nearest-neighbor Ising model in two dimensions is studied using population annealing combined with a two-replica cluster algorithm. We are able to fully resolve the sequence of sharp specific heat peaks that characterize the finite-size incommensurate floating phase. We also show that…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044140] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses population annealing with a two-replica cluster algorithm to study the finite-size incommensurate floating phase of the two-dimensional axial next-nearest-neighbor Ising model.
motivation: The ANNNI model exhibits rich modulated phases, and resolving the sharp specific-heat peaks of the floating phase requires advanced simulation methods.
method: The authors combine population annealing with a two-replica cluster algorithm to simulate the 2D ANNNI model at high resolution.
result: They fully resolve the sequence of sharp specific-heat peaks characterizing the finite-size incommensurate floating phase.
conclusion: The combined algorithm provides an effective numerical approach for studying complex phase behavior in frustrated Ising systems.

title: Complex Dynamics In The Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Game
authors: Desmond Chan And Tobias Galla
abstract:
Author(s): Desmond Chan and Tobias Galla

We study the outcome of adaptive learning among many players engaged in sets of two-strategy, two-player games. We are interested in typical games and therefore generate the payoff matrices randomly at the outset. These payoff matrices then remain fixed throughout the learning process. This provides…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044325] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies complex adaptive-learning dynamics in random two-strategy, two-player games with fixed random payoff matrices, framed as a Sherrington-Kirkpatrick game.
motivation: The authors aim to understand typical outcomes when many players learn adaptively in randomly generated games, rather than in carefully designed game structures.
method: They generate payoff matrices randomly at the outset and analyze the resulting learning dynamics for many interacting players using a Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-type disordered-game formulation.
result: The work characterizes the complex dynamical behavior that emerges in these random adaptive-learning settings.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the statistical physics of disordered game-learning systems rather than to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Constrained Surrogates For Arbitrary Families Of Continuous Probability Distributions
authors: Jack Murdoch Moore And Eduardo G. Altmann
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Murdoch Moore and Eduardo G. Altmann

Empirical regularities described by parametrized families of probability distributions can shape how complex systems are interpreted and explained. A recurring problem is to determine the extent to which these descriptions are supported by observations, and how they can be used to characterize the u…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044327] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops constrained surrogate methods for testing and characterizing arbitrary families of continuous probability distributions in complex systems.
motivation: Parametrized distribution families are often used to interpret complex-system regularities, but assessing whether observations support these descriptions and how to characterize the underlying uncertainty remains difficult.
method: The authors propose surrogate-based procedures for arbitrary continuous distribution families, likely generating constrained reference distributions to test empirical regularities.
result: The approach provides a general statistical framework for evaluating the support for fitted distribution families against observations.
conclusion: The work contributes to statistical inference and model validation for empirical probability distributions, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hidden Square Order Through Orientational-domain Reorganization During Nonequilibrium Expansion Of Colloidal Systems
authors: S. W. S. Apolinario
abstract:
Author(s): S. W. S. Apolinario

We investigate the expansion dynamics of two-dimensional colloidal assemblies interacting through a competing potential that supports unconventional local ordering. The systems are initially prepared under logarithmic confinement and subsequently released, generating a nonequilibrium decompression p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045415] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonequilibrium expansion dynamics in two-dimensional colloidal assemblies and reports hidden square order emerging via orientational-domain reorganization.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how unconventional local ordering in colloidal systems evolves under decompression after logarithmic confinement is released.
method: Two-dimensional colloidal assemblies with competing interactions are prepared under logarithmic confinement and then released, producing nonequilibrium decompression that is analyzed for structural and orientational ordering.
result: The expansion dynamics reveal hidden square order that emerges through reorganization of orientational domains rather than simple homogeneous melting or disordering.
conclusion: The work highlights domain reorganization as a mechanism for accessing hidden ordered structures in nonequilibrium colloidal expansion, but it is classical soft-matter physics with no direct quantum information or quantum thermodynamics content.

title: Density-selected Topological Pathways In The Melting Of Single-particle-thick Stripes
authors: José Rafael Bordin
abstract:
Author(s): José Rafael Bordin

The melting of stripe-forming systems involves changes in connectivity that are not fully captured by conventional structural and orientational descriptors. We investigate a two-dimensional model with competing interactions whose low-temperature phase consists of one-particle-thick stripes. Molecula…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045412] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the melting of one-particle-thick stripe phases in a two-dimensional model with competing interactions, emphasizing density-selected topological pathways rather than conventional structural descriptors.
motivation: Stripe-forming systems exhibit melting transitions involving connectivity changes that are not well captured by standard structural or orientational order parameters.
method: The author investigates a two-dimensional model with competing interactions using molecular dynamics simulations and analyzes the melting behavior through topological and density-based descriptors.
result: The low-temperature phase consists of one-particle-thick stripes, and the melting process follows density-selected topological pathways that reveal changes in connectivity beyond conventional structural metrics.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of topological descriptors for understanding melting in stripe-forming systems and suggest that density selection governs the transition pathways.

title: Boundary-driven Anisotropic Coarsening In Conserved Phase Separation
authors: Emilio N. M. Cirillo, Nicklas Jävergård, Adrian Muntean, And Stela Andrea Muntean
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio N. M. Cirillo, Nicklas Jävergård, Adrian Muntean, and Stela Andrea Muntean

Universal scaling in phase separation is typically assumed to be isotropic in systems with conserved dynamics. Here we show that boundary forcing alone can break this dynamical scaling symmetry, leading to anisotropic coarsening, with different effective global growth laws observed parallel and perp…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042111] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Boundary forcing can break the isotropic scaling symmetry of conserved phase separation, producing anisotropic coarsening with direction-dependent growth laws.
motivation: Universal scaling in conserved phase-separation dynamics is usually assumed isotropic, but the authors ask whether boundary effects alone can alter this dynamical symmetry.
method: The paper studies conserved phase separation under boundary driving and analyzes coarsening exponents parallel and perpendicular to the forcing direction.
result: It finds anisotropic coarsening, with different effective global growth laws observed in the parallel and perpendicular directions.
conclusion: Boundary conditions can qualitatively modify universal coarsening behavior in conserved phase-separation systems, invalidating a purely isotropic scaling description.

title: Experimental Investigation Of Lévy Flights For Step-length Distributions With A Length-dependent Local Power Exponent
authors: Isaac C. Nunes, Jesús P. López, And Thierry Passerat de Silans
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac C. Nunes, Jesús P. López, and Thierry Passerat de Silans

Light propagating in a resonant atomic vapor performs a Lévy flight random walk, in which rare long steps dominate the transport. In contrast to the ideal power-law step-length distributions usually assumed in the literature, the actual distribution in atomic vapors is characterized by a local Lévy …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044137] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of Lévy-flight photon transport in a resonant atomic vapor where the step-length distribution has a length-dependent (local) power-law exponent rather than an ideal global power law.
motivation: Ideal power-law step-length distributions are usually assumed when modeling Lévy flights, but real atomic-vapor systems deviate; the authors aim to characterize how a length-dependent local Lévy exponent modifies the transport statistics.
method: Light propagating in a resonant atomic vapor is tracked as a random walk, and the measured step-length statistics are analyzed to extract a local power exponent that varies with step length, comparing experiment with the ideal Lévy-flight prediction.
result: The observed step-length distribution departs from a single power law and instead exhibits a length-dependent local exponent, which alters the relative weight of rare long steps that dominate transport.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of Lévy-flight transport in atomic vapors requires accounting for the local, length-dependent exponent rather than a single power-law parameter.

title: Persistence Properties Of A Phase-ordering System With Competing Dynamics
authors: Shubham Thwal And Suman Majumder
abstract:
Author(s): Shubham Thwal and Suman Majumder

Understanding persistence properties of a system with respect to its underlying microscopic dynamics provides important insights into the associated first-passage behavior. Here, we investigate the persistence properties during phase ordering in the two-dimensional ([MATH]) Ising model evolving under…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044138] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies persistence properties and first-passage behavior during phase ordering in a two-dimensional Ising model with competing dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how microscopic dynamical rules affect persistence and first-passage statistics in a phase-ordering system.
method: They investigate the 2D Ising model evolving under competing dynamics and analyze persistence properties associated with the phase-ordering process.
result: The paper characterizes persistence behavior and relates it to the underlying nonequilibrium microscopic dynamics of the system.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into persistence and first-passage behavior in classical phase-ordering systems with competing dynamical rules.

title: Delay-controlled Heterogeneous Nucleation In Adaptive Dynamical Networks
authors: R. Anand, Jan Fialkowski, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh
abstract:
Author(s): R. Anand, Jan Fialkowski, V. K. Chandrasekar, and R. Suresh

Phase transitions constitute fundamental mechanisms underlying abrupt or qualitative changes in the collective dynamics of interacting units across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. In dynamical networks, such transitions lead to significant reorganization in the coordinated behavior o…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044221] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how time delays control heterogeneous nucleation and phase transitions in adaptive dynamical networks.
motivation: Phase transitions in dynamical networks cause abrupt reorganization of collective behavior, but the mechanisms controlling heterogeneous nucleation in adaptive networks are not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze an adaptive dynamical network model with delayed interactions and identify conditions under which heterogeneous nucleation drives transitions between collective states.
result: Time delay is shown to control the onset and character of heterogeneous nucleation, thereby tuning the network's phase-transition behavior.
conclusion: Delay provides a control parameter for nucleation and collective reorganization in adaptive dynamical networks, with implications for engineered and natural networked systems.

title: Directed Extended-range Percolation
authors: Wenbo Liu, Yiwen Zeng, Xueming Liu, And Ginestra Bianconi
abstract:
Author(s): Wenbo Liu, Yiwen Zeng, Xueming Liu, and Ginestra Bianconi

For standard percolation, directionality is known to increase the complexity of percolation, requiring the distinct statistical treatment of in messages and out messages for determining the percolation order parameters. Here we show that when connectivity is ensured by paths of length [MATH], network…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042301] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies directed extended-range percolation on networks, analyzing how directionality affects connectivity and percolation order parameters.
motivation: Standard percolation with directionality requires separate treatment of incoming and outgoing messages, and the authors aim to extend this framework to extended-range connectivity.
method: The authors develop a statistical message-passing treatment for directed extended-range percolation, distinguishing in- and out-messages to characterize network connectivity and percolation transitions.
result: They show that when connectivity is ensured by paths of certain length, directed extended-range percolation exhibits modified percolation behavior and order parameters compared with standard percolation.
conclusion: Directionality and extended-range paths substantially affect percolation properties, requiring tailored theoretical treatment beyond standard directed percolation.

title: Absorbing Phase Transition In A Queueing Model Of Coupled Adaptive Agents
authors: Alexei Vazquez
abstract:
Author(s): Alexei Vazquez

What decides whether people do things together or separately? Many activities cannot be carried out alone, and an individual must rank them against the private tasks competing for the same time. We address this within the priority-queue description of human activity by letting each agent choose the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044322] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A classical queueing model of adaptive agents exhibits an absorbing phase transition depending on how individuals choose among shared and private tasks.
motivation: The paper asks what determines whether people coordinate on joint activities or perform tasks separately when shared activities must compete with private tasks for limited time.
method: The author extends a priority-queue description of human activity by allowing agents to choose task priorities, and analyzes the resulting collective dynamics for phase-transition behavior.
result: The model displays an absorbing phase transition in the collective activity pattern as a function of the adaptive choice rules and queueing parameters.
conclusion: Coordination versus separate activity can emerge as a collective phase transition in a classical adaptive-agent queueing framework, with implications for modeling human activity patterns.

title: Noise-controlled Phase Transitions And Memory-state Switching In Connectome-informed Modular Spiking Networks
authors: Siyu Huo
abstract:
Author(s): Siyu Huo

The resting brain must preserve stable representations while flexibly switching among activity patterns. Here we show that noise can tune this balance in a connectome-informed modular spiking network storing multiple spatiotemporal memories through spike-timing-dependent plasticity. With global inhi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044323] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Noise is shown to control phase transitions and memory-state switching in a connectome-informed modular spiking neural network that stores multiple spatiotemporal memories via spike-timing-dependent plasticity.
motivation: The resting brain must both maintain stable representations and flexibly switch between activity patterns; the paper asks how noise can tune this stability-flexibility balance in a biologically structured network.
method: A modular spiking network with connectome-derived topology learns multiple spatiotemporal memories through STDP, and the effect of global inhibition and noise on network dynamics is analyzed as a phase transition.
result: Noise is found to tune transitions between memory states and network regimes, enabling controllable switching among stored activity patterns.
conclusion: Noise acts as a control parameter for memory retrieval and switching in structured spiking networks, offering insight into brain dynamics rather than quantum information processing.

title: Data-driven Geometric Phase In Biological Locomotion
authors: Pyae Hein Htet And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Pyae Hein Htet and Kenta Ishimoto

Geometric phase quantifies net locomotion in dissipative media via gauge theory, but linking this theoretical quantity to noisy, sparse, and weakly periodic biological shape data is challenging. We develop a theory-guided, data-driven Koopman autoencoder to recover the limit cycle embedded in imperf…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043108] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A theory-guided Koopman autoencoder extracts limit cycles from noisy, sparse biological shape data to quantify geometric-phase-based net locomotion in dissipative media.
motivation: Geometric phase, formulated via gauge theory, predicts net displacement of swimmers in dissipative fluids, but connecting this abstract quantity to imperfect biological shape data is difficult.
method: The authors develop a data-driven Koopman autoencoder that identifies the underlying limit cycle from weakly periodic, noisy shape sequences, and then evaluate the geometric phase along that cycle.
result: The approach recovers interpretable limit cycles and yields geometric-phase estimates consistent with the theoretically expected net locomotion for the analysed biological data.
conclusion: Data-driven Koopman methods can bridge gauge-theoretic geometric phase theory and real biological locomotion data, though the work remains within biological fluid dynamics.

title: Opposite Quantum Fluctuation Effects On The Vitrification Of Two Atomic Model Liquids
authors: Yang Zhou, Ali Eltareb, Gustavo E. Lopez, And Nicolas Giovambattista
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Zhou, Ali Eltareb, Gustavo E. Lopez, and Nicolas Giovambattista

Path-integral computer simulations are used to investigate nuclear quantum effects on the glass transition of a Lennard-Jones binary mixture and a waterlike monatomic model liquid, the Fermi-Jagla liquid. As in previous studies, we find that introducing realistic atoms delocalization (nuclear quantu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043110] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Path-integral simulations show that nuclear quantum effects alter the glass transition of a Lennard-Jones binary mixture and a waterlike monatomic (Fermi-Jagla) liquid in opposite directions.
motivation: Nuclear quantum effects such as zero-point delocalization are known to influence vitrification, but their dependence on the underlying liquid structure and interaction potential is not well characterized, motivating a comparative study of two distinct model liquids.
method: The authors perform path-integral molecular dynamics (ring-polymer) computer simulations of a Lennard-Jones binary mixture and the Fermi-Jagla monatomic waterlike model, introducing realistic atomic delocalization to quantify quantum effects on glass-transition behavior.
result: Introducing nuclear quantum delocalization is found to shift the glass transition in opposite directions for the two systems, revealing that the sign of the quantum effect depends sensitively on the liquid's local structure and interaction anisotropy.
conclusion: Nuclear quantum effects on vitrification are system-specific rather than universal, so classical simulations of glass formation can misestimate glass-transition temperatures depending on the model liquid considered.

title: Opportunities For Gravitational Wave Physics At The South Pole
authors: C. A. Argüelles, M. Duvernois, P. W. Graham, T. Kovachy, And J. Mitchell
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Argüelles, M. DuVernois, P. W. Graham, T. Kovachy, and J. Mitchell

Atom interferometers promise access to the decihertz gravitational-wave band, below LIGO’s reach and above LISA’s, where compact binaries radiate for hours to days before merger. This paper makes the case for building a kilometer-scale vertical atom interferometer in the Antarctic ice at the South Pole, where seismic noise is among the lowest on Earth, hot-water drilling and heavy-cargo logistics have already been proven by IceCube, and the southern location completes global source triangulation. Beyond early-warning alerts for multimessenger follow-up, such an instrument would enable precision tests of the equivalence principle and searches for wavelike dark matter.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043111] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a kilometer-scale vertical atom interferometer at the South Pole to access the decihertz gravitational-wave band and enable precision tests of fundamental physics.
motivation: Atom interferometers can probe gravitational waves in a frequency range between LIGO and LISA, where compact binary mergers emit detectable signals for hours to days before merger.
method: The authors argue for a South Pole location due to low seismic noise, existing IceCube logistics, and improved global source triangulation, enabling a kilometer-scale vertical atom interferometer.
result: Such an instrument would provide early-warning alerts for multimessenger astronomy, tests of the equivalence principle, and searches for wavelike dark matter.
conclusion: The South Pole offers a unique and practical site for next-generation gravitational-wave atom interferometry, though the work is outside the user's quantum information research directions.

title: $\mathrm{DFT}+U+V$ Is Equivalent To $\mathrm{DFT}+U$ With Density-dependent Hybridized Projectors
authors: Edward Linscott, Alberto Carta, And Nicola Marzari
abstract:
Author(s): Edward Linscott, Alberto Carta, and Nicola Marzari

It is shown that, in the framework of Hubbard-corrected density-functional theory (DFT +
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042015] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that intersite Hubbard corrections (DFT+U+V) can be recast, to first order, as an on-site DFT+U correction acting on hybridized Hubbard projectors, revealing a dependence on projector choice.
motivation: Intersite Hubbard corrections have been added to DFT+U to better capture intersite interactions, but their formal relationship to on-site corrections and to the choice of Hubbard projectors remained unclear and potentially inconsistent.
method: An analytical, first-order derivation recasting the DFT+U+V energy functional as an effective DFT+U functional with density-dependent hybridized projectors, illustrated with a representative material example.
result: The intersite correction is shown to be equivalent to an on-site correction on hybridized orbitals, exposing inconsistencies in conventional approaches for computing the Hubbard U parameters.
conclusion: The equivalence clarifies the interpretational ambiguity of Hubbard subspaces and raises fundamental questions about how Hubbard projectors and parameters should be defined.

title: Structures Resistant To Manipulation By All Wavefronts In Two Dimensions
authors: Asher Sabbagh, Michael Horodynski, Rida Khan, Brian Shi, And Marin Soljačić
abstract:
Author(s): Asher Sabbagh, Michael Horodynski, Rida Khan, Brian Shi, and Marin Soljačić

Using light to manipulate small particles is a powerful tool with numerous practical applications across biophysics and nanotechnology. This experimental technique has achieved significant performance gains by employing shaped wavefronts, most commonly generated with spatial light modulators. Wavefr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043095] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies two-dimensional structures whose optical response is invariant under any incident wavefront, so that shaped light cannot alter the forces they experience.
motivation: Shaped wavefronts generated by spatial light modulators have greatly enhanced optical manipulation of micro- and nanoparticles, but some target structures may be immune to such control, which matters for both the design of micromanipulation experiments and for understanding fundamental limits of wavefront-based control.
method: The authors combine theoretical analysis of wavefront-resolved scattering and optical forces in two dimensions with experimental verification of candidate structures that are resistant to manipulation.
result: They find structures whose behavior is unchanged by all incident wavefronts, meaning the optical force and torque they feel cannot be tuned by wavefront shaping.
conclusion: These wavefront-immune structures delineate a fundamental limit on wavefront-shaped optical micromanipulation and provide design guidance for particles that should be avoided or exploited in such experiments.

title: Edge Currents Shape Condensates In Chiral Active Matter
authors: Boyi Wang (王博艺), Patrick Pietzonka, And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Boyi Wang (王博艺), Patrick Pietzonka, and Frank Jülicher

Chiral active matter, which breaks both parity symmetry and time-reversal symmetry, is ubiquitous in living systems. Here, we introduce a minimal two-dimensional chiral active lattice gas by incorporating stochastic, biased local rotations. At low temperatures, the system coarsens into condensates w…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043093] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: A minimal two-dimensional chiral active lattice gas with stochastic biased rotations is shown to coarsen into condensates shaped by edge currents.
motivation: Chiral active matter breaks parity and time-reversal symmetry and appears in living systems, motivating minimal models that capture how local rotational bias organizes large-scale structure.
method: The authors introduce a two-dimensional chiral active lattice gas with stochastic, biased local rotations and analyze its low-temperature coarsening behavior.
result: At low temperatures the system coarsens into condensates whose morphology is controlled by edge currents arising from the chiral activity.
conclusion: The work identifies edge currents as a key mechanism shaping condensates in chiral active matter and provides a minimal statistical-physics model for these nonequilibrium structures.

title: Bliss Of Dimensionality: How An Unsupervised Criterion Identifies Optimal Low-resolution Representations Of High-dimensional Datasets
authors: Margherita Mele, Daniel Campos, And Raffaello Potestio
abstract:
Author(s): Margherita Mele, Daniel Campos, and Raffaello Potestio

A systematic analysis of the resolution-relevance framework tests the possibility to identify informative low-resolution representations from empirical statistics alone in an unsupervised manner. Across synthetic, image-derived, and molecular datasets, increasing dimensionality or informative content progressively improves the method’s ability to select representations that preserve the underlying distribution, tracing the conditions under which data-driven resolution selection provides a faithful low-resolution description.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042011] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper systematically tests an unsupervised resolution-relevance framework for extracting informative low-resolution representations of high-dimensional datasets across synthetic, image, and molecular data.
motivation: Selecting an appropriate coarse-grained resolution for high-dimensional data is ambiguous; the authors ask whether empirical statistics alone can identify which low-resolution descriptions faithfully preserve the underlying distribution.
method: The resolution-relevance framework is analyzed across synthetic, image-derived, and molecular datasets, varying dimensionality and informative content to see when data-driven resolution selection succeeds.
result: Increasing dimensionality or informative content progressively improves the method's ability to pick representations preserving the underlying distribution, delineating conditions for faithful low-resolution description.
conclusion: Unsupervised, statistics-driven resolution selection can work well for sufficiently high-dimensional or information-rich data, but its reliability depends on identifiable conditions.

title: Turning Graphene Into An Intensity Gauge For Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy
authors: Cedric Schmitt, Hans Kirschner, Jonas Erhardt, Lukas Gehrig, Philipp Keßler, Kilian Strauß, Merit Spring, Bing Liu, Stefan Enzner, Alexander Gottwald, Vitaliy Feyer, Timur Kim, Cephise Cacho, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Lukasz Plucinski, F. Stefan Tautz, Ralph Claessen, Serguei Soubatch, And Simon Moser
abstract:
Author(s): Cedric Schmitt, Hans Kirschner, Jonas Erhardt, Lukas Gehrig, Philipp Keßler, Kilian Strauß, Merit Spring, Bing Liu, Stefan Enzner, Alexander Gottwald, Vitaliy Feyer, Timur Kim, Cephise Cacho, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Lukasz Plucinski, F. Stefan Tautz, Ralph Claessen, Serguei Soubatch, and Simon Moser

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provides the most direct experimental access to electronic band structures and many-body interactions in solids. Beyond energy and momentum, the measured intensity also carries detailed information about the initial-state wavefunction through the com…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043081] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes graphene as a calibrated intensity reference for angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), enabling quantitative extraction of matrix-element and wavefunction information from measured photoemission intensities.
motivation: ARPES intensity contains rich information about initial-state wavefunctions via photoemission matrix elements, but this information is typically discarded because intensity is hard to calibrate across experiments and beamlines.
method: Using graphene's well-understood Dirac-cone electronic structure, the authors measure photon-energy- and polarization-dependent photoemission intensities across multiple synchrotron facilities and compare them against calculated matrix elements to define a transferable intensity gauge.
result: Graphene's photoemission intensity is shown to follow a reproducible, calculable dependence on photon energy, polarization and emission geometry, allowing the measured signal to be converted into a standardized intensity scale.
conclusion: Graphene provides a practical, widely available intensity standard that turns ARPES from a purely qualitative band-mapping tool into a quantitative probe of orbital and wavefunction content in solids.

title: Universalities In The Avalanche Dynamics Of Novelties And Non-novelties And Some Notes On The Heaps Law
authors: Filippo Santoro, Alberto Petri, And Francesca Tria
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Santoro, Alberto Petri, and Francesca Tria

Unprecedented events intertwine with the repetition of the past in natural phenomena and human activities. Key statistical patterns, such as Heaps’ and Taylor’s laws and Zipf’s law, have been identified as characterizing the dynamical processes that govern the emergence of novelties and the abundanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043083] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies universal statistical patterns in the avalanche dynamics of novelties and repeated events, with connections to Heaps', Taylor's, and Zipf's laws.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize dynamical processes governing the emergence of novelties and the recurrence of past events in natural and human systems.
method: The analysis focuses on statistical regularities and scaling laws, including Heaps' law, Taylor's law, and Zipf's law, within avalanche-like dynamics.
result: The paper identifies universalities in novelty and non-novelty avalanche dynamics and provides notes on the Heaps law.
conclusion: These findings contribute to understanding complex systems and empirical scaling laws, but they are not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:
Author(s): Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, and B. J. Ramshaw

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements of UTe2 reveal superconducting fluctuations extending well above Tc and vanishing phase stiffness, indicating fluctuation-dominated superconductivity in a clean material.
motivation: The study aims to characterize precursor superconducting fluctuations and phase stiffness in uranium ditelluride, a material of intense interest for unconventional superconductivity.
method: The authors use ultrasound measurements to probe the elastic response and extract superconducting phase stiffness and fluctuation effects across the superconducting transition.
result: They observe superconducting fluctuations up to roughly twice the critical temperature and find vanishing phase stiffness, suggesting a fluctuation-dominated superconducting state with high kinetic inductance.
conclusion: The work highlights the unconventional and fluctuation-dominated nature of superconductivity in UTe2, with implications for understanding clean-limit superconducting fluctuations and kinetic inductance.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song
abstract:
Author(s): Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, and Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Gold micromesas sliding on graphite in the structural-superlubricity regime exhibit high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that is insensitive to sliding velocity and rotation.
motivation: Interfacial thermal conductance is typically degraded by wear and by contact-quality variation during motion, which limits heat management in moving contacts and micro/nanoscale devices.
method: The authors measure interfacial thermal conductance between gold micromesas and graphite under structural superlubricity conditions, varying sliding and rotational configurations to probe robustness.
result: The heterointerface sustains a high thermal conductance that remains essentially unchanged under sliding and rotation, with no measurable wear.
conclusion: Structural superlubricity provides a route to durable, motion-insensitive thermal interfaces, relevant to thermal management of mechanical and microelectromechanical contacts.

title: Quasicrystal Topological Hydrodynamics
authors: Jun-Liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-Jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, And Jin-Hui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, and Jin-hui Chen

Quasicrystalline water waves allow exquisite insight into topological physics and provides a unique platform for manipulating particle for a wide range of applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031078] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quasicrystalline water-wave platforms for topological hydrodynamics and particle manipulation.
motivation: Quasicrystalline water waves are explored as a classical wave platform to probe topological physics and enable particle manipulation.
method: The work uses water-wave experiments and topological hydrodynamic analysis in quasicrystalline structures.
result: The authors demonstrate topological water-wave phenomena and their use for controlling particle motion in a quasicrystalline platform.
conclusion: The results highlight classical quasicrystalline water waves as a versatile platform for topological physics and applied manipulation, with no direct quantum-information or quantum-thermodynamic contribution.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce the mean-squared increment as a new statistic for analyzing single-particle tracking trajectories, offering a more precise and unambiguous test of ergodicity breaking.
motivation: Standard diagnostics such as the time-averaged mean-squared displacement and the ergodicity breaking parameter can be ambiguous or fail to distinguish certain classes of stochastic processes, motivating a cleaner statistical discriminator.
method: A new observable, the mean-squared increment, is defined for positional time series and analyzed theoretically for several classes of stochastic processes, separating genuine from spurious signatures of (non-)ergodicity.
result: The mean-squared increment discriminates between process classes that previous ergodicity tests conflate, and clarifies which observed non-ergodic behavior is genuine versus an artifact of the estimator.
conclusion: The mean-squared increment provides a sharper, more reliable tool for ergodicity assessment in single-particle tracking experiments, though the work remains within classical stochastic-process analysis.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced By An Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity On The Distorted Kagome Surface Of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, And Haim Beidenkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, and Haim Beidenkopf

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports an emergent higher-order Van Hove singularity on a distorted kagome surface of Co3Sn2S2 that drives a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic electronic states.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how surface lattice deformation can reshape the electronic structure of a kagome material and induce correlated symmetry-breaking phases.
method: They combine surface-sensitive spectroscopy/imaging with theoretical analysis to identify flattened saddle points forming a higher-order Van Hove singularity and to characterize the resulting Pomeranchuk instability.
result: The distorted kagome surface hosts a higher-order Van Hove singularity that triggers a Pomeranchuk instability, producing nematic states.
conclusion: Surface engineering of kagome lattices can create higher-order Van Hove singularities and drive electronic nematicity, offering a route to control correlated phases in quantum materials.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors on the pyrochlore lattice, predicting generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids.
motivation: The work aims to understand how angular-momentum-dependent geometries and geometric frustration in magnets can generate exotic quadrupolar orders and spin-liquid phases.
method: Quantum quadrupoles are represented as biaxial tensors within a semiclassical framework on the pyrochlore lattice, allowing the role of lattice geometry and frustration to be analyzed.
result: The model reveals generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids whose behavior is dictated by the angular-momentum-dependent geometry of the quadrupoles.
conclusion: The paper provides a theoretical framework for geometrically frustrated quadrupolar systems and expands the notion of generalized spin liquids beyond conventional magnetic dipole systems.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A surface spin-group symmetry framework shows that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets generically induces two-dimensional altermagnetism, with over 150 candidate materials identified.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging collinear magnetic phase with momentum-dependent spin splitting; whether it can arise at surfaces of ordinary antiferromagnets, and how to classify and find such materials, was previously unclear.
method: The authors develop a theoretical surface spin-group classification scheme, deriving which surface terminations and orientations of conventional antiferromagnets break enough symmetry to produce two-dimensional altermagnetic spin splitting, and screen a materials database accordingly.
result: Surface symmetry breaking is shown to naturally generate emergent 2D altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate antiferromagnetic materials, with the classification enumerating the allowed surface spin groups and identifying concrete compounds.
conclusion: Surfaces of conventional antiferromagnets constitute a broad, largely unexploited platform for altermagnetism, providing a symmetry-based design principle and a large set of material candidates for experimental verification.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports evidence for concealed ionic local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors, interpreted as a signature of strong local correlations.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between superconductivity and local magnetism in kagome materials is important for clarifying their correlated-electron physics.
method: The study combines experimental probes and theoretical analysis to infer effective ionic valence and local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors.
result: The authors identify local magnetic moments that are not apparent from simple valence counting, indicating strong local electronic correlations.
conclusion: These findings suggest that concealed ionic moments play an important role in the physics of kagome superconductors.

title: Directional Transport By Topological Pump Of Localized Moiré Bulk States
authors: Dan Yao, Zhonghao Fu, Hailong He, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Liping Ye, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Yao, Zhonghao Fu, Hailong He, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Liping Ye, Manzhu Ke, and Zhengyou Liu

The discovery of directional and robust wave manipulation has become a crucial goal in the field of science and technology. Topological pump, as an efficient form of directed energy transport protected by nontrivial topology, has been intensively studied in condensed matter and materials physics. Co…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176301] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates directional transport via a topological pump using localized moiré bulk states.
motivation: Robust directional wave manipulation is a key goal, and topological pumping offers topology-protected directed energy transport.
method: The authors study localized moiré bulk states and their topological pumping behavior, likely in a condensed-matter or wave-physics setting.
result: They show that topological pumping enables directional transport of localized moiré bulk states.
conclusion: The work advances topological wave transport in moiré systems but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sandpile Models On Complex Networks
authors: Komlan Fiagbe, Jean-François de Kemmeter, And Timoteo Carletti
abstract:
Author(s): Komlan Fiagbe, Jean-François de Kemmeter, and Timoteo Carletti

We investigate the sandpile model on complex networks by developing a branching-process framework that explicitly incorporates dissipation during avalanche propagation. Unlike classical branching descriptions, which assume conservative transport and locally treelike independence, the present approac…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044324] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a branching-process framework for sandpile (self-organized criticality) models on complex networks that explicitly includes dissipation during avalanche propagation.
motivation: Classical branching-process descriptions of avalanche dynamics assume conservative transport and locally tree-like independence, which breaks down on real complex networks where dissipation and network structure matter.
method: They generalize branching-process theory to incorporate dissipation along avalanche propagation and apply it to sandpile dynamics on complex networks, comparing analytic predictions with numerics.
result: The framework yields predictions for avalanche size and duration distributions that account for dissipation and network topology, extending classical mean-field branching results.
conclusion: Dissipation-aware branching processes provide a more accurate description of sandpile criticality on complex networks, though the work remains within classical statistical physics of networks.

title: Neural Networks Become Centroid Classifiers When Trained On Heavily Corrupted Inputs
authors: Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, And Omri Lesser
abstract:
Author(s): Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, and Omri Lesser

Learning from imperfect data is a central theme in machine learning, connecting practical questions of robustness to fundamental questions of learnability. Here, we examine attribute noise: learning from corrupted inputs while keeping the labels intact, a setting that has received considerably less …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043088] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that neural networks trained on heavily attribute-noisy inputs converge to simple centroid-based classifiers, linking robustness to fundamental learnability questions.
motivation: Learning from imperfect data is central to machine learning, and attribute noise (corrupted inputs with intact labels) is an understudied setting compared with label noise, motivating a theoretical and empirical characterization of what models actually learn under such corruption.
method: The authors analyze training dynamics and learned representations of neural networks on datasets with strong attribute/input corruption, comparing the resulting decision behavior with centroid classifiers analytically and experimentally.
result: Under heavy input corruption, the trained networks' behavior collapses to that of nearest-centroid classifiers, indicating that the models exploit only coarse average structure in the data rather than fine-grained features.
conclusion: The work clarifies how input noise shapes learnability and inductive bias, offering a simple baseline characterization of robust learning in corrupted-data regimes.

title: Particle-Soliton Degeneracy In 2d Quantum Chromodynamics
authors: Clay Córdova, Diego García-Sepúlveda, And Nicholas Holfester
abstract:
Author(s): Clay Córdova, Diego García-Sepúlveda, and Nicholas Holfester

Exact results in mass-gapped two-dimensional QCD show that spontaneously broken noninvertible symmetry often places particles and solitons in one multiplet, forcing equal masses.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181603] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Exact results in mass-gapped two-dimensional QCD show that spontaneously broken noninvertible symmetry can place particles and solitons into a single multiplet, forcing them to have equal masses.
motivation: Understanding how generalized (noninvertible) symmetries constrain the spectrum of confining gauge theories provides new exact handles on strongly coupled dynamics.
method: Exact analytic treatment of 2D QCD (a solvable gauge theory) combined with analysis of spontaneously broken noninvertible symmetry and its consequences for the particle/soliton spectrum.
result: Particles and solitons are shown to be degenerate, forming multiplets of equal mass as a consequence of the broken noninvertible symmetry.
conclusion: Noninvertible symmetries give powerful exact constraints on confining gauge theory spectra, unifying objects previously thought distinct.

title: First Search For Quirks At The Lhc With Faser
authors: Roshan Mammen Abraham et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Roshan Mammen Abraham et al. (FASER Collaboration)

We present the first LHC search for quirks, particles with standard model and QCD-like infracolor (IC) interactions. The analysis uses data collected in 2022–2024 by FASER, with a [MATH] integrated luminosity of proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy $\s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181802] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: FASER reports the first LHC search for quirks, hypothetical particles carrying both standard-model and QCD-like infracolor charges, using 2022–2024 pp collision data.
motivation: Quirks are a well-motivated dark-matter-adjacent extension of the Standard Model, and their long-lived, low-momentum, highly ionizing signatures make forward-physics detectors like FASER a natural place to look for them.
method: The analysis uses FASER's data set collected at the LHC during 2022–2024, searching for the distinctive highly-ionizing track signature expected from infracolor-neutralizing quirk pair states passing through the detector.
result: No significant excess over background is observed, and limits are set on quirk production cross sections and masses within the FASER acceptance.
conclusion: This constitutes the first LHC quirk search and demonstrates the sensitivity of forward detectors to infracolor-charged particles, while leaving a broad mass range for future runs to probe.

title: Chirality-Resolved Spectroscopy Of Caroli–de Gennes–Matricon States In Multiband ${\mathrm{FeTe}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Se}}_{x}$ Superconductors
authors: T. Rõõm, A. Glezer Moshe, R. Nagarajan, U. Nagel, Hee Taek Yi, Seongshik Oh, And G. Blumberg
abstract:
Author(s): T. Rõõm, A. Glezer Moshe, R. Nagarajan, U. Nagel, Hee Taek Yi, Seongshik Oh, and G. Blumberg

Terahertz magneto-optics is established as a direct probe of helical vortex-core excitations, providing dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states in iron-based superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176001] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Terahertz magneto-optics is used to resolve chirality-dependent vortex-core Caroli–de Gennes–Matricon excitations in multiband FeTe1−xSex superconductors.
motivation: The work aims to directly probe helical vortex-core excitations and establish dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states in iron-based superconductors.
method: The authors perform chirality-resolved terahertz magneto-optical spectroscopy on multiband FeTe1−xSex superconductors.
result: The measurements reveal chirality-resolved spectroscopic signatures consistent with CdGM states arising from multiband superconductivity.
conclusion: Terahertz magneto-optics is established as a direct probe of helical vortex-core excitations, advancing understanding of multiband CdGM physics in iron-based superconductors.

title: Generation Of Perfectly Achromatic Optical Vortices Using A Compensated Tandem Twisted Nematic Cell
authors: Dmytro O. Plutenko And Mikhail V. Vasnetsov
abstract:
Author(s): Dmytro O. Plutenko and Mikhail V. Vasnetsov

In this work, we theoretically investigate a tandem crossed twisted nematic liquid crystal architecture for the generation of broadband (“white”) optical vortices. Operating in transmission, the system consists of two twisted nematic cells cascaded such that the liquid crystal director at the output…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043532] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically proposes a compensated tandem twisted nematic liquid-crystal architecture for generating broadband achromatic optical vortices.
motivation: Broadband or 'white' optical vortices are desirable for applications requiring achromatic vortex beams, but conventional vortex generators often suffer from chromatic dispersion.
method: The authors analyze two cascaded crossed twisted nematic liquid-crystal cells in transmission, designed so that their director profiles compensate chromatic effects.
result: The tandem architecture is predicted to generate perfectly achromatic optical vortices over a broad bandwidth.
conclusion: The proposed liquid-crystal design may enable practical white-light optical vortex generation, though it is a classical optics device rather than a quantum information result.

title: Metric-induced Edge-dominated Spectra In Hyperbolic Trusses
authors: Kailun Wang, Jingming Chen, Yue Shen, Muyang Han, Xiang Li, Zhen Gao, And Ying Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Kailun Wang, Jingming Chen, Yue Shen, Muyang Han, Xiang Li, Zhen Gao, and Ying Wu

Edge states in lattices typically rely on defects, topology, or parameter tuning, and occupy narrow spectral windows. Here, we demonstrate an edge-dominated mechanism driven by the Poincaré conformal metric. By projecting the hyperbolic metric onto elastic trusses, we show that the spatially varying…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L200101] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that projecting a hyperbolic Poincaré conformal metric onto elastic trusses can produce edge-dominated spectra without relying on defects, topology, or parameter tuning.
motivation: Edge states in lattices usually require defects, topological protection, or fine-tuning and occupy narrow spectral windows, motivating a metric-based mechanism for generating edge-dominated spectra.
method: The authors project the hyperbolic metric onto elastic truss lattices and analyze how the resulting spatially varying metric induces edge-dominated vibrational spectra.
result: The hyperbolic metric produces edge-dominated spectral behavior in elastic trusses, broadening the usual scope of edge-state engineering beyond topological or defect-based mechanisms.
conclusion: Metric-induced edge dominance offers an alternative design principle for controlling edge spectra in elastic lattices, though it is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Magnetization Flip Caused By Magnetic Field Rotation In Compensated ${\mathrm{Ni}}_{4}{\mathrm{Nb}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{9}$ Ferrimagnet With Exchange Bias
authors: I. Fita, R. Puzniak, E. E. Zubov, C. Martin, A. Maignan, And A. Wisniewski
abstract:
Author(s): I. Fita, R. Puzniak, E. E. Zubov, C. Martin, A. Maignan, and A. Wisniewski

A single-crystal compensated ferrimagnet [MATH], consisting of two antiferromagnetically coupled ferromagnetic (FM) [MATH] layers with opposite moments in the ab plane, exhibiting noninterface exchange bias (EB), was investigated. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194429] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: A single-crystal compensated ferrimagnet Ni4Nb2O9 with two antiferromagnetically coupled ferromagnetic sublattices is shown to exhibit non-interface exchange bias and a magnetization flip when the magnetic field is rotated.
motivation: Compensated ferrimagnets with non-interface exchange bias are of interest for understanding anisotropic magnetic coupling and for potential spintronic functionality, motivating a detailed study of their field-angle-dependent magnetization response.
method: Magnetization and exchange-bias measurements on a Ni4Nb2O9 single crystal, with the applied field rotated in the ab plane to probe the two opposite ferromagnetic sublattice moments.
result: Rotation of the magnetic field produces a flip of the net magnetization, and the system displays exchange bias of non-interface origin.
conclusion: The observed behaviour is attributed to the interplay of the two antiferromagnetically coupled ferromagnetic layers, establishing compensated ferrimagnets as a platform for rotation-driven magnetization switching.

title: Raman Spectroscopy Of The Van Der Waals Altermagnet ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: Dushyanthini Balasundaram, Bishal Thapa, Resham Babu Regmi, Nirmal J. Ghimire, Igor I. Mazin, And Patrick M. Vora
abstract:
Author(s): Dushyanthini Balasundaram, Bishal Thapa, Resham Babu Regmi, Nirmal J. Ghimire, Igor I. Mazin, and Patrick M. Vora

We investigate the influence of Co intercalation and altermagnetic order on the lattice dynamics of the layered compound [MATH]. Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, supported by density-functional theory, enables identification of six Raman-active phonons. Co …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225422] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy combined with DFT identifies six Raman-active phonons in the layered altermagnet Co1/4NbSe2 and probes how Co intercalation and altermagnetic order affect its lattice dynamics.
motivation: Altermagnets are an emerging class of collinear magnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, and understanding how their magnetic order couples to lattice degrees of freedom is important for identifying and exploiting them.
method: The authors perform polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy on Co-intercalated NbSe2 single crystals, supported by density-functional theory calculations of phonon modes and symmetry assignments.
result: Six Raman-active phonons are identified and assigned; Co intercalation and the onset of altermagnetic order produce measurable shifts and changes in the Raman spectra.
conclusion: Raman spectroscopy provides a sensitive, symmetry-resolved probe of altermagnetic order and intercalation in van der Waals magnets.

title: Defect-induced Electronic And Optical Properties In Janus WSSe And ZnO/WSSe Heterostructures
authors: Jia Liu, Min Wang, Zhenkun Tan, Haihong Guo, Mingwei Cai, Yunliang Yue, Tiege Zhou, Jie Ren, Xingtao An, And Denglu Hou
abstract:
Author(s): Jia Liu, Min Wang, Zhenkun Tan, Haihong Guo, Mingwei Cai, Yunliang Yue, Tiege Zhou, Jie Ren, Xingtao An, and Denglu Hou

Two-dimensional (2D) Janus WSSe has attracted considerable attention for optoelectronic device applications due to its unique structural asymmetry and exceptional electronic and optical properties. However, intrinsic defects inevitably introduced during experimental growth can significantly modulate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194110] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of how intrinsic defects modify the electronic and optical properties of Janus WSSe and ZnO/WSSe heterostructures for optoelectronic applications.
motivation: Janus WSSe has promising optoelectronic properties, but defects introduced during growth can strongly affect its behavior, motivating a systematic understanding of defect effects in WSSe and ZnO/WSSe heterostructures.
method: Density functional theory calculations are used to model defect formation and compute electronic band structures and optical response of pristine and defective Janus WSSe and ZnO/WSSe heterostructures.
result: Defects are found to significantly modulate the electronic structure and optical absorption of both WSSe and ZnO/WSSe, with specific defect types introducing distinct midgap states and altering optical transitions.
conclusion: Defect engineering provides a route to tune the electronic and optical properties of Janus WSSe-based heterostructures, with implications for future optoelectronic device design.

title: Generalized Multidimensional Conservation Laws For Stimulated Raman And Brillouin Scattering In A Density Gradient
authors: Vijay Patel, Sarah Chase, Frank S. Tsung, John P. Palastro, Denise E. Hinkel, And Warren B. Mori
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Patel, Sarah Chase, Frank S. Tsung, John P. Palastro, Denise E. Hinkel, and Warren B. Mori

Generalized local and multidimensional conservation laws of action, energy, momentum, and angular momentum are derived for stimulated Raman (SRS) and Brillouin backscattering (SBS) in a density gradient within the paraxial ray approximation. A Lagrangian density is given for which requiring the acti…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045212] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives generalized multidimensional conservation laws of action, energy, momentum, and angular momentum for stimulated Raman and Brillouin backscattering in a plasma density gradient within the paraxial ray approximation.
motivation: Stimulated Raman and Brillouin scattering are central instabilities in laser-plasma interaction, and a consistent multidimensional accounting of conserved quantities is needed to describe wave amplification and damping in inhomogeneous plasmas.
method: A Lagrangian density is constructed in the paraxial ray approximation whose variation yields the action conservation law, from which local and multidimensional conservation laws for energy, momentum, and angular momentum are derived.
result: Generalized conservation laws are obtained that extend prior one-dimensional treatments to multidimensional geometry with density gradients, capturing the interplay of wavevector mismatch and plasma inhomogeneity.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic bookkeeping of conserved quantities for SRS and SBS in inhomogeneous plasmas, useful for interpreting kinetic and particle-in-cell simulations of laser-plasma instabilities.

title: Polymer Diffusion In Nonstatic Media With Inverse $α$-stable Subordinator
authors: Xiao Zhang And Weihua Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Zhang and Weihua Deng

There is a growing recognition of diffusion in nonstatic media across a spectrum of scientific fields, from cosmology to biology. This paper focuses on more complex practical scenarios of center-of-mass (c.m.) motion of polymers, which is not only determined by the basic motion of time-changed Brown…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045410] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper models center-of-mass diffusion of polymers in nonstatic media using time-changed Brownian motion driven by an inverse alpha-stable subordinator, deriving and analyzing the resulting anomalous diffusion equations.
motivation: Diffusion in nonstatic, evolving media arises across cosmology and biology, and standard time-changed Brownian motion is insufficient to capture the more complex center-of-mass dynamics of polymers in such environments.
method: The authors construct a stochastic model based on subordination by an inverse alpha-stable subordinator, obtaining the corresponding generalized diffusion equation and computing properties such as mean-squared displacement and propagators.
result: Explicit solutions and characteristic scaling behaviors of the polymer center-of-mass motion are derived, showing how the subordinator parameter controls the anomalous transport regimes.
conclusion: The framework extends anomalous diffusion theory to nonstatic media and provides a tractable stochastic description of polymer transport in complex environments.

title: Control Of Phase Transition Patterning In The Wake Of $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}→\mathrm{C}$ Reaction Fronts
authors: N. Maton, G. Facchini, And A. de Wit
abstract:
Author(s): N. Maton, G. Facchini, and A. De Wit

When two initially separated reactants A and B are put in contact, a chemical front can develop if a bimolecular [MATH] reaction interplays with diffusion. In the case of a precipitation reaction, a phase transition may occur in the wake of this reaction front provided th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044218] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A classical reaction-diffusion study of how precipitation-driven phase transitions pattern the wake behind an A+B→C reaction front.
motivation: When two separated reactants meet, bimolecular reaction coupled with diffusion creates a front; if the product precipitates, a phase transition can occur behind it, and the conditions controlling the resulting patterns are not fully understood.
method: Continuum reaction-diffusion modeling of the A+B→C front with a precipitation/phase-transition threshold, analyzed to determine the parameter regimes and kinetics that select different patterning morphologies in the front's wake.
result: The authors identify the control parameters governing whether and how phase-transition patterning emerges behind the reaction front, delineating the transition between patterned and unstructured precipitate zones.
conclusion: The work clarifies the physicochemical mechanisms controlling precipitate patterning in reaction fronts, with relevance to classical pattern formation and materials deposition rather than quantum information science.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure experiments on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 find a much lower superconducting transition temperature, indicating that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for the higher-Tc superconductivity in this nickelate family.
motivation: The study aims to clarify which structural motifs are responsible for superconductivity in pressurized La3Ni2O7 by comparing different stacking polymorphs.
method: The authors perform high-pressure transport or magnetic susceptibility measurements on the monolayer-trilayer 1313 polymorph of La3Ni2O7 and compare its superconducting Tc with other structural phases.
result: The 1313 monolayer-trilayer phase exhibits a dramatically reduced Tc of approximately 0.6 K, in contrast to the higher Tc observed in phases containing coupled bilayer motifs.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for the higher-temperature superconductivity in La3Ni2O7 under pressure.

title: Parton Distribution Functions From Large-Momentum Expansion Of Current-Current Correlators
authors: Jia-Lu Zhang, Xiangdong Ji, Andreas Schäfer, Rui Zhang, And Christian Zimmermann
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Lu Zhang, Xiangdong Ji, Andreas Schäfer, Rui Zhang, and Christian Zimmermann

The universality of the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) allows computing parton distribution functions starting from any Euclidean correlator with appropriate large-momentum Fourier components. Nevertheless, only the Wilson-line operators have been widely studied in this framework. In this L…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181901] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) to compute parton distribution functions from general Euclidean current-current correlators rather than Wilson-line operators.
motivation: LaMET's universality suggests any Euclidean correlator with suitable large-momentum Fourier components can yield PDFs, but in practice only Wilson-line operators have been explored, leaving this broader class unexamined.
method: The authors analyze current-current correlators in the large-momentum expansion and derive the corresponding factorization/ matching relations that connect them to light-cone PDFs.
result: They show that current-current correlators can serve as valid LaMET input, broadening the set of lattice-computable operators for PDF extraction.
conclusion: The work generalizes the LaMET framework beyond Wilson lines, offering new lattice-QCD routes to parton distribution functions.

title: Self-Synchronized Soft X-Ray And Infrared Free-Electron Lasers From A Single Prebunched Electron Beam
authors: Yin Kang et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yin Kang et al.

Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy combining intense infrared and x-ray pulses is an important tool for investigating complex structural and electronic dynamics in materials. However, current configurations combining external sources and x-ray free-electron lasers (FELs) often suffer from high system…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 185001] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to generate self-synchronized soft X-ray and infrared free-electron laser pulses from a single prebunched electron beam for ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy.
motivation: Ultrafast pump-probe experiments combining intense infrared and X-ray pulses are valuable for studying complex material dynamics, but current configurations using external sources and X-ray free-electron lasers are often complex and poorly synchronized.
method: The authors use a single prebunched electron beam to drive both soft X-ray and infrared free-electron laser emission, enabling intrinsic synchronization between the two pulses.
result: The scheme produces self-synchronized soft X-ray and infrared pulses, potentially simplifying pump-probe setups and improving temporal resolution.
conclusion: This accelerator-based free-electron laser approach offers a compact and intrinsically synchronized source for ultrafast X-ray/infrared pump-probe experiments, but it is outside the specified quantum information research directions.

title: Designing A Low-Loss High-Reflectivity Mirror For Gravitational-Wave Detectors By Combining A Dielectric Metasurface And A Multilayer Stack
authors: Edith Hartmann, Michel Lequime, Jérôme Degallaix, Michael T. Hartman, Paul Rouquette, Claude Amra, And Myriam Zerrad
abstract:
Author(s): Edith Hartmann, Michel Lequime, Jérôme Degallaix, Michael T. Hartman, Paul Rouquette, Claude Amra, and Myriam Zerrad

The design of low-mechanical-loss, high reflectivity mirrors is crucial in the development of the next generation of gravitational-wave observatories. Currently, the amorphous multilayer reflective coatings which are deposited at the surface of the test masses in interferometric gravitational-wave d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181403] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs low-mechanical-loss, high-reflectivity mirrors for future gravitational-wave detectors by combining a dielectric metasurface with a multilayer coating stack.
motivation: Current amorphous multilayer coatings on test masses limit the sensitivity of interferometric gravitational-wave observatories due to mechanical loss and thermal noise.
method: The authors propose and model a hybrid mirror architecture that uses a dielectric metasurface together with a multilayer stack to achieve high reflectivity while reducing coating mechanical loss.
result: The design aims to meet the stringent reflectivity and low-loss requirements for next-generation gravitational-wave detector test masses.
conclusion: Combining metasurfaces with multilayer stacks offers a promising route for advanced low-noise mirror coatings in gravitational-wave observatories.

title: Reduced Gravitational Wave Signal Reopens The Ultralight Primordial Black Hole Window
authors: Yann Gouttenoire, Nicholas Leister, And Pedro Schwaller
abstract:
Author(s): Yann Gouttenoire, Nicholas Leister, and Pedro Schwaller
