The hot big bang may have emerged from evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs) lighter than [MATH]. Standard monochromatic treatments predict nearly simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and a large poltergeist scalar-induced gravitational wave signal. We con…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181002] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Cosmological study showing that accounting for non-monochromatic (extended) mass distributions of ultralight primordial black holes reduces the predicted scalar-induced gravitational wave signal, reopening the allowed parameter window.
motivation: Standard monochromatic treatments of PBH evaporation predict near-simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and an overly large 'poltergeist' scalar-induced gravitational wave background, which appeared to rule out ultralight PBHs.
method: Aspects of the evaporation and reheating history are modeled with a spread of PBH masses rather than a delta-function distribution, and the resulting induced gravitational wave spectrum is computed.
result: The extended mass distribution smooths reheating and suppresses the induced gravitational wave signal, bringing it below current observational bounds.
conclusion: Ultralight primordial black holes remain a viable scenario for the origin of the hot big bang, since the previously excluded window is reopened once realistic mass distributions are considered.

title: Curvature Potential Formulation For Thin Elastic Sheets
authors: Yael Cohen, Animesh Pandey, Yafei Zhang, Cy Maor, And Michael Moshe
abstract:
Author(s): Yael Cohen, Animesh Pandey, Yafei Zhang, Cy Maor, and Michael Moshe

Thin sheets, from graphene to biological membranes, exhibit wrinkling, folding, and thermal deformations driven by geometric nonlinearities. They are treated using weakly nonlinear theories such as the Föppl–von Kármán equations, whose reliance on small slopes and a single-valued height field exclud…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 188201] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a curvature-based potential formulation for thin elastic sheets that captures wrinkling, folding, and thermal deformation beyond the small-slope, single-valued height-field limitations of Föppl–von Kármán theory.
motivation: Weakly nonlinear plate theories such as Föppl–von Kármán rely on small slopes and a single-valued height field, which excludes strongly folded or multivalued configurations common in graphene and biological membranes.
method: A formulation is developed in terms of a curvature potential rather than a height field, allowing geometric nonlinearities of thin sheets to be treated without the small-slope and single-valued assumptions.
result: The approach reproduces and extends descriptions of wrinkling, folding, and thermal deformation in thin sheets where conventional weakly nonlinear elastic models break down.
conclusion: The curvature potential framework offers a more general continuum-mechanical description of thin elastic sheet morphologies, with relevance to soft matter and membrane physics rather than quantum information.

title: Local Obstructions To Trapped-Region Escape In Modified Gravity
authors: Francisco S. N. Lobo
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco S. N. Lobo

Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an “effective” stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. We develop a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181402] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how energy conditions imposed on effective stress tensors in modified gravity obscure which sector governs null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions.
motivation: In modified gravity, energy conditions are usually imposed on an effective stress tensor that mixes matter with extra gravitational degrees of freedom, leaving unclear which sector actually controls null convergence and trapped-region formation.
method: A framework is developed to separate the matter and geometric contributions to the effective stress tensor and to derive local obstructions to escaping trapped regions.
result: Local conditions are identified that prevent trapped-region escape once the effective energy condition is decomposed into its matter and gravitational parts.
conclusion: The work clarifies how modified-gravity degrees of freedom affect horizon structure and trapped surfaces, refining how energy conditions should be formulated in such theories.

title: Escape From Heterogeneous Diffusion
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

Many physical processes depend on the time it takes a diffusing particle to find a target. Though this classical quantity is now well understood in various scenarios, little is known when the diffusivity depends on the location of the particle. For such heterogeneous diffusion, the multiplicative no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 187101] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for classical diffusing particles when the diffusion coefficient varies spatially, characterizing escape from heterogeneous diffusion.
motivation: Many physical target-search processes depend on diffusion times, but existing theory is largely limited to homogeneous diffusivity; spatially dependent diffusivity is less understood.
method: The authors analyze a classical stochastic diffusion model with position-dependent diffusivity, likely using multiplicative noise and first-passage-time techniques.
result: They derive or characterize escape/first-passage behavior for heterogeneous diffusion, revealing how spatial variation in diffusivity alters target-finding times.
conclusion: The work advances classical stochastic process theory for heterogeneous media but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Rotational Excitation Of Asymmetric-top Molecular Ions By Electron Impact: Application To ${\mathrm{H}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}^{+}$, ${\mathrm{HDO}}^{+}$, And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}^{+}$
authors: Joshua Forer
abstract:
Author(s): Joshua Forer

The rotational excitation of the three asymmetric-top molecular ion isotopologues [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] is studied theoretically using a combined framework of electron-molecule R matrix scattering theory, multichannel quantum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042820] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies rotational excitation of asymmetric-top molecular ions (H2O+, HDO+, D2O+) by electron impact using R-matrix scattering theory and multichannel quantum defect theory.
motivation: Understanding electron-impact rotational excitation of molecular ions is important for modeling astrophysical and plasma environments, but it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics.
method: Combined framework of electron-molecule R-matrix scattering theory and multichannel quantum defect theory to compute cross sections for rotational transitions.
result: The authors calculate rotational excitation cross sections for the three isotopologues, providing theoretical data for these asymmetric-top molecular ions.
conclusion: The study offers a theoretical treatment of electron-impact rotational excitation relevant to molecular physics and astrochemistry, with no direct connection to the specified research directions.

title: Theory Framework For Medium-mass Muonic Atoms
authors: S. Rathi, I. A. Valuev, Z. Sun, M. Heines, P. Indelicato, B. Ohayon, And N. S. Oreshkina
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rathi, I. A. Valuev, Z. Sun, M. Heines, P. Indelicato, B. Ohayon, and N. S. Oreshkina

We present a state-of-the-art theoretical approach for computing bound-state energies in muonic atoms, incorporating improved quantum electrodynamics effects and nuclear polarization corrections with a systematic assessment of theoretical uncertainties. Our approach is based on a combination of the …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042819] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a theoretical framework for calculating bound-state energies in medium-mass muonic atoms with improved QED and nuclear-polarization corrections.
motivation: Precise muonic-atom spectroscopy can probe nuclear structure and test quantum electrodynamics, requiring accurate bound-state energy calculations and uncertainty estimates.
method: The authors combine state-of-the-art QED corrections with nuclear polarization effects and a systematic treatment of theoretical uncertainties for medium-mass muonic atoms.
result: The framework provides improved theoretical predictions for bound-state energies in muonic atoms, including quantified uncertainties from QED and nuclear-polarization contributions.
conclusion: This work supports precision tests of atomic and nuclear theory in muonic systems but is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Role Of Oxygen Vacancies In Stabilizing The Orthorhombic Phases Of $\mathrm{H}{\mathrm{f}}_{0.5}\mathrm{Z}{\mathrm{r}}_{0.5}{\mathrm{O}}_{2}$ Nanoparticles
authors: Yuriy O. Zagorodniy, Eugene A. Eliseev, Valentin V. Laguta, Petr Jiricek, Jana Houdkova, Lesya D. Demchenko, Oksana V. Leshchenko, Victor N. Pavlikov, Lesya P. Yurchenko, Anna O. Diachenko, Michail D. Volnyanskii, Oleksandr S. Pylypchuk, Myroslav V. Karpets, Mikhail P. Trubitsyn, Dean R. Evans, And Anna N. Morozovska
abstract:
Author(s): Yuriy O. Zagorodniy, Eugene A. Eliseev, Valentin V. Laguta, Petr Jiricek, Jana Houdkova, Lesya D. Demchenko, Oksana V. Leshchenko, Victor N. Pavlikov, Lesya P. Yurchenko, Anna O. Diachenko, Michail D. Volnyanskii, Oleksandr S. Pylypchuk, Myroslav V. Karpets, Mikhail P. Trubitsyn, Dean R. Evans, and Anna N. Morozovska

In this work we study the stabilization of the orthorhombic phases in small [MATH] nanoparticles (average size ∼7 nm) annealed under different oxygen partial pressures. Concentration of the oxygen vacancies, which is determined by a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214111] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how oxygen vacancies stabilize orthorhombic phases in small Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 nanoparticles annealed under different oxygen partial pressures.
motivation: Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 is important for ferroelectric applications, and understanding phase stabilization in nanoparticles is relevant for controlling its functional properties.
method: The authors synthesize and anneal Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 nanoparticles under varying oxygen partial pressures and characterize the resulting phases and oxygen-vacancy concentrations.
result: Oxygen vacancies are found to play a key role in stabilizing orthorhombic phases in the approximately 7 nm nanoparticles.
conclusion: The work provides insight into defect-mediated phase control in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 nanoparticles, with relevance to ferroelectric materials science rather than quantum information.

title: Symmetries And Equivalence Transformations In Linear Stability Theory And Their Implications For The Dispersion Relation
authors: Kilian Vinzenz Wilhelm, Johannes Conrad, Martin Oberlack, And Yongqi Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Kilian Vinzenz Wilhelm, Johannes Conrad, Martin Oberlack, and Yongqi Wang

The present work revisits hydrodynamic linear stability theory from the perspective of Lie symmetries. For the linearized Navier-Stokes equations of a two-component shear flow, the expected symmetries and equivalence transformations of the Navier-Stokes group are recovered, while additional ones ari…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045107] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits hydrodynamic linear stability theory for a two-component shear flow using Lie symmetry and equivalence-transformation methods to derive implications for the dispersion relation.
motivation: Linear stability analysis of shear flows is central to predicting transition to turbulence, and the authors aim to systematize the known symmetries of the linearized Navier-Stokes equations to constrain the resulting dispersion relations.
method: Lie group analysis is applied to the linearized Navier-Stokes equations of a two-component shear flow, recovering the symmetries and equivalence transformations of the Navier-Stokes group and identifying additional ones arising in the linearized setting.
result: The symmetry and equivalence-transformation structure is fully characterized, and these symmetries are shown to impose constraints and mappings on the dispersion relation of the linear stability problem.
conclusion: Lie symmetries provide an organizing principle for linear stability theory, allowing known solutions and dispersion relations to be generated or related via equivalence transformations.

title: Generalized Schamel Nonlinear Schrödinger Dynamics Of Ion-acoustic Wave Packets In Electronegative Plasmas With Trapped Negative Ions
authors: Chérif Souleman Panguetna, Conrad Bertrand Tabi, Stéphanie Ganyou, And Timoléon Crépin Kofané
abstract:
Author(s): Chérif Souleman Panguetna, Conrad Bertrand Tabi, Stéphanie Ganyou, and Timoléon Crépin Kofané

We investigate the amplitude modulation of ion-acoustic wave packets in an unmagnetized electronegative plasma composed of cold positive ions, Boltzmann electrons, and negative ions following a Schamel trapped-particle distribution. The trapped-particle description is relevant to weakly collisional …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045213] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives and analyzes a generalized Schamel-type nonlinear Schrödinger equation governing amplitude modulation of ion-acoustic wave packets in an unmagnetized electronegative plasma with trapped negative ions.
motivation: Electronegative plasmas containing trapped negative ions are relevant to weakly collisional laboratory and space environments, and the authors aim to understand how trapped-particle distributions modify the nonlinear envelope dynamics of ion-acoustic wave packets.
method: A reductive perturbation (multiple-scales) expansion is applied to the fluid-Poisson system with cold positive ions, Boltzmann electrons, and a Schamel trapped-particle distribution for negative ions, yielding a generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation whose coefficients depend on the trapping parameter.
result: The generalized Schamel nonlinear Schrödinger equation admits both bright- and dark-type envelope solutions, and the trapping parameter is shown to modulate the dispersion, nonlinearity, and stability properties of these wave packets.
conclusion: Trapped negative ions qualitatively reshape the modulational dynamics of ion-acoustic wave packets in electronegative plasmas, providing a theoretical basis for interpreting nonlinear electrostatic structures in such media.

title: Impedance Of An Electric Double Layer Capacitor With A Multi-component Electrolyte
authors: David Fertig
abstract:
Author(s): David Fertig

I derive the impedance response of an ideal electrolyte containing an arbitrary number of mobile ionic species between blocking planar electrodes, described by the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations. By transforming the linearized equations to a charge-salt description, the response is written in terms…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045413] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives the impedance response of an ideal multi-component electrolyte between blocking planar electrodes using the linearized Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations recast in a charge-salt description.
motivation: Electric double layer capacitors with multi-species electrolytes are common in energy storage, but their impedance response is typically analyzed only for simple binary electrolytes, leaving a gap for arbitrary ionic mixtures.
method: The linearized Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations for an arbitrary number of mobile ionic species are transformed into charge-salt variables, yielding an analytic expression for the impedance between blocking planar electrodes.
result: The impedance is expressed in a closed form capturing the contributions of each ionic species, providing a generalization of prior binary-electrolyte results to multi-component electrolytes.
conclusion: The derived expression offers a practical analytical tool for interpreting impedance spectra of multi-component electrolyte double-layer capacitors.

title: Unique Nonconcentric Semicircular Arrays Of Nanoparticles Via Controlled Gravitational Force
authors: Sanjoy Khawas, Suman Bhattacharjee, And Sunita Srivastava
abstract:
Author(s): Sanjoy Khawas, Suman Bhattacharjee, and Sunita Srivastava

The dynamic behavior of the three-phase contact line (TPCL) during droplet evaporation plays a critical role in governing particle assembly processes, enabling spatially controlled deposition of nanomaterials at micro/nanoscales. This phenomenon utilizes evaporation-driven capillary and possible Mar…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045506] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates controlled gravitational-force-assisted formation of unique nonconcentric semicircular nanoparticle arrays during droplet evaporation.
motivation: The authors aim to understand and control three-phase contact line dynamics and particle assembly during evaporation-driven deposition at micro/nanoscales.
method: Droplet evaporation experiments and analysis of capillary, Marangoni, and gravitational effects are used to direct nanoparticle deposition into nonconcentric semicircular arrays.
result: Spatially controlled nonconcentric semicircular nanoparticle assemblies are achieved by tuning the gravitational force and evaporation-driven contact line behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a route to engineered nanoparticle architectures via controlled droplet evaporation, with relevance to colloidal assembly and microscale patterning.

title: Evolutionary Hysteresis: Cycling About In A Rugged Landscape
authors: Luke Piszkin And Dervis Can Vural
abstract:
Author(s): Luke Piszkin and Dervis Can Vural

In this work, we integrate theoretical modeling, molecular simulation, and empirical analysis to identify and characterize evolutionary hysteresis. We first show how epistatic interactions create bistable fitness landscapes and structural hysteresis in a two-locus Wright-Fisher model, revealing two …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044408] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies and characterizes 'evolutionary hysteresis' — history-dependent, bistable outcomes in evolving populations — using a two-locus Wright-Fisher model, molecular simulation, and empirical analysis.
motivation: Epistatic interactions can make fitness landscapes rugged and multi-peaked, raising the question of whether populations retain memory of their evolutionary trajectory, analogous to hysteresis in physical systems.
method: A theoretical two-locus Wright-Fisher model with epistasis is analyzed to show bistability in fitness landscapes, complemented by molecular simulation and empirical data analysis.
result: Epistatic interactions are shown to generate bistable fitness landscapes and structural hysteresis, so that cycling an environment parameter does not return the population to its initial state.
conclusion: Evolutionary dynamics on rugged landscapes exhibit genuine hysteresis, implying that current environment alone does not determine population state and that evolutionary history must be accounted for in predicting adaptation.

title: Emergence And Coexistence Of Periodic And Unstructured Motion In Future-avoiding Random Walks
authors: A. Schmaus, K. Stiller, And N. Molkenthin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Schmaus, K. Stiller, and N. Molkenthin

Self-avoiding random walks on graphs can be seen as walkers interacting with their own past history. Here, we consider a complementary class of dynamics, mutual future-avoiding random walks (MFARWs), where stochastically driven walkers are avoiding each other's planned future trajectories. Such syst…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044219] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes mutual future-avoiding random walks, a classical stochastic graph dynamics where walkers avoid each other's planned future trajectories, leading to coexistence of periodic and unstructured motion.
motivation: Self-avoiding random walks model walkers interacting with their own past; the authors study the complementary case where walkers interact by avoiding each other's future paths.
method: The authors define mutual future-avoiding random walks on graphs and analyze the resulting dynamics, likely using stochastic models and graph-theoretic or statistical-physics techniques.
result: The dynamics exhibit both periodic and unstructured motion phases that can emerge and coexist depending on parameters and graph structure.
conclusion: Future-avoiding walk dynamics provide a distinct class of history-dependent stochastic processes with rich collective behavior, but the work is classical and not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Plasma Density Manipulation In Staged Discharge Capillaries For Plasma-based Accelerators
authors: Angelo Biagioni, Lucio Crincoli, Romain Demitra, Mario Galletti, Valerio Lollo, Donato Pellegrini, Riccardo Pompili, Massimo Ferrario, And Arie Zigler
abstract:
Author(s): Angelo Biagioni, Lucio Crincoli, Romain Demitra, Mario Galletti, Valerio Lollo, Donato Pellegrini, Riccardo Pompili, Massimo Ferrario, and Arie Zigler

Plasma wakefield acceleration of charged particle beams relies on specialized devices for plasma generation and confinement. In both particle-driven wakefield acceleration and beam-focusing experiments, these devices are designed to precisely control plasma properties to optimize beam-plasma interac…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045210] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports on staged discharge capillaries for controlling plasma density profiles used in plasma wakefield accelerators.
motivation: Plasma wakefield acceleration requires precise control of plasma density and confinement in order to optimize beam-plasma interactions for particle-driven acceleration and beam-focusing experiments.
method: Staged capillary discharge devices are developed and characterized to manipulate the plasma density profile along the acceleration channel.
result: The devices enable controlled plasma density manipulation relevant to optimizing wakefield acceleration and beam focusing.
conclusion: Staged discharge capillaries offer a practical route to tailored plasma density profiles for plasma-based accelerator applications.

title: Microfluidic Oscillatory Rheology Of Transported Soft Particles
authors: Matteo Milani, Joshua D. Mcgraw, Anke Lindner, And Stefano Aime
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Milani, Joshua D. McGraw, Anke Lindner, and Stefano Aime

Shape-optimized microfluidic channels enable high-throughput characterization of microscopic soft matter, providing precise spatiotemporal stress fields to bridge bulk mechanical measurements and single-particle dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041005] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Shape-optimized microfluidic channels are used to perform oscillatory rheology on soft microscopic particles with well-controlled spatiotemporal stress fields.
motivation: Bridging bulk mechanical measurements of soft matter with single-particle dynamics requires high-throughput techniques that provide precise, well-defined stress fields at the microscale.
method: Microfluidic channels with optimized geometries generate oscillatory stress fields, enabling high-throughput characterization of transported soft particles and simultaneous tracking of their deformation dynamics.
result: The approach yields precise spatiotemporal stress control and allows direct linking of single-particle mechanical response to bulk rheological behavior.
conclusion: The platform offers a versatile tool for soft-matter microrheology, though it lies entirely in classical fluid mechanics and materials characterization.

title: Comparing Different Physics Fields Using Statistical Linguistics
authors: María Fernanda Sánchez-Puig, Carlos Gershenson, And Carlos Pineda
abstract:
Author(s): María Fernanda Sánchez-Puig, Carlos Gershenson, and Carlos Pineda

The large digital archives of the American Physical Society (APS) offer an opportunity to quantitatively analyze the structure and evolution of scientific communication. In this paper, we perform a comparative analysis of the language used in eight APS journals (Phys. Rev. A, B, C, D, E, Lett., X, R…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044320] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-linguistics comparison of the language used across eight APS journals to characterize the structure and evolution of scientific communication.
motivation: Large digital archives such as those of the APS enable quantitative, corpus-level study of how scientific subfields differ in writing style and how their language evolves over time.
method: Corpus-based statistical linguistics applied to text from Phys. Rev. A, B, C, D, E, Lett., X and R, using lexical and frequency-based measures to contrast the journals.
result: The authors identify systematic linguistic differences between the journals, reflecting disciplinary conventions and the internal structure of physics subcommunities.
conclusion: Statistical linguistics offers a quantitative lens on scientific communication, but the work is bibliometric/scientometric rather than physics or quantum-information research.

title: Minimal Network Of Brain Dynamics: Hierarchy Of Approximations To Quasicritical Neural Network Dynamics
authors: Jeremy B. Goetz, Naruepon Weerawongphrom, Rashid V. Williams-García, John M. Beggs, And Gerardo Ortiz
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy B. Goetz, Naruepon Weerawongphrom, Rashid V. Williams-García, John M. Beggs, and Gerardo Ortiz

We present an interacting model of neural network dynamics that incorporates key biological features, including multiple forms of inhibitory interactions. We develop a hierarchy of analytical mean-field approximations to characterize nonequilibrium phase transitions between ordered, disordered, and …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044321] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The authors build an interacting model of neural network dynamics with multiple inhibitory interaction types and derive a hierarchy of mean-field approximations to describe nonequilibrium phase transitions between ordered, disordered, and quasicritical regimes.
motivation: Biological neural networks exhibit quasicritical dynamics that are difficult to capture analytically, and existing models often neglect the diversity of inhibitory interactions present in real cortex.
method: An interacting neural network model incorporating several forms of inhibition is analyzed via a hierarchy of analytical mean-field approximations, comparing successive levels of approximation against the phase structure.
result: The hierarchy of mean-field treatments characterizes nonequilibrium phase transitions among ordered, disordered, and quasicritical states and identifies a minimal network description reproducing the key dynamics.
conclusion: A reduced interacting network model with structured inhibition suffices to capture quasicritical neural dynamics, providing an analytically tractable framework for brain-network criticality.

title: Space-time Correlations Of Passive Scalars In Colored-noise Flows
authors: Long Wang And Guowei He
abstract:
Author(s): Long Wang and Guowei He

The space-time correlation of a passive scalar advected by a Gaussian colored-noise velocity with wavenumber-dependent correlation times and power-law spatial spectra is investigated in the present paper. Within the inertial-convective subrange, we derive an analytical solution for the space-time co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045106] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives analytical space-time correlations for a passive scalar advected by Gaussian colored-noise velocity fields with power-law spectra.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how colored-noise advection with wavenumber-dependent correlation times shapes passive-scalar space-time statistics in the inertial-convective subrange.
method: They model the velocity as Gaussian colored noise with power-law spatial spectra and solve analytically for the passive-scalar space-time correlation within the inertial-convective subrange.
result: An analytical expression for the space-time correlation is obtained, revealing how spectral exponent and correlation-time scaling control the scalar's temporal decorrelation.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into passive-scalar turbulence in colored-noise flows, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Multibody Interactions Activate Liquid State Of Acoustically Levitated Particle Ensembles
authors: Nina M. Brown And Heinrich M. Jaeger
abstract:
Author(s): Nina M. Brown and Heinrich M. Jaeger

Nonreciprocal forces are often a consequence of asymmetry in the properties of the interacting objects. However, even if all objects are identical and isotropic, and the pairwise interactions between two objects are completely reciprocal, nonreciprocal forces can still appear when an arrangement of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043105] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that nonreciprocal multibody interactions can drive an acoustically levitated ensemble of identical particles into a liquid-like state.
motivation: The authors investigate how nonreciprocity can emerge even when individual objects are identical and pairwise interactions are reciprocal, focusing on collective behavior in levitated particle ensembles.
method: They use acoustic levitation to assemble particles and analyze the resulting multibody interactions and emergent collective dynamics.
result: Nonreciprocal forces arising from the arrangement activate a liquid state of the particle ensemble.
conclusion: Collective nonreciprocity can produce fluid-like behavior in levitated granular or colloidal systems, with implications for classical active matter.

title: Stressing And Probing With Light: A Thermo-optical Investigation Of Soft Solids
authors: Rafael Gervasone, Arianna Erba, Roberto Piazza, And Stefano Buzzaccaro
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael Gervasone, Arianna Erba, Roberto Piazza, and Stefano Buzzaccaro

Internal stresses in arrested soft solids can be generated not only by mechanical loading but also by spatially nonuniform temperature fields, which impose incompatible thermal strains and activate coupled thermoelastic and poroelastic responses. Here, we introduce an all-optical stress-and-probe pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043112] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an all-optical stress-and-probe technique to study internal stresses generated by nonuniform temperature fields in arrested soft solids, revealing coupled thermoelastic and poroelastic responses.
motivation: Internal stresses in soft solids can arise not only from mechanical loading but also from spatially nonuniform temperature fields that impose incompatible thermal strains, and existing methods lack a purely optical way to both generate and probe these stresses.
method: The authors develop an all-optical stressing-and-probing platform, using light to create localized heating-induced thermal strain fields while optically measuring the resulting deformation and stress response in soft solid samples.
result: The experiments reveal distinct thermoelastic and poroelastic relaxation signatures, showing how thermal gradients activate coupled mechanical responses in arrested soft solids.
conclusion: Light-induced thermal stressing combined with optical probing provides a versatile, contactless route to characterize stress and poroelasticity in soft matter systems.

title: Evaluating Criteria For Bubbling In Coupled Chaotic Oscillators
authors: Giulio Tirabassi, Raul de Palma Aristides, Cristina Masoller, And Daniel J. Gauthier
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Tirabassi, Raul de Palma Aristides, Cristina Masoller, and Daniel J. Gauthier

The stability of the synchronized state of coupled time-varying systems can be predicted with good accuracy for noiseless identical oscillators. Such an assumption, however, is unrealistic for real systems where small heterogeneity and noise are always present. In the case of chaotic oscillators, sm…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043102] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper evaluates criteria for the bubbling instability in coupled chaotic oscillators under realistic conditions with noise and parameter heterogeneity.
motivation: Synchronization stability of coupled chaotic systems is well understood for ideal noiseless identical oscillators, but real systems contain noise and heterogeneity that can invalidate standard predictions.
method: The authors analyze coupled chaotic oscillator models and assess criteria for bubbling, likely combining stability analysis with numerical simulations under noise and parameter mismatch.
result: The study identifies how well existing bubbling criteria perform when noise and heterogeneity are present and clarifies their limitations.
conclusion: The work refines the understanding of synchronization stability and bubbling in coupled chaotic oscillators, but it is a classical nonlinear-dynamics study with no direct quantum-information or quantum-thermodynamics connection.

title: Improved Electron Beam Stability In Laser Wakefield Acceleration Through Control Of Laser Angular Chirp And Wavefront Stability
authors: Zhan Jin, Yan-Jun Gu, Shingo Sato, Nobuhiko Nakanii, Kai Huang, Izuru Daito, Toshiya Muto, Yoshio Mizuta, Szuba Wojciech, Masaki Kando, And Tomonao Hosokai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhan Jin, Yan-Jun Gu, Shingo Sato, Nobuhiko Nakanii, Kai Huang, Izuru Daito, Toshiya Muto, Yoshio Mizuta, Szuba Wojciech, Masaki Kando, and Tomonao Hosokai

Stable operation of laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA) is essential for future applications of compact radiation sources and advanced accelerators. In this work, we investigate stabilization of LWFA electron beams through control of laser angular chirp and wavefront stability. We show that angular …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043090] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: This work stabilizes electron beams from laser wakefield acceleration by controlling laser angular chirp and wavefront stability.
motivation: Laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA) promises compact radiation sources and advanced accelerators, but its practical use requires stable, reproducible electron beams that are currently limited by laser fluctuations.
method: The authors experimentally investigate how tuning laser angular chirp and actively maintaining wavefront stability affect the shot-to-shot pointing, energy, and charge stability of LWFA electron beams.
result: Controlling angular chirp and suppressing wavefront aberrations is shown to improve the stability of the accelerated electron beams, reducing fluctuations in beam parameters.
conclusion: Careful laser pulse-front and wavefront control is an effective route toward stable LWFA operation, relevant for future compact accelerator and radiation-source applications.

title: Cosmological And High-Energy Physics Implications From Gravitational-Wave Background Searches In LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s O1–O4a Runs
authors: A. G. Abac et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. G. Abac et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration)

Numerous well-motivated particle-physics-based models are constrained using the most recent LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041023] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic gravitational-wave background searches from O1-O4a are used to constrain cosmological and high-energy particle-physics models.
motivation: A stochastic gravitational-wave background offers a unique probe of early-Universe cosmology and beyond-Standard-Model physics, motivating constraints from the latest observing runs.
method: Cross-correlation searches for an isotropic stochastic background in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O1-O4a data are interpreted against a broad set of well-motivated cosmological and particle-physics model predictions.
result: Upper limits on the stochastic background amplitude translate into constraints on numerous cosmological and high-energy physics scenarios, ruling out or bounding their parameter spaces.
conclusion: Gravitational-wave background searches provide competitive, complementary constraints on early-Universe and particle physics models, with sensitivity expected to improve in future runs.

title: Orientation-Dependent Structural Phase Transitions And Melting In Shock-Compressed MgO
authors: Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, And June K. Wicks
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, and June K. Wicks

Shockwave observations resolve the high pressure structural transition and melting temperature of MgO, a critical planetary building block.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041019] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Shock-compression experiments and analysis resolve the high-pressure structural phase transition and melting curve of MgO, a key planetary constituent.
motivation: MgO is a major building block of rocky planetary interiors, so its high-pressure phase diagram and melting behavior are needed to model super-Earth mantles and shock-processing of planetary materials.
method: Laser-driven shock wave experiments (with velocimetry diagnostics) combined with structural analysis to identify phase boundaries and melt onset along the Hugoniot, including orientation-dependent effects.
result: The authors map an orientation-dependent structural transition and determine the melting temperature of MgO at extreme shock pressures, refining the high-pressure phase diagram.
conclusion: The findings constrain planetary interior models and equation-of-state tables for MgO under dynamic compression conditions.

title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism In Hematite
authors: Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, And Tsuyoshi Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, and Tsuyoshi Kimura

X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041015] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports electric-field-induced X-ray nonreciprocal dichroism in hematite, revealing hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles supported by theoretical calculations.
motivation: The authors aim to detect and characterize hidden higher-order magnetic multipole order in hematite using electric-field-controlled X-ray absorption spectroscopy.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy is performed under an applied electric field, with experimental dichroism signatures interpreted through theoretical calculations.
result: The measurements uncover signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite, and theory supports the observed nonreciprocal dichroism.
conclusion: Electric-field-induced X-ray nonreciprocal dichroism provides a probe of hidden magnetic multipole order in hematite, with implications for understanding complex magnetic ordering in condensed matter.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates memory effects in microfluidic flow networks using soft elastic fibers that act as fluidic hysterons via flow-structure feedback.
motivation: It aims to understand how history-dependent behavior and memory can emerge in fluidic networks from mechanical feedback rather than electronic or quantum components.
method: The authors study soft elastic fibers inside microfluidic channels and analyze the coupled flow-structure interactions that produce hysteretic states.
result: They show that the fibers create fluidic hysterons and enable memory of previous flow actions in the network.
conclusion: Such flow-based memory may provide a classical mechanical route to history-dependent fluidic computation or sensing, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Programmable Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulator In Twisted Crystalline Flatbands [Phys. Rev. X 16, 011015 (2026)]
authors: Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, and Xiaobo Lu
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum notice correcting the authors' earlier paper on a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator realized in twisted crystalline flatbands.
motivation: The original work aimed to demonstrate a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator in twisted crystalline flatband systems, and the erratum serves to correct errors in that published record.
method: Erratum corrections to a condensed-matter transport/characterization study of twisted crystalline flatbands; no new quantum-information methodology is presented.
result: The erratum reports corrections to the original Phys. Rev. X article; the substantive physics concerns quantum anomalous Hall effect, not quantum information or thermodynamics.
conclusion: The paper is a condensed-matter erratum with no direct bearing on quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, enabling potential mechanical computing applications.
motivation: The work explores mechanically recoverable nanostructured materials as a platform for memory and computing beyond conventional electronic implementations.
method: The authors characterize the constitutive mechanical response of vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams and identify return point memory behavior.
result: The foams show return point memory in their mechanical response, indicating stable history-dependent states that can be used for mechanical memory.
conclusion: Such elastically recoverable nanostructured materials may open new opportunities for mechanical computing, though the work is outside quantum information science.

title: Exact Geometric Optics Of Parabolic Mirrors: The Angular Caustic And Geometric Stability Analysis
authors: Luciano Medina And Eric Davis
abstract:
Author(s): Luciano Medina and Eric Davis

We derive an analytical solution for the angular caustic in parabolic mirrors, extending geometric optics beyond the paraxial approximation. By solving the ray-mapping equations for the parabolic profile, we determine the topology of the critical ray manifold. We find that the focal singularity is n…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043530] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive exact analytical solutions for the angular caustic of parabolic mirrors beyond the paraxial approximation and analyze the geometric stability of the critical ray manifold.
motivation: Paraxial approximations break down for strongly curved or wide-aperture parabolic mirrors, so an exact description of caustic topology and focal singularity structure is needed for precise optical design and aberration analysis.
method: Ray-mapping equations for the parabolic profile are solved analytically to determine the topology of the critical ray manifold, followed by a geometric stability analysis of the caustic structure.
result: An exact closed-form expression for the angular caustic is obtained, revealing a modified topology of the focal singularity relative to paraxial predictions.
conclusion: The exact treatment provides a rigorous geometric-optics account of parabolic mirror focusing that departs from paraxial results, with implications for the design of wide-aperture reflective optics.

title: Local Noise Shielding Guides The Separation Of Binary Chiral Mixtures
authors: Qi Zhou, Yuan-Rui Wang, Peng Wang, Jie Huo, And Xu-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Zhou, Yuan-Rui Wang, Peng Wang, Jie Huo, and Xu-Ming Wang

The efficient separation of chiral particles is a crucial topic in active matter, where intrinsic rotational motion can generate rich nonequilibrium collective behaviors. So far, few investigations have explored the separation of binary chiral mixtures by guiding particle motion through local noise …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045416] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how locally applied noise can be used to guide and separate binary mixtures of chiral active particles.
motivation: Efficient separation of chiral particles is important in active matter, yet few works have examined how local noise can be exploited to sort binary chiral mixtures.
method: The authors presumably model chiral active particles with intrinsic rotational motion and numerically or analytically examine the effect of spatially localized noise on particle transport and separation.
result: Local noise is shown to guide particle motion in a way that enables spatial separation of the two chiral species.
conclusion: Local noise shielding provides a viable mechanism for chiral separation in nonequilibrium active matter systems.

title: Heterogeneous Ice Nucleation With TIP4P/Ice: The Role Of Lattice Mismatch
authors: M. Camarillo, J. Oller-Iscar, M. M. Conde, J. Ramírez, S. Blazquez, And E. Sanz
abstract:
Author(s): M. Camarillo, J. Oller-Iscar, M. M. Conde, J. Ramírez, S. Blazquez, and E. Sanz

Ice formation, a crucial phase transition for life on Earth, mainly occurs through heterogeneous nucleation on a solid substrate. Despite the importance of this phenomenon, the correlation between the structure of the substrate and its ability to induce ice nucleation remains poorly understood. In t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045418] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Classical molecular dynamics simulations with TIP4P/Ice examine how substrate lattice mismatch controls heterogeneous ice nucleation.
motivation: Heterogeneous ice nucleation is important in atmospheric and environmental science, but the relationship between substrate structure and ice-nucleating ability remains poorly understood.
method: The authors use TIP4P/Ice water models to simulate ice nucleation on solid substrates and analyze the role of lattice mismatch between the substrate and ice.
result: The study relates substrate lattice mismatch to nucleation behavior and identifies structural features that promote or inhibit heterogeneous ice formation.
conclusion: Lattice mismatch is a key factor in heterogeneous ice nucleation, providing microscopic insight for understanding and possibly designing ice-nucleating surfaces.

title: Experimental Observation Of Drift Acoustic Cnoidal Waves In A Magnetized Plasma
authors: Tanmay Karmakar, Rosh Roy, Lavkesh Lachhvani, Raju Daniel, Bhoomi Khodiyar, Prabal K. Chattopadhyay, Abhijit Sen, And Sayak Bose
abstract:
Author(s): Tanmay Karmakar, Rosh Roy, Lavkesh Lachhvani, Raju Daniel, Bhoomi Khodiyar, Prabal K. Chattopadhyay, Abhijit Sen, and Sayak Bose

We report the experimental observation of highly nonlinear coherent structures in a linear magnetized plasma characterized by a strong background density gradient and significant [MATH] velocity shear under high ion-neutral collisionality. These structures, identified as drift acous…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045211] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of drift acoustic cnoidal waves in a magnetized plasma with density gradients and velocity shear.
motivation: The work seeks to characterize strongly nonlinear coherent plasma structures under high ion-neutral collisionality in a linear magnetized plasma device.
method: The authors perform plasma experiments in a linear magnetized plasma with a strong background density gradient and significant velocity shear, identifying nonlinear coherent structures as drift acoustic cnoidal waves.
result: Highly nonlinear coherent structures consistent with drift acoustic cnoidal waves are experimentally observed.
conclusion: The findings provide experimental evidence for drift acoustic cnoidal wave formation in magnetized plasmas, but the topic lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unambiguous Characterization Of In-plane Dielectric Response In Nanoconfined Liquids: Water As A Case Study
authors: Jon Zubeltzu
abstract:
Author(s): Jon Zubeltzu

The in-plane dielectric constant of nanoconfined water has attracted growing interest in recent years. Nevertheless, assigning a bulklike dielectric constant to a molecularly thin film is convention dependent because it requires choosing an effective water width. We propose the in-plane 2D polarizab…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045505] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a convention-independent 2D in-plane polarizability to characterize the dielectric response of molecularly thin nanoconfined water films.
motivation: Assigning a bulklike dielectric constant to a molecularly thin water film is ambiguous because it requires an arbitrary choice of effective water width, so a width-independent descriptor is needed.
method: Classical molecular simulation/statistical-mechanical analysis of nanoconfined water, defining an in-plane 2D polarizability and comparing it with conventional bulklike dielectric constant assignments.
result: The 2D polarizability provides an unambiguous, convention-free quantification of the in-plane dielectric response, resolving the width-dependence ambiguity of effective dielectric constants.
conclusion: The 2D polarizability framework offers a cleaner route to characterize dielectric behavior in nanoconfined liquids, with water serving as the demonstrative case study.

title: Contraction-deformation Coupling Enables The Wave-driven Morphodynamics And Mode-locking Of Confined Active Gel Droplets
authors: Ryota Sakamoto And Arash Abedijaberi
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Sakamoto and Arash Abedijaberi

Wavelike patterns play fundamental roles in living systems, from single cells to cell collectives, organizing essential functions from wound repair to morphogenesis. While biochemical waves are well established, it remains unclear how the force propagation of cytoskeletal contraction waves regulates…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043109] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows how coupling between contraction and deformation in confined active gel droplets produces wave-driven morphodynamics and mode-locking of oscillatory patterns.
motivation: Wavelike patterns are central to living systems, but it is unclear how force propagation from cytoskeletal contraction waves regulates shape dynamics in confined active materials.
method: The authors model/analyze confined active gel droplets in which contractile activity is coupled to mechanical deformation, and characterize the resulting wave patterns and their locking behavior.
result: Contraction-deformation coupling generates self-organized waves whose dynamics become mode-locked under confinement, dictating droplet morphology.
conclusion: Mechanical feedback between contraction and deformation is a key organizing principle for spatiotemporal patterning in active gel systems.

title: Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic Phases With Orthogonal And Tilted Structures
authors: Jordan Hobbs, Calum J. Gibb, William C. Ogle, Peter Medle Rupnik, Natan Osterman, Nerea Sebastián, Alenka Mertelj, And Richard. J. Mandle
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Hobbs, Calum J. Gibb, William C. Ogle, Peter Medle Rupnik, Natan Osterman, Nerea Sebastián, Alenka Mertelj, and Richard. J. Mandle

The discovery of the ferroelectric nematic phase has brought with it a plethora of new polar liquid crystalline (LC) phases. One in particular is the antiferroelectric smectic A [MATH] phase. In this article, we show via observation and analysis of satellite peak…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043085] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports modulated antiferroelectric smectic liquid-crystal phases with orthogonal and tilted structures, analyzed via satellite peak observations.
motivation: The discovery of ferroelectric nematic phases has motivated the search for related polar liquid-crystalline phases, including antiferroelectric smectic A phases.
method: The authors use observation and analysis of satellite peaks to characterize modulated antiferroelectric smectic phases and distinguish orthogonal versus tilted structures.
result: The study identifies and describes modulated antiferroelectric smectic phases with orthogonal and tilted arrangements, providing structural evidence from diffraction or scattering satellite peaks.
conclusion: The work expands the family of polar liquid-crystalline phases and clarifies the structural behavior of modulated antiferroelectric smectic systems.

title: Observation Of Electroweak Production Of Pairs Of $z$ Bosons In Proton-Proton Collisions At 13 TeV
authors: A. Gevorgyan et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Gevorgyan et al. (CMS Collaboration)

The first evidence of electroweak (EW) production of pairs of [MATH] bosons in association with two jets (jj) in the final state [MATH], where [MATH], [MATH], is reported by the CMS experiment. The analysis is based on a data sample of proton-proton ([MATH]) collisions at $=1…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181801] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The CMS experiment reports the first evidence for electroweak production of a pair of Z bosons in association with two jets in 13 TeV proton-proton collisions.
motivation: Electroweak diboson production with two jets probes the quartic gauge couplings and vector boson scattering sector of the Standard Model, testing the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking.
method: Analysis of CMS proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV, selecting final states with a Z boson pair and two forward jets, with backgrounds estimated from data and simulation and the EW signal extracted via multivariate or fit-based techniques.
result: The electroweak ZZjj production process is observed with a significance establishing first evidence, consistent with Standard Model predictions within uncertainties.
conclusion: This measurement provides the first evidence for electroweak ZZ production in association with two jets, constraining anomalous quartic gauge couplings and vector boson scattering.

title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement Of $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ Confronts Ab Initio Theory
authors: Kristian König, Patrick Müller, Tobias Gesser, Emily Burbach, Stefano Gandolfi, Matthias Heinz, Phillip Imgram, Alessandro Lovato, Pieter Maris, Takayuki Miyagi, Wilfried Nörtershäuser, Robert Roth, Achim Schwenk, And Julien Spahn
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian König, Patrick Müller, Tobias Gesser, Emily Burbach, Stefano Gandolfi, Matthias Heinz, Phillip Imgram, Alessandro Lovato, Pieter Maris, Takayuki Miyagi, Wilfried Nörtershäuser, Robert Roth, Achim Schwenk, and Julien Spahn

Located at the neutron shell closure [MATH], the long-lived radioactive isotope [MATH] plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of [MATH] has remained less precisely known than that of its stable …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 182501] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: A precision laser-spectroscopy measurement of the 14C nuclear charge radius is compared against ab initio nuclear structure calculations to test modern nuclear forces.
motivation: 14C sits at the N=8 neutron shell closure and is widely used in geochronology, yet its charge radius was known far less precisely than those of neighboring stable isotopes, limiting benchmarks for ab initio theory.
method: Collinear laser spectroscopy on the long-lived radioactive isotope yields an accurate charge radius, which is then confronted with ab initio calculations using chiral effective field theory interactions and many-body solvers.
result: The improved charge radius deviates from some ab initio predictions, exposing tensions in the description of the 14C nucleus and in the employed nuclear interactions.
conclusion: The measurement provides a sharp new benchmark for nuclear theory and highlights where current ab initio methods and interactions require refinement.

title: Using The Force Landscape Of An Active Solid To Predict Plastic Deformation
authors: Tyler Hain, Edan Lerner, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler Hain, Edan Lerner, and M. Lisa Manning

Nonactive disordered solids feature quasilocalized excitations that control plasticity, similar to crystal lattice defects, identified via harmonic or anharmonic analyses of the potential energy landscape. We extend this idea to active matter, focusing on dense packings of self-propelled rods. We ge…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 188301] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors extend the potential-energy-landscape framework for disordered solids to active matter, using a force landscape to identify quasilocalized excitations that predict plastic deformation in dense packings of self-propelled rods.
motivation: In passive disordered solids, quasilocalized excitations identified from the potential energy landscape control plasticity, analogous to crystal defects; the authors ask whether an analogous force-landscape construction can predict plastic rearrangements in active, self-driven systems.
method: They construct a force landscape for dense packings of self-propelled rods and Ge them to locate soft, quasilocalized modes, then correlate these excitations with subsequent plastic deformation events in simulations.
result: The force-landscape-derived excitations successfully predict where plastic deformation occurs in the active solid, showing that landscape-based structure-property relations carry over from passive to active disordered solids.
conclusion: Force-landscape analysis provides a predictive tool for plasticity in active matter, generalizing the quasilocalized-excitation picture of deformation beyond equilibrium disordered solids.

title: Topological Defects In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Aaron L. Galper, Henrik N. Barck, Conor M. Floyd, Elliot A. Snyder, Charlie J. Schofield, Sorin A. P. Jayaweera, Ian G. Mcguire, And Sharon J. Gerbode
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron L. Galper, Henrik N. Barck, Conor M. Floyd, Elliot A. Snyder, Charlie J. Schofield, Sorin A. P. Jayaweera, Ian G. McGuire, and Sharon J. Gerbode

When colloidal particles in single layer have some space to move up or down, they can form a buckled crystal. Two kinds of translational order, a nearly triangular lattice and a frustrated pattern of up and down particles, have defects whose interaction affects the evolution of the system.

#SoftMatterSpotlight #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045417] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: This soft-matter experiment/theory study examines how topological defects interact in buckled colloidal monolayers that exhibit two competing translational orders.
motivation: Colloidal monolayers with out-of-plane freedom can buckle into crystals with competing up/down and triangular ordering, and the role of defects in the evolution of such frustrated order is not well understood.
method: The authors combine experiment and theory to characterize the defects arising in the nearly triangular lattice and the frustrated up/down checkerboard-like pattern, and analyze their interactions.
result: Two kinds of translational order are identified, each hosting defects whose mutual interaction governs how the buckled crystal evolves.
conclusion: Defect interaction is a key driver of the structural evolution in buckled colloidal monolayers, with implications for the design and control of frustrated colloidal materials.

title: Landau Theory Applied To Antiferroelectric Ordering In Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals
authors: Manisha Badu, Arjun Ghimire, Milon, Priyanka Kumari, Hari Krishna Bisoyi, Oleg D. Lavrentovich, James Gleeson, Antal Jakli, And Samuel Sprunt
abstract:
Author(s): Manisha Badu, Arjun Ghimire, Milon, Priyanka Kumari, Hari Krishna Bisoyi, Oleg D. Lavrentovich, James Gleeson, Antal Jakli, and Samuel Sprunt

The polarization and mass density modulation associated with antiferroelectric ordering in two ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals, a prototypical single compound (referred to as DIO) and a commercial mixture (FNLC919), are studied experimentally as a function of temperature. The wave number of th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043097] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies antiferroelectric ordering in ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals using Landau theory and temperature-dependent polarization/density modulation measurements.
motivation: The work aims to understand the antiferroelectric phase behavior and modulation wave number in prototypical and commercial ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals.
method: The authors measure polarization and mass density modulation as functions of temperature in DIO and FNLC919, analyzing the results within a Landau-theoretical framework.
result: They characterize the temperature dependence of the modulation wave number and associated order parameters for antiferroelectric ordering in these liquid-crystal systems.
conclusion: The findings clarify the antiferroelectric ordering behavior in ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039 (2026)]
authors: Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, And Nicole Abaid
abstract:
Author(s): Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, and Nicole Abaid
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 049002] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the published article on the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion.
motivation: The original work analyzes how cluster structure in a classical flocking model evolves across scales, and the erratum corrects errors in that published analysis.
method: Purely a correction notice; the underlying study uses Vicsek-model simulations and topological/geometric cluster characterization.
result: The erratum reports corrections to the original Phys. Rev. Research article (8, 033039); no new quantum results are presented.
conclusion: The paper concerns classical active-matter flocking and has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: BESIII observes transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations near threshold, studying its production and decay dynamics.
motivation: Charmed baryon polarization probes the strong-interaction dynamics of baryon production, a poorly understood aspect of hadron formation in e+e- collisions.
method: Analysis of BESIII detector data on e+e- annihilation events near the Λc+Λ̄c- threshold, extracting the Λc+ transverse polarization from angular distributions of its decay products.
result: A nonzero transverse polarization of the Λc+ is observed, indicating nontrivial spin dynamics in the production process near threshold.
conclusion: The measurement provides constraints on models of baryon production and spin correlations in the charmed-baryon sector.

title: Tipping Points Of The Ocean Oxygen: A Dynamical Systems Perspective
authors: Amer Alsulami And Sergei Petrovskii
abstract:
Author(s): Amer Alsulami and Sergei Petrovskii

Ocean oxygen as a potential Earth tipping element has been largely overlooked in the literature. This Perspective argues that a dynamical systems approach complemented with a mathematical model accounting for the oxygen production by phytoplankton photosynthesis can provide a valuable insight into this issue.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041006] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective argues that ocean oxygen should be treated as a potential Earth tipping element and that dynamical-systems modeling of phytoplankton oxygen production can illuminate its behavior.
motivation: Ocean oxygen is largely overlooked as a possible Earth tipping element despite its importance for planetary habitability and marine ecosystems.
method: The authors propose a dynamical-systems perspective complemented by a mathematical model that accounts for oxygen production by phytoplankton photosynthesis.
result: The paper argues that such a modeling approach can provide valuable insight into ocean-oxygen tipping-point dynamics, though no specific quantitative results are given in the abstract.
conclusion: A dynamical-systems framework incorporating phytoplankton oxygen production is advocated as a useful direction for understanding potential ocean deoxygenation tipping points.

title: Closing The Mass Window For Stupendously Large Black Holes
authors: Christopher Gerlach, Yann Gouttenoire, Antonio J. Iovino, And Nicholas Leister
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Gerlach, Yann Gouttenoire, Antonio J. Iovino, and Nicholas Leister

Primordial black holes heavier than
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 181401] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: Primordial black holes heavier than about 10^10 solar masses are ruled out as dark matter because their isocurvature perturbations exceed cosmic microwave background limits.
motivation: The paper tests whether stupendously large primordial black holes can constitute dark matter without violating existing cosmological constraints.
method: The authors compute the isocurvature perturbations generated by supermassive primordial black holes and compare them with current CMB bounds.
result: Black holes above a mass threshold produce isocurvature perturbations exceeding observational limits, closing the mass window for this dark matter candidate.
conclusion: Stupendously large primordial black holes cannot be the dark matter, tightening constraints on primordial black hole dark matter models.

title: Geometry-induced Shifts In Dielectric-loss Peaks Of Amorphous Ices
authors: Kaito Sasaki And Yoshiharu Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Kaito Sasaki and Yoshiharu Suzuki

Dielectric relaxation times of powdered amorphous ices have served as kinetic benchmarks for the glass dynamics of water. To examine the effect of sample geometry on the dielectric spectra, we measured in situ dielectric spectra of bulk and emulsified high- and low-density amorphous ices at $P≃0.01\…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L043402] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how sample geometry affects dielectric-loss peaks in bulk and emulsified amorphous ices.
motivation: Dielectric relaxation times of powdered amorphous ices are used as kinetic benchmarks for water glass dynamics, so the authors examine whether sample geometry distorts the measured dielectric spectra.
method: They perform in situ dielectric spectroscopy on bulk and emulsified high- and low-density amorphous ices at low pressure and compare the resulting relaxation spectra.
result: The dielectric-loss peaks shift depending on sample geometry, indicating that geometric effects must be accounted for when interpreting dielectric relaxation data of amorphous ices.
conclusion: Geometry-induced shifts are relevant for benchmarking glass dynamics of water using dielectric spectroscopy of amorphous ice samples.

title: From Localized Discharge To Distributed Granular Filtration On An Inclined Mesh
authors: Javier Pillado, Valérie Vidal, Nicolás Taberlet, And Germán Varas
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Pillado, Valérie Vidal, Nicolás Taberlet, and Germán Varas

Granular discharge through a single orifice is classically described by the Beverloo law, but this localized geometry becomes prone to clogging when the aperture size [MATH] is only a few grain diameters [MATH]. Here, we study dry avalanches of monodisperse glass beads over an inclined perforated mesh as …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045411] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how dry granular avalanches of monodisperse glass beads flow and clog over an inclined perforated mesh, moving from localized orifice discharge to distributed granular filtration.
motivation: Classical Beverloo-law descriptions of granular discharge through a single orifice break down when the aperture is only a few grain diameters wide, where clogging dominates; the authors ask how flow behavior changes when discharge is instead distributed over many apertures on an inclined mesh.
method: Experiments on dry avalanches of monodisperse glass beads flowing down an inclined perforated plate, with systematic variation of mesh aperture size relative to grain diameter, analyzed through discharge rates and clogging statistics.
result: The transition from localized single-orifice-like discharge to a distributed filtration regime is characterized, showing how aperture-to-grain size ratio and inclination control flow rate and clogging probability.
conclusion: The findings extend granular discharge phenomenology beyond the Beverloo regime and provide design guidance for sieving and filtration geometries with many small apertures.

title: Periodic Modulation Of The Space-filling Nature Of The Turbulent Flame Leads To Periodic Spiky Heat Release Oscillations
authors: Sivakumar Sudarsanan, Manikandan Raghunathan, Shwetha Viswesh, And R. I. Sujith
abstract:
Author(s): Sivakumar Sudarsanan, Manikandan Raghunathan, Shwetha Viswesh, and R. I. Sujith

Spiky oscillations are characterized by slow-fast dynamics and are observed in excitable media such as neuronal membranes and cardiac cells. In a turbulent reactive flow system, we observe that the heat release rate exhibits self-sustained periodic, spiky oscillations in synchrony with the sinusoida…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045105] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Turbulent reactive flow experiments show that periodic modulation of the flame's space-filling nature produces self-sustained spiky, slow-fast heat-release oscillations analogous to excitable media.
motivation: Spiky slow-fast oscillations are well known in excitable biological media, but whether turbulent flames can exhibit such self-sustained excitable dynamics and how they synchronize with imposed modulation is unclear.
method: Analysis of heat-release-rate time series from a turbulent reactive flow (combustion) system under sinusoidal acoustic/flow forcing, characterizing the spiky waveform and slow-fast dynamics.
result: The heat release rate oscillates periodically in a spiky, slow-fast manner in synchrony with the sinusoidal modulation; the spikiness is tied to periodic changes in the space-filling character of the turbulent flame.
conclusion: Turbulent flames can behave as excitable media with modulated slow-fast dynamics, offering a dynamical-systems view of thermoacoustic oscillation generation.

title: Connectivity, Rigidity, And Gelation In Linker-mediated Colloidal Networks
authors: Taejin Kwon, Murari Singh, Javier Alejandro Sanchez-Gallegos, Román Perdomo-Pérez, Ramón Castañeda-Priego, And Thomas M. Truskett
abstract:
Author(s): Taejin Kwon, Murari Singh, Javier Alejandro Sanchez-Gallegos, Román Perdomo-Pérez, Ramón Castañeda-Priego, and Thomas M. Truskett

Using molecular dynamics simulations, the authors explore gelation in colloids tied together by reversible linkers. They find that different connectivity measures govern ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation.

#AdvancingField #WellStructured #SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045408] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics simulations show that distinct connectivity measures control ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation in linker-mediated colloidal networks.
motivation: The work aims to clarify how reversible linkers and network connectivity determine gelation in colloidal systems, where different physical transitions may be governed by different structural measures.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations of colloids connected by reversible linkers and analyze percolation, mechanical rigidity, and rheological response.
result: They find that ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation are governed by different connectivity metrics rather than a single common threshold.
conclusion: The results provide a nuanced picture of gelation in linker-mediated colloidal networks and highlight the need to distinguish structural, mechanical, and rheological connectivity criteria.

title: Active Mechanics Of Sea Star Oocytes
authors: Peter J. Foster, Alexandra Zampetaki, Jinghui Liu, Sebastian Fürthauer, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Foster, Alexandra Zampetaki, Jinghui Liu, Sebastian Fürthauer, and Nikta Fakhri

Cell shape changes, driven by the contractile actomyosin cortex, are essential for multicellular organisms. Yet, how contractility and cell shape changes emerge from molecular-scale interactions between proteins in the actomyosin cortex remains unclear. Oocytes of the bat star Patiria miniata exhibi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043103] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how contractile actomyosin cortex dynamics produce cell shape changes in sea star (Patiria miniata) oocytes, combining experiments with active matter modeling.
motivation: Cell shape changes driven by the actomyosin cortex are essential in multicellular organisms, but how molecular-scale protein interactions give rise to macroscopic contractility and shape change remains unclear.
method: Live imaging and mechanical measurements of starfish oocytes are combined with an active gel/active matter theoretical description of the contractile cortex.
result: The authors characterize the emergent contractile behavior and shape dynamics of oocytes and connect them to the underlying active mechanical properties of the cortex.
conclusion: Active mechanical descriptions can account for oocyte shape changes, offering insight into how molecular-scale activity translates into cellular-scale mechanics.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations on single actin filaments under periodic shear reveal a transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaotic dynamics.
motivation: The reversibility of driven elastic filaments at low Reynolds number is of broad interest in soft-matter and biological fluid dynamics, where the onset of irreversibility and chaos in simple semiflexible structures is not well understood.
method: Combined microfluidic experiments on individual actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filament dynamics under periodic shear flow.
result: A previously unknown transition from time-reversible, non-chaotic motion to intermittent, noise-amplified chaotic dynamics is identified as a function of shear parameters.
conclusion: Periodically sheared semiflexible filaments can exhibit spontaneous loss of reversibility and chaotic attractors, with implications for mixing and transport in biological and soft-matter systems.

title: Empirical Study Of Bidirectional Pedestrian Flow In Angled Corridors: Effects Of Flow Ratio And Geometry
authors: Weiying Chen, Rui Wang, Junheng Yang, Xiaodong Zang, And Qiang Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Weiying Chen, Rui Wang, Junheng Yang, Xiaodong Zang, and Qiang Luo

Understanding bidirectional pedestrian movement in angled corridors is important for pedestrian facility design and crowd management. This study presents controlled laboratory experiments with 48 participants. The experiments cover six corridor angles from [MATH] to [MATH] and four flow-ratio…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044135] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A controlled laboratory experiment characterizes bidirectional pedestrian flow through corridors with six different bend angles and four flow ratios.
motivation: Designers of pedestrian facilities and crowd managers need empirical data on how corridor geometry and opposing flow ratios affect walking dynamics, an aspect that remains poorly quantified for angled corridors.
method: Experiments with 48 participants were run in corridors spanning six angles (from a specified range) and four directional flow ratios, with trajectories analyzed to extract flow, density, and lane-formation statistics.
result: The study quantifies how corridor angle and flow ratio systematically alter bidirectional flow efficiency, lane formation, and congestion patterns.
conclusion: The findings provide empirically grounded guidance for pedestrian facility design and crowd-management strategies in angled corridors.
